articleTitle: Blockchain-based trusted authentication in cloud radio over fiber network for 5G
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Cloud radio access network (C-RAN) interconnects thousands of terminal devices to support the services of Internet of Things (IoT) in 5G area. However, centralized access authentication of each terminal has been performed in mobile core network which causes an extremely high operating and capital expenditure of network. Traditional C-RAN cannot provide an authentic mechanism to guarantee the security of services and creditability of device and resource accessing with low network cost. We first propose a blockchain-based trusted authentication (BTA) architecture for 5G with blockchain-based anonymous access (BAA) scheme in cloud radio over fiber network. The feasibility and efficiency are verified on enhanced SDN testbed to enable blockchain as a service.

articleTitle: Non-invasive smart health monitoring system based on optical fiber interferometers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Vital signs (including breath and heartbeat) monitoring is a key tool in healthcare. Current monitors need invasive electronic sensors attached to user's body, which is inconvenient and uncomfortable. We demonstrate photonic smart health monitoring system based on phase-sensitive optical fiber interferometers. Users simply lie/sleep on a sensor mat embedded with optical fiber interferometers. Breath and heartbeat will introduce slight strain changes on the mat and affect the light propagating within the fiber. Breathing and heartbeat waveforms can be achieved by analyzing the output light with signal processing. The system can collect user's signals continuously and remotely to provide big data for health analysis. Our technique is non-invasive, highly sensitive, and immune to electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: Visible light positioning and communication cooperative systems
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A cooperative system for visible light positioning (VLP) and visible light communication (VLC) is proposed based on the spread-spectrum plugin of optical identification (OPID). By keeping the existing VLC frame structure untouched, two different implementation schemes were designed by adding the location information field into the communication information field for VLP applications. It is deemed to be a good solution to overcome the mutual exclusion between VLP and VLC systems.

articleTitle: Visible light communication using a solar-panel receiver
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a solar panel utilized as a photodetector with simultaneous energy harvesting is proposed in visible light communication (VLC). The solar cell is a self-styled passive device, which can convert optical signals into electrical signals. The generated energy can potentially be used to power user terminals or at least to prolong operation time. This work is an important step towards the future local area networks and vehicle to vehicle communication. In our proposed VLC system, a 3-W blue LED is as the light source and a low-cost solar panel is acted as the detector. A communication with a data rate of 15.03 Mbit/s and a bit error rate of 1.6883X 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is successfully achieved using 16-quadrature amplitude modulation (16-QAM) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) technology over a 2-m air channel.

articleTitle: A Visible Light Communication (VLC) based Intelligent Transportation System for lorry fleet
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The Visible Light Communication (VLC) is a good candidate technology for the application of Intelligent Transportation System (ITS). This paper focuses on typical application scenario between the traffic lights and lorry fleet. Based on the theoretical analysis and numerical calculation, we get the relationship between the speed of the lorry fleet and the conversion time of the traffic lights. The result is meaningful for effectively reducing the potential accidents caused by lorry's frequent acceleration and deceleration.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of optical camera communications based indoor visible light positioning system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an indoor visible light positioning system based on optical camera communications, in which the transmitted coordinate data are spatially separated and demodulated by a camera. The receiver's position is calculated based on the coordinates of light-emitting diodes in the real word and in the image.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of visible light communication systems based on ACO-OFDM, DCO-OFDM and ADO-OFDM
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We compared the performance of the asymmetric and direct current bias limiting optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (ADO-OFDM), asymmetric limiting optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (ACO-OFDM), and the direct current bias limiting optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM) in visible light communication (VLC) systems. We optimize the power ratio between ACO and DCO parts in ADO-OFDM. The results show that ADO-OFDM has better performance than DCO-OFDM at small bias value, which indicate higher power spectral efficiency. It is also shown that the BER of ACO-OFDM with 16-QAM format is smaller than that of ADO-OFDM with 4-QAM format.

articleTitle: Fabrication and experiment of a FBG strain sensor in high temperature environment
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The fabrication and experiment of a high temperature FBG strain sensor is presented in this paper. Firstly, the high temperature resistant FBG has been fabricated and tested in high temperature environment. Secondly, a novel alloy rhombus packaging structure is designed for packaging the FBG sensor suitable in high temperature strain detection. The fabrication process and strain sensing mechanism of the FBG sensor are introduced. Finally, The FBG high temperature strain sensor is tested experimentally by setting up a high temperature strain experimental system, and the experimental results show that the fabricated FBG sensor could be applied in high temperature strain detection environment of 300 V with the sensitivity of 1.620 pm/με in the range of 0με~1500με.

articleTitle: Analysis of indoor VLC positioning system with multiple reflections
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) using light emitted diodes (LEDs) has been considered as the most attractive solution for indoor positioning. In this paper, an indoor visible light positioning system taking account of multiple reflections is investigated. Based on received signal strength indication (RSSI) algorithm, the positioning error distributions are simulated and show that the reflections badly influence the positioning accuracy. To obtain the positioning system with better performance, we propose a hybrid algorithm of strong signal selection and weighted centroid (SSS/WC) based on multiple LEDs. The results show that the algorithm can greatly improve the positioning accuracy.

articleTitle: Prediction of congestion degree for optical networks based on bp artificial neural network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Prediction of congestion degree is critical for optical networks to cooperate with the network control strategies. Proposed in this paper is a method of congestion degree prediction for optical networks based on BP artificial neural network. The principles are presented, and the simulation results show that our proposed is competent for network congestion degree prediction.

articleTitle: A channel model for indoor visible light communication system with specular reflection
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel channel model for indoor visible light communication (VLC) system with specular reflection. In contrast to the previous indoor visible light communication simulation models, our model is not restricted to diffuse reflection, with specular reflection considered. The simulation environment is set up in MATLAB and our model is capable of obtaining several channel characteristics such as the channel impulse responses (CIRs), the mean excess delay and the root-mean-square (RMS) delay spread, etc.

articleTitle: Research on image matching based on improved RANSAC-SIFT algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to reduce the false matching rate and matching time, an improved algorithm based on RANSAC-SIFT was proposed. The feature points were extracted by SIFT algorithm firstly. Then most of the mismatching points were eliminated according to the constraints that matching distances tend to be consistent. Finally the remaining points were regarded as pre matching points for achieve fine matching with RANSAC algorithm. The experimental results show that the improved RANSAC algorithm has much improved the matching accuracy and compression matching time.

articleTitle: A long-distance underwater laser communication system with photon-counting receiver
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design and demonstrate a long-distance underwater optical communication system with photon-counting receiver. Monte-Carlo simulations are conducted to determine system parameters and estimate system performance. According to the simulation results, a Q-switched all solid state 532nm laser with pulse energy of 100uJ@10kHz is used as the optical source of transmitter. A telescope with 1° field of view, 100mm clear aperture, and a photon counting detector is used to collect the laser in the photon-counting receiver. We then present an experimental implementation in a long tank filled with clean water. The experimental results show that optical communication is established over a distance of 85m(~24 optical attenuation lengths) at a data rate of 80kbps.

articleTitle: An optical access network framework for smart factory in the industry 4.0 era supporting massive machine connections
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed an optical access network for the deployment of CPS and the realization of smart factories aim for Industry 4.0. Through the distributed optical network, factory control center can virtualize machines, thereby realizing machine co-operation and monitoring product quality, which is the foundation of deploying CPS and realizing smart factory. While the optical access network provides a networking framework for smart factories, the massive machines call for high branching ratio. Hence, we demonstrate a high branching ratio PON which is able to support more than 131,072 machines.

articleTitle: Indoor intelligent visible light system based on Triple-Domain-Cooperation scheme
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Visible light communication has drawn much attention due to the extensive use of light emitting diodes (LED). For ultra-dense small cell deployment, visible light communication has to define the position of users for providing services and switch policies, and deal with the superposition of the light. In this paper, we propose an indoor intelligent visible light system based on Triple-Domain-Cooperation scheme (TDC) which integrates visible light communication and positioning. In our experiment, the positioning based on four color theorem gets the average positioning error of 0.04m, and the communication's bit error rate of lO<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> was realized in a 0.6m*0.6m*0.65m space at the same time.

articleTitle: In-line interference mitigation method based on Adaptive modulation and coding for satellite system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: As in-line interference between geostationary(GEO) and Non-Geostationary(NGEO) systems is becoming more and more serious. We propose an efficient utilisation of the adaptive modulation and coding (AMC) scheme for spectral coexistence of GEO and NGEO satellites to mitigate in-line interference. Results of Simulation show that the proposed scheme can improve the performance of the NGEO system in comparison with the traditional method of mitigating the co-channel interference.

articleTitle: Nonuniform quantification DAC for improving the performance of IMDD-based FBMC system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We firstly demonstrate a low-bit DAC with a nonuniform quantification scheme in intensity modulated direct detection with filter bank based multicarrier (IMDD-FBMC) system for improving the signal-to-quantification noise ratio (SQNR). In this scheme, owing to the Gaussian-like distribution of FBMC signals, the low-level waveform occupies much more bits to mitigate the quantization noise hence improving the system performance. By simulation, the feasibility of this method is verified in the 10-Gb/s 16-OQAM modulated FBMC system with 4/5-bit DAC over 20-km fiber transmission. Results show that, the SQNR and the receiver sensitivity can achieve ~3dB and ~8.7 dB improvements compared to the common scheme with a 4-bit DAC.

articleTitle: An evaluation model of water quality based on DSA-ELM method
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The evaluation technology of water quality is of great significance for monitoring and management of surface water quality. In this paper, the Extreme Learning Machine algorithm was optimized with the Dolphin Swarm Algorithm. Optimal weight and threshold of Extreme Learning Machine algorithm was searched by the process of creating a virtual team and seeking the best position of Dolphin Swarm. Four parameters of Ph, dissolved oxygen(DO), Potassium permanganate index (CODMn) and ammonia-nitrogen(NH3-N) were chosen to evaluate the level of the water and the Extreme Learning Machine algorithm optimized by Dolphin Swarm Algorithm (DSA-ELM) was used as the evaluation model of the water quality. In this paper, the water quality of 18 monitoring sites of Huai river was evaluated by DSA-ELM and ELM method. Compared the ELM algorithm model, the DSA-ELM model has the advantage of high accuracy and good stability.

articleTitle: Research on integrated space-air-ground TT&C and communication network based on space tracking ship
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To satisfy the TT&C and communication needs of aviation and aerospace flight vehicle, it is necessary to construct integrated Space-Air-Ground TT&C and Communication network with all-sided covering and flexible networking. The three-layered architecture of the integrated network is designed, and the composition, function and feature of each layer are discussed. By taking the advantages of good mobility and deployment of space tracking ship, consider the role and function of sea based platform in integrated Space-Air-Ground TT&C and Communication networks, and propose networking mode based on formation centre and sea based node relay.

Author Keywords: Integrated Space-Air-Ground TT&C and Communication Network

articleTitle: Multi-wavelength lasing oscillation based on polarization hole burning effect in an Erbium-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel multi-wavelength switchable laser system is proposed and demonstrated, which is based on polarization hole burning (PHB) effect in an erbium-doped fiber (EDF) laser (EDFL). In this EDFL, multiple fiber Bragg gratings with different wavelengths are used as comb filter. The PHB effect is enhanced by polarization separating of the multi-wavelength lasing lines through adjusting the polarization controllers (PCs). So the lasing lines with different wavelength, different polarization state can consume the erbium-doped particles with different polarization, leading to a suppression of the mode competition effect in the EDF and a stable multi-wavelength lasing operation. In the experiment, we obtain four-wavelength stable lasing oscillation.

articleTitle: Ultrasound generation from side wall of optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ultrasound technique has been widely applied in various areas such as diagnostic applications, structure health monitoring, etc. Most advanced applications require novel ultrasonic transmitters, where fiber optic technique has been proved to be a great candidate due to its compact dimension, high frequency, and highly harsh environment survivability. Therefore, extensive research has been conducted on developing novel fiber optic ultrasound transmitters for the recent decades. This review paper will briefly review the history of the fiber optic ultrasound generation and then will focus on the ultrasound generation from the side wall of optical fibers. Several applications based on this technique will be discussed and the future of the technology will be previewed.

articleTitle: High speed visible light communication system using QAM-DMT modulation based on digital zero-padding and differential receiver
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have proposed a novel hybrid software and hardware equalization scheme based on digital zero-padding pre-equalization and differential reception. We have experimental demonstrated a red LED based visible light communication system over 1-meter free space transmission with the measured BER below 7% FEC threshold. The signal is QAM-DMT modulated and the modulation level is varying from 32QAM to 128QAM. By applying the proposed hybrid scheme the measured maximum bit rate can be improved from 2.32Gb/s to 2.59Gb/s. And the highest modulation order is enhanced from 64QAM to 128QAM. Our experimental results clearly validate the feasibility of the scheme in future high-speed visible light communication system.

articleTitle: Underwater visible light communications based on spatial diversity
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of underwater visible light communications (UVLC) systems employing multiple transmitters and/or multiple receivers to exploit the advantage of spatial diversity. Experimental results are further provided to evaluate the error performance of single input multiple outputs (SIMO), multiple inputs single output (MISO) and multiple inputs multiple outputs (MIMO) UVLC systems when orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation is utilized. Our results reveal that the proposed system configuration can indeed offer significant system performance enhancements in terms of the attainable bit error rate.

articleTitle: Optical superimposition-based PAM-4 signal generation for visible light communication
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A pulse amplitude modulation with 4 levels (PAM-4), generated by optical superimposition, is first proposed and experimentally demonstrated for visible light communication (VLC). It can overcome the shortcomings of the PAM-4 signals generated in the electrical domain, with enhanced tolerance to the modulation nonlinearities of a light emitting diode (LED). A proof-of-concept experiment employing two blue LEDs has been conducted in this work. We achieve a 12.288-Mb/s PAM-4 signal, within a 2.5-MHz system bandwidth, by superimposing two different on-off keying (OOK)-modulated signals in the optical domain and investigate the BER performance over 2-m, 3-m, 4-m, 5-m and 6-m air channels. At this bit rate, the available maximum transmission distance is 4 m in the air and the corresponding BERs of the two OOK signals are 8.39×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> and 1.43 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, respectively.

articleTitle: Distributed acoustic sensing based on correlation analysis of fast and linear sweep OFDR
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present a method to produce continuous, fast and truly-linear frequency-sweep optical signal driven by arbitrary waveform generator. By using this signal as the optical source, a high-repetition-rate optical frequency domain reflectometry is experimentally demonstrated with linear response to outside perturbation. This work has significant value for achieving high performance distributed acoustic sensing.

articleTitle: Static provisioning for advance reservation in elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes joint frequency and time domain optimization of static scheduling for advance reservation (AR) requests in elastic optical networks (EONs). We formulate the problem as an integer linear program (ILP) and then propose two scheduling schemes. Simulation results show that compared with ILP, our scheme can achieve the same performance in terms of spectrum utilization with efficient time complexity.

articleTitle: Techniques of rain fade countermeasures in Ka-band satellite communication on ships
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ka-band communication is an important development direction of satellite communication, the rain fade has been the main factor which restricts the engineering application; rainfall spatial structure in the sea, the layered and convection rain cause great influence to the Ka-band satellite communication. The paper analyzes the reasons of rain fade, points out the electromagnetic wave absorption, thermal noise and depolarization is the important factor of Ka-band rain fade, according to the characteristics of the maritime shipping, puts forward rain fade methods such as the uplink power control, frequency diversity, rate diversity, adaptive modulation.

articleTitle: Ballistocardiography based on optical fiber sensors
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ballistocardiography (BCG) is a non-invasive method for measuring the reaction force of the human body to the ejection of blood at each cardiac cycle. It is now being the subject of renewed research interest due to recent technological advancement in the field of sensors. In this paper, we summarize our work on BCG with optical fiber sensors for various applications in the past 6 years. These include wearable BCG and non wearable BCG. In the non wearable BCG, there are bed based BCG, chair based BCG and standing BCG for various applications including measurements of heart rate, respiratory rate, sleep monitoring, cuff-less blood pressure measurement and perioperative pediatric vital signs monitoring. We report the first novel application of microbend fiber sensor for simultaneous measurements of heart rate, respiratory rate and body posture/position.

articleTitle: An defragmentation scheme for extending the maximal unoccupied spectrum block in elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In Elastic Optical Net-works (EONs), dynamic allocation and release of lightpaths will lead to frequency spectrum fragment issue which making the optical spectrum into non-aligned, isolated and small-sized spectrum segments. Defragmentation strategies are key issues to minimize this problem. In this paper, we investigate the states of spectrum when the bandwidth blocking probability (BBP) is high, and propose a modified defragmentation scheme to alleviate spectrum fragmentation in dynamic network environments by extending the maximal unoccupied spectrum blocks. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations show that the proposed scheme can effectively reduce the degree of fragmentation of the network and extend the maximal unoccupied spectrum blocks.

articleTitle: DTN routing algorithm based on service probability and limited copy for satellite networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: There are some shortcomings in the delay tolerant network (DTN) routing algorithm, such as low message delivery rate, low network efficiency and high cost in the satellite network. In order to solve the problem above, this paper proposes a limited copy algorithm MPWLC based on service probability. In MPWLC, not only is the number of copies limited, but the storage resources of the satellite are also taken into account to ensure reliable data transmission. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the efficiency of the network and ensure the reliable data transmission.

articleTitle: Mode converter based on the long-period fiber gratings written in the six-mode fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate the fabrication of long-period fiber gratings written in six-mode fiber by CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-laser pulses as a mode converter to realize the mode conversion from LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode to LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode, LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> mode and LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> mode successfully with efficiencies of more than 90%, respectively.

articleTitle: A phase compensation method for Monopulse tracking receiver of ship-borne satcom station
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To solve the phase deviation problem caused by antenna orientation centre deviation during the phase calibration of Monopulse tracking receiver on ship-borne sitcom station, a phase compensation method is proposed to enhance the phase calibration precision. The working principle of monopulse tracking receiver is discussed, the demodulation process of sum and difference signal, and the cause of phase deviation based on current phase calibration method is analysed. Then, a phase compensation method based on deviation source is proposed, and the phase calibration operation procedure detail is discussed. Results based on the current and proposed phase calibration methods are compared, and the proposed method enhances the phase calibration index effectively, which means a more precise phase result is acquired.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of NOMA visible light communications based on SCFDM
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) scheme in combination with single carrier frequency division multiplexing (SCFDM) for visible light communications (VLC), which in principle could provide high spectral efficiency, high tolerance against multi-path and a lower peak-to-average ratio (PAPR). Compared with orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based NOMA, NOMA-SCFDM has higher tolerance to LED nonlinearity and better bit error rate (BER) performance.

articleTitle: Low latency passive optical node for optical access network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel passive optical node with low latency for optical access network (OAN) is proposed, in which the optical circuit just consists of several optical splitters. 1310nm/ 1490nm wavelength division is used in the node. At 1310nm wavelength, any optical network unit (ONU) in one group can transmit the uplink signal to OLT and any ONU in the other group. This realizes communication between two ONUs to handle the east-west traffic directly. Compared with conventional point-to-multipoint passive optical network, simulation results show the node can reduce the average frame latency evidently and handle traffic burst well.

articleTitle: Modeling of the impacts of nonlinear propagation on EVM for digital coherent receivers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Analytical model is proposed to estimate EVM under the case of nonlinear noise for coherent optical fiber communications with digital receivers. Theoretical formula is obtained, which is validated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Design of yarn break detection based on tunnel magnetoresistance effect
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The yarn break detection system of ring spinning based on tunnel magnetoresistance effect is proposed in the paper. The TMR element is used to detect the anomaly signal caused by rotating traveler. The signal reflects the rotation speed of traveler and the yarn break is monitored by speed measurement. The yarn break sensor, section detection module, machine monitoring module are designed and implemented. The performance test result indicates that the system can satisfy the practical application of yarn break detection with the advantages of compact size, high sensitivity, strong anti-interference capability and so on.

articleTitle: Service risk analysis for power communication over optical transport networks based on link failure
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, service risk model based on the fiber link failure is defined for the power communication over optical transport networks (OTN). We also propose the computation methods for the probability of fiber link failure, and the service losses. The method for service risk analysis is designed and the probability of fiber link failure is analyzed. The reliability loss caused by the single fiber link failure is evaluated. In the end, the effectiveness of the service risk model is verified by exploiting the practical network model.

articleTitle: The OAM transmission fiber based on circular photonic crystal fiber structure
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a kind of orbital angular momentum (OAM) mode supporting fiber based on photonic crystal fiber structure, give a design strategy for designing a family of circular photonic crystal OAM fiber with the good transmission performance features such as good quality OAM modes, enough separation of the effective indices, low confinement loss, flat dispersion, large effective area, and low nonlinear coefficient.

articleTitle: Brillouin optical time domain analyzer enhanced by artificial/deep neural networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report our recent studies on the use of Neural Networks to process the measured Brillouin gain spectrum (BGS) from Brillouin Optical Time Domain Analyzer (BOTDA) and extract temperature information along fiber under test (FUT). Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is trained with ideal Lorentizian BGS before it is used for temperature extraction. Its performance is evaluated by comparison to conventional curve fitting techniques, showing better accuracy especially at large frequency scanning step during the acquisition of BGSs. We have also applied advanced hierarchical Deep Neural Network (DNN) in BOTDA for temperature extraction to improve the training and testing efficiency. We believe that ANN/DNN can be attractive tools for direct temperature or strain extraction in BOTDA system with high accuracy.

articleTitle: A segmentation modulation based spectral allocation scheme for elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Elastic optical network (EON) has been receiving extensive attention due to its inherent flexibility and the efficiency with which it allocates fiber bandwidth. Depending on the physical impairment, the distance adaptive modulation scheme can be adopted to ensure the transmission quality. However, distance adaptive modulation scheme will occupy more spectrum resources for the long-distance path. A segmentation modulation based spectral allocation scheme for EON is proposed to shorten the distance of each section by making working path segmentation, which reduces the occupied frequency slots (FS) by adopting high-level modulation. As a result, the proposed scheme will efficiently reduce the allocated FS and improve the overall spectrum resource utilization of the network.

articleTitle: Simultaneous measurement of temperature and refractive index with thin-core fiber MZI containing fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A thin-core fiber based Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) for simultaneous measurement of temperature and refractive index is demonstrated. It is formed by sandwiching a short section of highly germanium-doped fiber between two single-mode fibers and writing a fiber Bragg grating (FBG) on the germanium-doped fiber. Simultaneous measurement is achieved based on the different responses of the interferometer and the FBG to the two parameters. Experimental results show that temperature sensitivity of 74.2pm/°C and refractive index sensitivity of 6.75nm/RIU are achieved, respectively.

articleTitle: Detection of Ni2+ with optical fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer coated with chitosan/MWCNT/PAA
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical fiber Nickel ions (Ni<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>) sensor based on a Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) formed by cascading two coating-functionalized fiber tapers is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The functional coating is a multi-layer film of chitosan/muli-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNT)/poly acrylic acid (PAA) formed directly onto the fiber surface via a layer-by-layer assembly technique. As the heavy metal ions get absorbed by the coating, transmission spectra of the MZI sensor changes due to refractive index variation of the coating. A high sensitivity of 56.5 dB/mM is achieved for concentration of Ni<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ranging from 0.3 to 0.7 mM.

articleTitle: Speckle-based fiber sensor for temperature measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The applications of specklegram analysis techniques have been developed recently. In this paper, we represent a fiber-optic method to measure the temperature through the analysis of output specklegrams. The proposed all-fiber device excites higher-order modes through splicing a multimode fiber (MMF) to a single-mode fiber (SMF) with a core offset. The basic principle of the sensor is based on determining the change occurring to a speckle pattern when the fiber is heated under different temperature. This change in the speckle pattern is computed by comparing it with a reference speckle pattern recorded at a known temperature and therefore can be related to the temperature change. The experiments manifest the approximately linear relation between correlation coefficient and temperature. Furthermore, we also demonstrate the effects of other related parameters to the sensor.

articleTitle: Secure chaotic communication with spectrum expansion/compression
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A security-enhanced chaos communication scheme by expanding and compressing the spectrum of modulated chaotic carrier is proposed, in virtue of a spectrum expansion module composed of two phase modulators and two dispersion mediums. The numerical results demonstrate that the efficient bandwidth of modulated chaotic carrier can be expanded up to several tens of GHz and the RF spectrum is uniformly flat. Moreover, the security of the proposed system is discussed by comparing the bit error ratio (BER) of legitimate receiver and that of eavesdroppers who try to extract message from the public link by the ways of direct filtering and synchronization utilization. It is indicated that the BER of illegal interception message is much larger than the legal one. The security of the proposed scheme is much higher than the conventional scenario without spectrum expansion and compression.

articleTitle: A novel optical encoding scheme based on spectral phase encoding for secure optical communication
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel optical encoding scheme based on spectral phase encoding, in which optical codes are randomly selected from a code set for code hopping. The security performance is analysed. It can achieve the identical security level with short hopping pattern, efficiently improving the system resources.

articleTitle: Joint IT and spectrum resource load balancing for VNF selection in inter-datacenter elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The selection of virtualized network functions (VNFs) in service provisioning is a critical issue in inter-datacenter elastic optical networks. In this paper, considering load balancing of IT and spectrum resources, we propose two joint balancingfactors, i.e., Global Balancing factor (GB-factor) and Local Balancing factor (LB-factor) for VNFs selection. Then a Joint-Optimization Selection (JOS) algorithm is designed based on the joint balancingfactors. Simulation results show that GB-factor based JOS can achieve better performance compared with LB-factor based JOS and benchmark algorithm.

articleTitle: Mode conversion-based crosstalk-aware routing, spectrum and mode assignment in space-division multiplexing elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A mode conversion-based crosstalk-aware routing, spectrum and mode assignment (MC-CA RSMA) algorithm is introduced in space-division multiplexing elastic optical networks (SDM-EONs) over few-mode fibers. Simulation results show the MC-CA RSMA algorithm can greatly reduce the impact of inter-mode crosstalk on network performance compared with benchmark algorithms.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensing using all-dielectric metasurface with analogue of electromagnetically induced transparency
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we design an all-dielectric metasurface, which can produce a sharp transmission peak due to analogue of electromagnetically induced transparency to realize refractive index sensing. The structure is a periodic lattice of a silicon dumbbell-shaped bar and a silicon ring resonator on the bulk fused silica substrate. The EIT phenomenon of the proposed metasurface and the refractive index sensing are both investigated using the finite integral method. The simulated results show the sensitivity to the refractive index reaches 2356.59 nm/RIU in the mid-infrared wavelength band.

articleTitle: High speed visible light communication based on pulse amplitude modulation
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Novel technologies based on pulse amplitude modulation (PAM) are studied for a high-speed visible light communication (VLC) system. In this paper, we summarize the latest progress on high-speed PAM-VLC systems including phase shifted Manchester coding, Nyquist filter, weighted pre-equalization, multi-band access, and hybrid time-frequency domain equalization, which supporting VLC high data-rate and high spectral efficiency over indoor free-space transmission.

articleTitle: High-sensitivity phase noise measurement of RF sources by photonic-delay line and digital phase demodulation
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-sensitivity phase noise measurement scheme using photonic-delay line and digital phase demodulation is proposed, which is free of complicate calibration and amplitude noise by using digital phase demodulation. In the experiment, a phase noise measurement sensitivity as high as -134 dBc/Hz@10 kHz@10 GHz is achieved applying a 2-km single mode fiber as the delay line. Besides, accurate phase noise measurement in a large frequency bandwidth from 2 to 35 GHz is achieved.

articleTitle: A random filtering mapping method for PAPR reduction based on generalized frequency division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In the paper, we propose a new method, namely Random Filtering Mapping (RFM), through which the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of the Generalized frequency division multiplexing (GFDM) signal is reduced. Then, the improved signal is transmitted through the Radio Over Fiber (ROF) system of Single SideBand (SSB) modulation and optical fiber of 60Km. The simulation results show that the PAPR of the RFM-GFDM signal is about 5dB lower than the original GFDM signal. In addition, the EVM of the RFM-GFDM signal is about 0.5%–5% lower than the original GFDM. The proposed method greatly improves the performance of the GFDM signal in ROF system, which is a better choice for transmission.

articleTitle: Design overview of a rapid mapping resolution system for enabling identifier/location separation in satellite network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The current satellite network design is approaching an inflection point with mobile devices as the primary enduser devices. In addition, identifier/location separation is commonly used to enhance mobility in future satellite networks. To this end, a key issue must be addressed is the design of rapid mapping resolution system. In this work, a design overview of a rapid mapping resolution system is presented. Two key design elements, the space-based distributed design as well as the dynamic replica placement algorithm are also described to achieve the goals including low lookup latency, low update cost and high system availability.

articleTitle: A scheme of ultraviolet communication system with polar channel coding
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a scheme of ultraviolet (UV) communication system, with polar channel coding method. The bit error rate (BER) performance of the UV polar code scheme is analyzed by simulations and offline experiments, in contrast with low-density parity-check (LDPC) scheme. Results suggest that the polar code scheme has a better BER performance than LDPC scheme in the UV communication system.

articleTitle: A weighted clustering algorithm based on node stability for Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of instability clustering in Ad Hoc Networks with complex and changeable node motion, this paper proposes a weighted clustering algorithm based on node stability(SA-WCA). In this algorithm, we propose a node stability factor based on node received power, which does not need to calculate the specific distance between nodes and can only judge the relative motion between the nodes according to the transmitting power and the received power of the node. The newly defined factors have a more scientific evaluation on the stability of the nodes. The Simulation studies the performance of the clustering algorithm such as the number of clusters reconstruction, the change rate of nodes and the load balance factor and compared with the Lowest ID algorithm (LOWID), the Highest degree algorithm (HIGHD) and the Weighted clustering algorithm (WCA). The results show that the proposed algorithm is superior to other algorithms in improving the stability of cluster structures.

articleTitle: Free-space broad-spectrum optical communication based on supercontinuum
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a free-space optical (FSO) communication system with supercontinuum source generated by dispersion shift fiber (DSF) from pulsed light modulated by optical switches is designed and constructed. In addition, the experimental results of free-space optical communication between broadband and narrowband light source are compared. Verifying the feasibility of broad-spectrum FSO communication link through atmospheric turbulence can be achieved by reducing the inter-symbol interference caused by excessive noise with addition of adaptive equalizer. The experimental results show that the super continuum can be used as the optical signal carrier, and the signal can be wirelessly transmitted under the space atmospheric channel condition.

articleTitle: Low-bias high-speed modified uni-traveling-carrier photodiode
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the high-speed modified uni-traveling-carrier photodiode (MUTC-PD) was designed and fabricatedfor low reverse bias. The 3-dB bandwidth and responsivity of MUTC-PD with 24-μm mesa diameter at 1-V reverse bias is 22.5 GHz and 0.22 A/W at the wavelength of1550 nm, respectively. The dark current of the device is less than 4nA at 3.3 V reverse bias. The fabricated device can achieve high performance at low reverse bias is confirmed.

articleTitle: Distributed sensing network using a chirped ultra-weak fiber Bragg grating array
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A distributed sensing network using a chirped ultra-weak fiber Bragg grating array is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. This network is based on time-division multiplexing (TDM) technique. We use a path-match interferometry to obtain interference signal, then amplitude, phase, frequency and location information can be demodulated from interference signal by employing the passive 3 × 3 coupler demodulation technique. Experiment was demonstrated on detecting vibration signals on the tracks, the vibration signals generated by a piezoelectric transducer (PZT), and underwater acoustic waves driven by a signal generator. The experimental results show that this system can well demodulate vibration signals generated by PZT and acoustic signals under the water with a relatively frequency response between 50Hz to 800Hz.

articleTitle: Weakly-coupled mode-division-multiplexing systems and networks supporting large quantity of independent modes
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Weakly-coupled mode-division-multiplexing (MDM) is a promising approach to overcome the capacity crunch in optical transmission systems and networks. In this paper, we present the latest progresses of weakly-coupled MDM transmission over multi-mode fiber (MMF) or few-mode fiber (FMF) supporting large quantity of independent modes with intensity modulation and direct detection.

articleTitle: Effect of kGy dose level gamma radiation on Ge-doped FBGs and femtosecond-laser-inscribed pure-silica-core FBGs
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The effect of gamma radiation with a maximum dose of 180 kGy at a dose rate of 10.15 kGy/hour on both standard Ge-doped fiber Bragg Gratings (Ge-FBG) and femtosecond-laser-inscribed pure-silica-core fiber Bragg Gratings (FL-PS-FBG) have been investigated. In the case of Ge-FBGs, a maximum Bragg wavelength shifts (BWS) of 140 pm and a decrease of the reflection peak power of 16 dB has been observed. The observed large peak power change was resulted from radiation induced loss and do not dependent on the temperature variation which make it a good candidate for radiation dosimetry applications. On the other hand, FL-PS-FBGs exhibit good radiation resistance characteristics and the observed maximum radiation induced BWS and the decrease of the reflection peak power is as small as 40 pm and 1 dB, respectively, which make it suitable for temperature sensing applications in high dose radiation environment.

articleTitle: Simulation of the performance of phase-sensitive OTDR based on Ultra-weak FBG array using double pulses
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A phase-sensitive optical time domain reflectometry sensing system based on Ultra-weak FBG Array using double pulses is proposed. The principle of this sensing system is elaborated. A series of simulations are carried out to optimize the parameters to increase the sensing distance of this system. The parameters contain reflectivity of UWFBG, the interval between adjacent UWFBGs and pulse width. The optimal reflectivity and pulse width corresponding to different grating space are found out to achieve a longer sensing distance.

articleTitle: A research platform for software defined satellite networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Software Defined Satellite Networking (SDSN) provides an innovative perspective to manage satellite network through logically centralized network view and standard interfaces between the control and data plane. Significant advantages of SDSN include enabling integration of space and terrestrial network, flexible and efficient resource management, rapid and economical network function updating, etc. However, at present, there is not an experiment platform specially for SDSN, restricting the in-depth study of SDSN. Therefore, in this paper, we propose OpenSatNet, a platform for software defined satellite networking research. OpenSatNet uses lightweight OS-level virtualization, including network namespaces and virtual network devices, can emulate a realistic satellite network and has a user-friendly graphical user interface (GUI). Through OpenSatNet, researchers can easily conduct a realistic experiment for SDSN on their PCs. The snapshot routing for SDSN is implemented to demonstrate the operation of our platform.

articleTitle: Study on SV packet transmission delay measurement of IEC 61850-9-2 process bus networks in smart substation
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Owing to the uncertainty of SV packet transmission delay in switches, the synchronization of network sampling based on the compensation for SV packet transmission delay must rely on an external synchronization system. This letter gives a structure of Ethernet switch based on FPGA aiming to measure the time delay of SV packets transmission, and proposes a method of measuring and storing the time delay using link delay and switch delay time information to extend the IEC 61850-9-2frame.

articleTitle: A truthful auction mechanism for service deployment in cloud-integrated WOBAN
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Though auction has been exploited to deploy services or allocate resources in the literatures, an efficient truthful auction mechanism is required to charge service providers as buyers for deployable locations as sellers in a Cloud-Integrated WOBAN(CIW)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. In this paper, we first design a truthful auction mechanism for service deployment in a CIW, which can be divided into two stages: the match between buyers and seller and the final deal price determination. Then, we formally prove truthfulness, which is the crucial property of auction mechanism. Finally, the simulation results show that our mechanism achieves truthfulness and that buyers and sellers gain revenue both.

articleTitle: Phase noise estimation in coherent optical communication based on local convex optimization
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a novel phase noise estimation method (PNE) for multi-level modulations is proposed based on local optimization (LO PNE). The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated and discussed in a 200G bit/s coherent transmission system. It has been proved, the usage of throwing-point (TP) test rotation and convex programming in LO_PNE reduce the complexity of phase estimation for arbitrary modulation to one in three of BPS and achieve accurate estimation.

articleTitle: A chitosan-coated humidity sensor based on Michelson interferometer with thin-core optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel humidity sensor, which is based on Michelson interferometer (MI) with thin core fiber (TCF) coated with chitosanis proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Its principle is that the light in the single-mode fiber (SMF) core is excited into the cladding of the TCF, and the light transmitted from the end face of the TCF is reflected back to the SMF core. When the chitosan is coated on the end face of the TCF, its refractive index (RI) is changed, causing the shift of the wavelength and intensity of the interference pattern. The structure can be double demodulated, and the sensitivity is highest achievable is 0.058dB/%RH (relative humidity unit), 0.043nm/%RH respectively. The sensor is low cost, easy to make.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of OOK and PAM modulations in underwater optical wireless communication system based on APD receiver
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the properties of underwater optical wireless communication (UOWC) have been demonstrated based on the Monte Carlo method. We investigate the underwater channel responses of different wavelengths under different water conditions. The results show that the optimum transmission wavelength is switched from 450nm (blue) to 595nm (red) when the water condition is changed from pure to turbid harbour water. Moreover, the maximum transmission distances are achieved when using OOK/PAM based on APD receiver. In pure water, the maximum transmission distance is up to 116m at 10Mb/s data rate and 1W transmitted electrical power.

articleTitle: Extended Kalman filter for polarization demultiplexing in stokes space
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A PolDemux method using Extended Kalman Filter is proposed, which is general and independent on channel RSOP models for RSOP tracing, and shows great RSOP tracing speed, moderate PMD tolerances, fast convergence and lower complexity.

articleTitle: Algorithm research of routing and spectrum allocation based on OSNR impairment model in elastic optical network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: High spectrum efficiency and flexibility are the advantages of elastic optical network, which is the future direction of optical network development. Routing and resource allocation is one of the core technologies of flexible optical networks. This paper propose an improved RSA algorithm in the elastic optical network which based on OSNR impairment model. It considers both QoT (quality of transmission) and available spectrum resources of the network in routing selection and spectrum allocation. Theoretical analysis and simulation results show that compared with the traditional RSA algorithm, the proposed algorithm can improve the transmission efficiency and quality, and reduce the traffic blocking rate.

articleTitle: Full-range carrier frequency offset estimation for CO-OFDM based on CMA equalizers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A constant modulus algorithm-(CMA) based carrier frequency offset estimation method for coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) system is proposed. Theoretical analysis and simulation results indicate that the frequency offset estimation range of the proposed algorithm can achieve [-5.9, +5.9] GHz, and the mean normalized estimation error can be kept under 0.001 even the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) value is as low as 2 dB.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a feedback-assisted orbital angular momentum-based underwater wireless optical link across the underwater-to-air interface
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a feedback-assisted 1.08 Gb/s orbital angular momentum (OAM)-based underwater-to-air wireless optical link with a floating mirror for beam steering. The experimental results show favorable performance of the proposed feedback scheme in the present of the change of water level.

articleTitle: Wavefront compensation simulation of modulating retroreflector free-space optical link utilizing micro corner-cube-reflector arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The wavefront compensation effect of the micro corner-cube-reflector arrays (MCCRAs) in modulating retroreflector (MRR) free-space optical (FSO) link is investigated by wave-optics (WO) simulation method that is based on the split-step beam propagation method and phase screen theory. Two kinds of the MCCRAs with the cell's apertures of the triangle and hexagon are considered with the aid of the numerical ray-tracing approach. Integrating the reflection phase of the MCCRAs into WO simulations, the double-pass propagation of light beam through the turbulent atmosphere is simulated to study the characteristics of the returned optical beam. We find the spread spot of the optical beam reflected from the MCCRAs is rather convergent as compared with that reflected from a single corner cube reflector. Hence, we draw a conclusion that the MCCRAs can in principle yield a powerful wavefront compensation in MRR FSO communication links.

articleTitle: Ballistocardiography based on optical fiber sensors
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ballistocardiography (BCG) is a non-invasive method for measuring the reaction force of the human body to the ejection of blood at each cardiac cycle. It is now being the subject of renewed research interest due to recent technological advancement in the field of sensors. In this paper, we summarize our work on BCG with optical fiber sensors for various applications in the past 6 years. These include wearable BCG and non wearable BCG. In the non wearable BCG, there are bed based BCG, chair based BCG and standing BCG for various applications including measurements of heart rate, respiratory rate, sleep monitoring, cuff-less blood pressure measurement and perioperative pediatric vital signs monitoring. We report the first novel application of microbend fiber sensor for simultaneous measurements of heart rate, respiratory rate and body posture/position.

articleTitle: Latency and efficiency driven dynamic content replacement in elastic optical datacenter networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We study the problem of dynamic content replacement in terms of network state variation in elastic optical datacenter networks. A dynamic content replacement scheme is proposed to minimize spectrum consumption, blocking probability and network latency.

articleTitle: High-speed free-space optical card-to-card transmission architecture based on homodyne coherent detection
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a 60cm free-space optical card-to-card wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) transmission architecture using OFDM modulation and coherent detection is proposed and demonstrated, which can offer flexibility and high speed transmission simultaneously. The experimental results show that the net data rate is up to 106.9Gb/s and the receiver sensitivity is -34dBm at the BER threshold of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>.

articleTitle: Wireless virtual network embedding algorithm through topology awareness
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the dynamic arrival of the virtual network requests in the wireless network environment leads to the unbalanced allocation of the substrate network resources and the low acceptance rate of the subsequent requests, a topology-aware wireless virtual network embedding algorithm (WVNEA-TA) is proposed. By analyzing the dynamic topological attributes of the virtual network and the substrate network from local and global perspective, the algorithm sorts the mapping priority of the nodes in embedding process. In addition, considering the substrate link interference and the link load, the algorithm could select substrate bearer path with lower interference and well-resourced. The simulation results show that WVNEA-TA algorithm improves the acceptance rate, and increases the network R/C ratio.

articleTitle: An implementation of optical network virtualization based on OpenVirteX
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Network Virtualization (NV) realizes the decoupling of network infrastructure and network services. With the emergence of the Software Defined Network (SDN), it is easier to implement NV supporting dynamic heterogeneous underlay network. In this paper, we present and experimentally validate an Optical Network Virtualization (ONV) architecture based on OpenVirteX (OVX) supporting bandwidth on demand (BoD).

articleTitle: All fiber on-line Raman detection system with silver-coated hollow fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a portable online Raman detection system with all fiber components, by inserting two large-diameter optical fibers respectively into each end of the inner metal-coated capillary for Raman excitation and signal collection simultaneously. The all fiber structure not only could enhance the interaction length between the excitation beam and the detecting material, but also provide a very effective Raman signal collection mechanism. Furthermore, in our proposed setup, the output fiber is bent back to the input side and form a Sagnac loop. Both inserted fibers act as the input port as well as the output port for the transmission and reflection mode simultaneously. With the combination of both modes and both beam directions, the Raman signal could be roughly enhanced 4 times. The result of theoretical modelling and the experimental measurement confirm that this portable all fiber detection system is a very effective way for Raman excitation and signal detection, which could be widely used for liquid and gas online detection system.

articleTitle: Visible smartphone spectrometer based on the transmission grating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a portable visible spectrometer using an Android smartphone is proposed, designed and experimentally tested. The entire optical system consists of a 10 μm slit, the collimator lens, a 300 lines/mm transmission grating, and the imaging lenses. The CMOS image sensor of the smartphone is utilized for optical imaging. Then a built-in app will calculate the spectrum. Minimum spectral resolution of 7 nm is achieved according to the ZEMAX simulations. The whole size of the external device is 44*44*50 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and can be easily installed on the backside of the smartphone. This visible spectrometer can be applied in various fields, such as food safety, water contamination detection, air quality examination, and so on.

articleTitle: Dual-passband microwave photonic filter for fiber axial strain measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A dual-passband microwave photonics filter (MPF) for fiber axial measurement is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The MPF is mainly implemented using a phase modulator (PM) and two cascaded fiber Bragg grating Fabry-Perot (FBG-FP) filters with different central wavelengths. According to the phase-modulation to intensity-modulation (PM-IM) conversion in the MPF, dual-passband can be generated. The fiber axial strain will change the wavelength of the FBG-FP filter, and resulting in the frequency difference variation between the notch of the FBG-FP and the laser source. Thus, the passband frequency can be easily affected by the fiber axial strain applied onto the FBG-FP filter. Strain measurement is executed by recording the change of frequency difference between the sensing passband and reference passband so as to overcome the environmental influence. Finally, a high strain sensitivity of 137.046 MHz/με is achieved.

articleTitle: Optical millimeter-wave generation with frequency multiplication in radio over fiber system based on the external modulation
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This work demonstrated the specific process and the influence factors of the optical millimeter-wave (MM-wave) generation and proposed the selection and control of the optical sidebands in Radio-over-Fiber (ROF) system based on the external modulation technology. In the system, it is explained theoretically and experimentally that the optical sidebands and the amplitude of optical sidebands can be controlled by adjusting the influence factors of the optical MM wave generation.

articleTitle: An OSNR calculating method based on network topology for optical network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the OSNR expressions for the cascaded system in the practical optical network is derived from the definition of OSNR. Then we analyse the OSNR changes in optical channels resulted from the variation of network topology, which is verified by optical network simulation software at the end of the paper.

articleTitle: Research on automatic target acquisition and tracking in an infrared tracking system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In an infrared tracking measurement system, using inter-image subtraction and position detection method to achieve the goal of automatic capture, using centroid tracking, correlation tracking and edge tracking related goals of automatic tracking, the test of this method with good results in actual use, which provide technical reference for the development and use of infrared tracking measurement system.

articleTitle: Hydrogen peroxide detection based on near-infrared TDLAS and Herriott cell
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A compact open-path tunable diode laser absorption spectrometry (TDLAS) sensor has been developed for gas-phase hydrogen peroxide (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) concentration monitoring during sterilization and aseptic disinfection. The sensor was based on a open-path multi-pass Herriott cell and wavelength modulated near-infrared diode laser. The sensor was calibrated by titrating the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> water which was obtained by exhausting measured gas-phase H2O2 through a water bubbler. A detection limit of 15 ppm with single measurement is achieved in the range of approximately 0–2000 ppm. The response time is 1s, mainly limited by ramping frequency and processing speed. It offers a combination of sensitivity, fast response, dynamic range, cost effectiveness and easy operation not available in alternative H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> detectors.

articleTitle: Evaluation index system of electric power SD-OTN service riskfactors
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: At present, the power communication network has many evaluation indexes, but the existing OTN operation risk evaluation index is only a simple statistical index, and lack of analysis and evaluation and prediction of indicators. It is more important to optimize the software defined-optical transmission network (SD-OTN) performance and improve the network bandwidth. In order to explore the auxiliary decision of the OTN index system to the management, this paper designs and gives the operational risk assessment index of the large-capacity OTN and multi-factor comprehensive index system according to the particularity and its own characteristics.

articleTitle: High-extinction-ratio periodic pulse signal generation based on MZ modulator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: High extinction ratio is needed in high precision Optical Time Domain Reflectometer (OTDR) to enlarge the dynamic range. By transmitting part of pulse signal modulated by a Mach-Zehnder (MZ) optical modulator back to the input of the modulator via a feedback circuit, the pulse signal can be multi-modulated by one MZ optical modulation. And this technique offers great enhancements in the performance of extinction ratio and peak power of the output pulse. This paper present a theoretical analysis of this system, give out a system-parameters-setting methods to make the result output from the system is falling in line with expectation. A simulation platform and computer simulation are done to validate the validity of the system.

articleTitle: Wideband optical cancellation of RF interference with phase change
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A microwave photonic based RF interference cancellation scheme is proposed to compensate for wideband phase changes of the interference signals, in which microwave photonic phase shifter is particularly employed. In the proposed cancellation scheme, a known interferer is delayed, attenuated, phase shifted so as to be subtracted from the received signal at the output. The microwave photonic phase shifter based on a dual-parallel Mach-Zehnder modulator (DPMZM) is utilized to achieve wideband optical cancellation with phase changes. Proof-of-concept experiment results validate the scheme and demonstrate a 30-dB cancellation depth for a wideband signal over 4 GHz at most, limited by the bandwidth of an electrical hybrid and the bias drifting of the modulators.

articleTitle: Optical encryptions and decryptions based on all-optical shift register
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an optical encryption /decryption system based on all-optical shift register. The key used for encryption and decryption is an all-optical pseudorandom bit sequence (PRBS). By analysing the performance of the core functional unit of this system, which is composed of SOA-based logic XOR and all-optical clocked D flip-flops, we demonstrated the system's capability of producing stable optical PRBS signals, encrypting/decrypting the optical signals.

articleTitle: Dual-channel all-optical encryption using hybrid modulation format XOR gates based on FWM in HNLF
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-optical encryption/decryption scheme for 10-Gbaud quadrature phase shift keying (QPSK) and binary phase shift keying (BPSK) signals based on hybrid modulation formats exclusive-or (HMF-XOR) gates is proposed. Both theoretical analysis and simulation results are conducted to evaluate the feasibility of optical encryption/decryption scheme. The received OSNR penalties of decrypted QPSK and BPSK signals at BER of 10~<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> are 1dB and 0.7dB, respectively, the concentrated constellations and clear eye-diagrams indicate the high performance of decrypted signals.

articleTitle: Optical fiber humidity sensor based on cascaded peanut-shape structure
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We developed a new technique for constructing humidity sensor comprised of two cascaded peanut-shape structure which were coated with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and in between was also coated with PVA. The coating changes with the humidity which resulting in the change of the effective refractive index, and lead to the change of the interference wavelength. Experiments show that, with the humidity changes between 27%-72%RH, the sensitivity is -0.55336nm/%RH. We also tested its temperature tolerance, and a sensitivity of 0.06135nm/°C within the area of 30-90°C was collected, which shows little influence on humidity sensing when in a relatively stable temperature. Compared with other sensors, our sensor is inexpensive and has a high sensitivity.

articleTitle: High resolution FBG sensor and its applications in Geophysics
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-resolution FBG sensor is proposed for crust deformation observation and earthquake monitoring. A narrow-linewidth tunable fiber laser is used to interrogate the FBG. The wavelength shift of the FBGs due to seismic signal is measured by swept optical suppressed carrier single sideband (SSB-SC) interrogation technique with a reference FBG. The self-noise level is tested to be lower than NHNM. A crust deformation observation experiment is carried out in a seismic monitoring station. The results of clear tidal signals and seismic signals are given.

articleTitle: Fiber vibration sensing technologies based on draw-tower grating arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A distributed vibration sensing system with Michelson interferometer based on width-band ultra-weak fiber Bragg grating (UWFBG) arrays in Draw Tower Grating (DTG) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The precise of the space between adjacent UWFBG is less than 1mm, which is conducive to precise positioning and rapid demodulation. The system is capable of measuring vibrations of up to 1 kHz over 1.6 km with 2.5m spatial resolution.

articleTitle: A new all-fiber LP01/LP02 mode converter in mode division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a new all-fiber mode converter was proposed, which can achieve LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> to LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> mode conversion and vice versa. The proposed mode converter is based on a tapered core and four bipyramids combined structure with annular distribution; the tapered core is used to excite the high-order modes while the bipyramids combined structure curb the undesired high-order modes and make the LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> dominate. A analysis shows that conversion efficiency of 89% and extinction ratio of 12dB over the whole C-band; and the performance of the mode converter is not sensitive to minor changes in structural parameters. The proposed mode converter also can achieve LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> back to LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>.

articleTitle: Real-time data processing algorithm for phase-demodulation distributed fiber-optic vibration sensor with signal-to-noise ratio over 30 dB
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
