abstract: The phase-detection distributed fiber-optic vibration sensor based on time-gated digital optical frequency domain reflectometry has linear response to vibration signals with long measurement distance. However, the computational complexity and large amount of data stream makes it difficult to realize online data processing. This paper introduces the realization of fully pipelined processing system based on field-programmable gate array (FPGA), with which the phase can be extracted in real time. In experiments, an 800 Hz sinusoidal vibration signal is detected along 5 km fibre located at the far end, and the spatial resolution is about 5 m.

articleTitle: A portable pigment concentration measurement system based on optical fiber spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to conveniently measure the concentration of artificial pigments in different solutions, a portable measurement system was developed based on miniature fiber optic spectrometer (MFOS). With this system, the absorbance curves and the absorption coefficients in the visible band for five kinds of artificial pigments in different solutions were measured and calculated. By measuring the concentration of each pigment in mixed pigments solution, the reliability of the system was verified and the experimental results show that the relative error is within ±5%. Finally, with this portable pigment concentration measurement system, we successfully measured the concentration of artificial pigments in Fanta.

articleTitle: 10-Gb/s homodyne receiver based on costas loop with enhanced dynamic performance
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Coherent optical receivers have been widely used in free-space optical communication. We report on a coherent receiver with a homodyne optical phase-locked loop using a Costas loop. Differing from the conventional configuration, the demonstration in this paper with enhanced dynamic performance using an auxiliary acquisition and locking circuitry is able to achieve fast phase locking to signal laser within 10 s at an initial frequency offset as large as +/-12 GHz. The proposed receiver can also compensate for Doppler shifts caused by the relative motion of satellites in real-time. 10-Gb/s Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) data has been demodulated with sensitivity of -39.5 dBm at Bit Error Rate (BER) of 1E-9.

articleTitle: Miniature sensor based on Fiber-graphene-integrated NEMS
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a new fiber-optic current sensor based on graphene nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS) with a graphene membrane covering the hole on a fiber tip and two gold electrodes on opposite sides of the tip. The suspended graphene membrane will deform due to thermal effect when electrical current flows through it. Then the strain in the graphene nanomechanical resonator will change and it leads to the shift of resonant frequency. The proposed sensor is compact and shows a sensitivity as high as ~ 262.5 kHz/mA<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It can also be used for magnetic field sensors based on Lorentz force.

articleTitle: High order remodulation scheme based on R-QDSOA at colorless ONU
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To achieve the better combination of cost and communication capacity, this paper proposes a colourless ONU remodulation scheme based on R-QDSOA in WDM-PON. The R-QDSOA can provide a modulation bandwidth over 20GHz and achieve directly modulation of high-order signal. Here, two remodulation schemes (respectively NRZ/4QAM and 4QAM/NRZ) at different modulation rates are implemented, which offers good BER performance. And the BER would get worse and the input optical power dynamic range would decrease with the increase modulation rate. Then, compared to NRZ/4QAM, 4QAM/NRZ has higher remodulation rate with BER lower the FEC limit, but the waveform jumping will cause burr phenomenon.

articleTitle: Cooperative multi-target tracking with MIMO radar
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Radio fuze has attracted much study in ground-based air-defence artillery field. It requires a high-resolution radar to recognize, position, track and control multiple projectiles. For this, we present a cooperative multiple-target tracking (CMTT) mechanism with MIMO radar, where projectiles can actively transmit signal to radar for target identification, localization, and tracking. The signal is modulated with identified information and detected at radar with receive beamforming. With strict timing synchronization, CMTT is able to provide better precision performance as shown in numerical example.

articleTitle: Measurement of aircraft wing deformation using fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A feasible method of measuring the aircraft wing deformation based on fiber Bragg grating (FBG) is introduced. The strains of the wing can be obtained by means of FBGs attached on the surface of the model airfoil. A finite element model (FEM) is established to obtain the numerical analysis results of strain and deformation of the wing. The experimental deformation of the airfoil can be deduced by analyzing these data through a specific derivation procedure without a mechanical analytic formula. A good agreement can be achieved from the experimental results and direct measurement.

articleTitle: Crack detection in ferromagnetic metal by low frequency magnetic flux leakage technique
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A two-dimension magnetic flux density distribution of the ferromagnetic metal was simulated by using finite element analysis method. From the magnetic flux density distribution, the crack in ferromagnetic metal can be detected through the magnetic flux leakage. Experimental results showed that the magnetic flux density decreased gradually with the increasing of the width and depth of the crack under the width range of 1 to 5 mm and depth range of 0 to 6 mm, respectively.

articleTitle: A novel BV-WSS based flow aggregation (BV-WSS-FA) scheme for finer-grained services in elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The flow aggregation scheme which aggregates a large number of finer-grained services into one large flow can save transceivers and improve spectrum efficiency. It ensures that all services in the aggregated flow have a same routing. Moreover, the spectrum allocated to all finer-grained services in the aggregated flow is continuous. Compared with independent transmission scheme which conducts the distance-adaptive routing and spectrum allocation for each finer-grained service, the flow aggregation scheme consumes more spectrum resource and has a high blocking rate. To address this problem, we proposed a novel BV-WSS based flow aggregation (BV-WSS-FA) scheme which only ensures that the spectrum allocated to all finer-grained services in the aggregated flow is continuous. A heuristic algorithm is designed for BV-WSS-FA. Numerical results show that BV-WSS-FA can greatly reduce network cost without consuming more spectrum resources.

articleTitle: A mode-locked fiber laser generating high purity cylindrical vector beams based on a mode selective coupler in a figure-8 cavity
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate an all-fiber passively mode-locked laser with pulsed cylindrical vector beam output based on a mode selective coupler (MSC) in a figure-8 cavity, The MSC made of a two mode fiber and a standard single mode fiber is used as both the intracavity transverse mode converter and mode splitter. Through adjusting the polarization state in the laser cavity, both radially and azimuthally polarized beams have been obtained with high mode purity which are measured to be > 94%. The mode-locked laser pulses have duration of 17 ns and a repetition rate of 0.66 MHz, operating near a wavelength of 1556.3 nm with a spectral bandwidth of 3.2 nm.

articleTitle: Research on the application of second order remotely pumped amplifier in ultra long haul optical transport network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper reports a 400-km ultra-long haul unrepealed transmission system in a 8×10 Gbit/s optical transmission network (OTN) by using forward Raman amplifier and backward second order remotely optical pumped amplifier(ROPA). A second order ROPA is obtained by adding an auxiliary second order pump to the first order ROPA. Through experiment, we compare the performance of 1st ROPA and 2nd ROPA in a 400-km unrepeated OTN system. We can get 77.5dB loss budget for 1st ROPA and 80.7dB loss budget for 2nd ROPA. More 3.2 dB link budget is got by use of 2nd remote pump.

articleTitle: Characteristic of two cascaded M-Z interferometers based on spherical-shape structures
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Characteristic of two cascaded Mach-Zehnder interferometers based on spherical-shape structures is investigated. When the light in the fiber core is excited into high-order cladding mode, part of the light can propagate along the fiber cladding for a long distance. By cascading two identical interferometers formed by dual spherical-shape structures, it proves that the high-order cladding modes are almost exhausted when they propagated about 50cm along the cladding layer, and they nearly have no influence in the transmission spectrum when they propagate more that 60cm. At the same time, by changing the length and dropping the refractive index liquid between the two cascaded interferometers, it demonstrates that the relative higher cladding mode has lower refractive index and it leaks very fast, so it will propagate a shorter distance, and on the contrary, the relative lower cladding mode has higher refractive index and it leaks slowly, so it will propagates a longer distance.

articleTitle: Optical measurement of special cigarette filter based on OpenCV
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents an automatic optical non-contact measurement method to measure the groove depth, groove number and groove surface area ratio of grooved cigarette filter. After preprocessing of the image of grooved filter, Morphological open operation was used to eliminate false groove detection. Then the contours of outer boundary and grooves were found and the parameters of the filters were calculated. The accuracy of 5 micrometers can be reached.

articleTitle: A novel fabrication method of fiber-tip Fabry-Perot interferometer for high-sensitivity gas-pressure measurements
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel polyvinyl chloride (PVC) diaphragm-based fiber-tip Fabry-Perot interferometer for gas pressure measurements with ultra-high sensitivity. The PVC diaphragm has been coated to the end facet of a well-cut standard single-mode fiber by use of a plastic welder. Ultrahigh pressure sensitivity of ~66.07 nm/MPa at 1565 nm and a low temperature cross-sensitivity of -5.5 KPa/°C have been experimentally demonstrated. The proposed sensor has advantages of high pressure sensitivity, miniature size, low cost and easy fabrication.

articleTitle: Nonlinear parameters of the hybrid graphene-silicon waveguides
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Because of graphene's large nonlinear refractive index, a nonlinear model is established to characterized the nonlinear parameters. With graphene, the nonlinear parameters of the hybrid graphene-silicon waveguides increase tens of times. Figure of merits of such waveguides indicate that graphene could be used to enhance the nonlinear performances of silicon waveguides.

articleTitle: A hybrid plasmonic microfiber knot resonator and mechanical applications
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, a hybrid plasmonic microfiber knot resonator (HPMKR) is demonstrated as well as its multi-sense applications. A microfiber knot resonator (MKR) is attached to gold film and generates the hybrid plasmonic mode. The HPMKR has an extinction ratio of more than 10 dB in C-band, with the Q-factor of more than 47,000. For a chosen polarization, the resonator has an extinction ratio of nearly 15 dB, even though the diameter of the microfiber is more than 5 μm, which is unattainable for a normal MKR. We choose PDMS as the encapsulating material to package the device. Then the device can be utilized as a pressure sensor with sensitivity of 9.34 pm/kPa, and a vibration sensor with the range from tens of hertz to several kilohertz. And our sensor can also be utilized as a wearable health monitor.

articleTitle: Building the ECO-system for the digital electro-optics platform (X-on Silicon)
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Digital Electro-optics Platform is the main concept of Jasper Display Corp. (JDC) to develop various applications. These applications are based on our X-on-Silicon technologies, for example, X-on-Silicon technologies could be used on Liquid Crystal on Silicon (LCoS), Micro Light-Emitting Diode on Silicon (μLEDoS), Organic Light-Emitting Diode on Silicon (OLEDoS), and Cell on Silicon (CELLoS), etc. LCoS technology is applied to Micro Display, Spatial Light Modulator (SLM), Dynamic Optics, Wavelength Selective Switch (WSS), Holographic Display, Microscopy, Bio-tech, 3D Printing and Adaptive Optics, etc. In addition, μLEDoS technology is applied to Augmented Reality (AR), Head Up Display (HUD), Head-mounted Display (HMD), and Wearable Devices.

articleTitle: Improving extinction radio in few-mode fiber interferometer with small-mode-area single mode fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The comb filters consist of few mode fiber and standard single mode fiber suffer from low extinction radio. Replacing standard single mode fiber with small-mode-area fiber can better the balance excitation in few mode fiber, thus improve the extinction radio. A lab-made small-mode-area single mode fiber was utilized to a commercial few mode fiber and increase the extinction radio from 2.5dB to 6.5dB. The effect of repeat fusion is also presented.

articleTitle: Multiple dedicated end-to-service path protection (MDESPP) scheme in optical distributed datacenter networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To improve the local accessibility performance, some important services are usually replicated and maintained in multiple datacenters. A user can request any datacenter which hosts the required service. The traditional end-to-end path is gradually replaced by the end-to-service path. To resist the frequently occurred natural disasters or human-made faults, survivability technologies need to be deployed. The dedicated path protection scheme which is simple and easily conducted has become a practical approach to deal with random concurrent multi-failures. In this paper, we study the multiple dedicated end-to-service path protection (MDESPP) scheme in optical distributed datacenter networks (ODDNs). An Integer Linear Program (ILP) formulation and a heuristic algorithm are developed for the MDESPP scheme. Numerical results show that the proposed MDESPP scheme can greatly improve success rate compared with traditional end-to-end path protection, and is easy to be conducted.

articleTitle: A planning method of grouping ONUs based on load balancing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of large scale, huge load and different service requirements of the ethernet passive optical network (EPON), a new networking strategy, grouping management of optical network units (ONU), is proposed. In this paper, we first consider the economy, network delay and load balance, and establish the cost model, the load balance model and the network delay model. Secondly, we plan the number and location of access points (AP) and the method of grouping ONUs, and use the genetic simulated annealing algorithm to obtain the optimal grouping scheme of ONUs. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that the ONUs grouping method proposed in this paper can achieve the optimal cost of network construction, at the same time the method also can meet the requirements of network delay and load balance.

articleTitle: High-sensitivity quasi-distributed temperature sensors based on weak FBGs Fabry-Perot structure with metal coating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This letter puts forward weak FBGs Fabry-Perot (FP) structures with copper coating for quasi-distributed temperature measurement. The weak FBGs (−33dB) are fabricated by on-line draw tower. The sensors system exhibits the superiorities of high signal to noise ratio (SNR). At the same time, wavelength/frequency/time multiplexing immensely increases the capacity of the sensing system. In the experiment, the sensors show the high temperature sensitivity, reaching to 24.68 pm/°C because of the sensors deposited metal film. The results imply the feasibility of high-sensitivity quasi-distributed temperature measurement.

articleTitle: Rapid identification of plastics based on Raman spectroscopy with the combination of support vector machine
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A rapid method for identification of plastics based on Raman spectroscopy with the combination of support vector machine (SVM) is presented in this paper. Plastics studied consist of polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polymethyl methacrylate, polyacetal, polypropylene, polystyrene and polyvinyl chloride. With spectral preprocessing and principal component analysis (PCA), support vector machine model for identification of plastics was established. The results show that the presented method can identify the plastics rapidly with accuracy of 100%. Indicating that support vector machine used to rapid identification of plastics performs well based on Raman spectroscopy.

articleTitle: A research of media access control for indoor VLC LAN based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A MAC protocol for indoor VLC LAN based on CSMA/CA is described in the paper. Theoretically, the protocol can do well in solving HTP and terminal motion. We adopt RTS/CTS mechanism to avoid transmission collision among terminals. Also, an appropriate frame format based on IEEE 802.3 and IEEE 802.11 is proposed, contributing to solve HTP and terminal motion problem. At last, we established a demo system which supports one-to-two full-duplex communication. The work affords solid practical basis for Point-To-Multipoint (P2MP) VLC system.

articleTitle: The technology of distributed electric grid fiber Raman temperature sensing for intelligent
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A temperature demodulation method by using compensation of fiber attenuation and dispersion for distributed temperature sensors (DTS) is proposed and demonstrated in order to improve the DTS measuring speed and accuracy. Firstly, the attenuation coefficients difference between anti-Stokes and Stokes backscattering is modified, which avoids the calibration processing on the entire sensing optical fiber and reduces system operation time. Secondly, dispersion shift algorithm is applied to correct the position of Stokes backscattering, and then the intensity of Stokes backscattering can be obtained at the same position with anti-Stokes backscattering, which eliminates the influence of optical fiber dispersion on temperature demodulation and improves the accuracy of temperature measurement.

articleTitle: Square pulses from an all-polarization-maintained dumbbell-shaped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper· we demonstrate a Yb-doped· all-polarization-maintained· dumbbell-shaped fiber laser operating in dissipative soliton resonance regime. A nonreciprocal phase shifter is introduced to a reflective nonlinear optical loop mirror to reduce the self-starting threshold. The duration of the square pulses generated can be adjusted from 207ps to 20.6 ns by increasing pump power. Up to 512 nJ energetic and pulse-breaking-free pulses are obtained. The repetition rate is 3.97 MHz and the corresponding average output power reaches 2.04 W. To the best of our knowledge· this is the first reported DSR pulse in an all-PM dumbbell-shaped fiber laser.

articleTitle: Research on the characteristics of microfiber coupler
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The Optical transmission characteristics of microfiber coupler in micron dimension were analyzed. The optical field distribution between two fibers was gotten by numerical simulation with beam propagation method, and then the variation of the output light power of the coupler with different length is obtained. Based on the experimental platform for the production of microfiber coupler, the energy value of two output ports of microfiber coupler in the 10mm to 35mm stretching length range is analyzed. The simulation and experimental results show that the energy of two output ports is transferred periodically with the change of tensile length. Along with the increase of the stretch length, the loss of coupler is further increased. This provide useful reference for further optimization of the production technology and process of microfiber coupler.

articleTitle: A 13.8-W, high-efficiency, α-cut Tm, Ho:YAP laser pumped by two laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a high-power, high-efficiency Tm, Ho:YAlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (Tm, Ho:YAP) laser pumped by two laser diodes. The Tm (5 at.%) and Ho (0.5 at.%):YAP crystal is cut along the a axes, and the resulting crystals are measured 4 × 4 × 8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The laser crystal is double end-pumped by two 18.0-W fiber-coupled laser diodes at 793.6 nm, and the output power of the Tm, Ho:YAP laser is 13.8W in continuous wave (CW) mode operation. An optical-optical conversion efficiency of 38.3% is acquired, corresponding to a slope efficiency of 40.6%.

articleTitle: Best match algorithm in time and wavelength division multiplexed passive optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Recently Time and Wavelength Division Multiplexed Passive Access Network (TWDM-PON) supporting 40Gb/s transmission rate becomes the main trend. If the ONU has some problems and cannot send data using the allocated bandwidth (i.e., ONU is failed), the bandwidth will be wasted. In this paper, we propose a Best Match Algorithm(BM) to reduce this waste. We put the traffic of ONUs into matching wavelength and time slots to improve the bandwidth utilization as soon as possible. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can reduce the average time delay and increase the bandwidth utilization, especially when a larger number of failed ONUs are involved in the resource optimization algorithm.

Author Keywords: Time and Wavelength Division Multiplexed Passive Optical Network

articleTitle: In-line Mach-Zehnder interferometric refractive index sensor based on concatenating two single-mode fiber half-tapers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An in-line Mach-Zehnder interferometric refractive index (RI) sensor is demonstrated by concatenating two single-mode fiber (SMF) half-tapers separated by one section of SMF. The cladding modes excited at the first half-taper interferes with the core mode at the second half-taper to generate the interference fringe. Theoretical and experimental results consistently show that the interference fringe shifts toward shorter wavelengths with the external RI sensitivity of 102.3 nm/RIU in the monitoring RI range from 1.333 to 1.413. In addition, the sensing device may endure the axial stress more than 3200 με with the strain sensitivity of 1.72 pm/με.

articleTitle: A novel joint timing/frequency offset estimation algorithm for CO-OFDM system with low OSNR
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A joint timing offset (TO) and frequency offset (FO) estimation method based on Radon-Wigner transform (RWT) is first proposed for coherent optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (CO-OFDM) systems. The result shows that the timing and frequency synchronization performance of the proposed method are both better than the Schmidl & Cox method and fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) algorithm in a poor OSNR condition.

articleTitle: An OADM based on cascaded phase-shifted linearly chirped fiber grating and Mach-Zehnder interferometer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a new structure of optical add-drop multiplexer based on cascaded phase shifted linearly chirped fiber Bragg grating (CPSLCFBG) and Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) is proposed. The spectrum of drop port and output port of the OADM is analyzed using transmission matrix method by optimizing of CPSLCFBG with Cap apodization function. At the port of the drop and the output, which has equidistant multi channels with almost equal output power and very narrow bandwidth, even about 40 channels, and the transmission performance is very good.

Author Keywords: cascaded phase shifted linearly chirped fiber Bragg grating

articleTitle: 1.6W multi-wavelength YDF based random fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated experimentally a stable 1μm multi-wavelength YDF based random fiber laser by using a polarization independent Sagnac-loop mirror with output power of 1.6W and high OSNR of 30dB.

articleTitle: Investigation of amplification characteristic for DPSK signal in SOA
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The amplification characteristics of DPSK signal in semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) is numerically simulated and experimentally demonstrated for the first time. The results show that the bit pattern effect (BPE) of the DPSK signal is induced by SOA. According to the results, when pulsewidth of the signal is comparable to the gain recovery time of SOA, the BPE is severe. And when the pulsewidth of the signal becomes much larger or shorter than the gain recovery time of SOA, the BPE is alleviated. In addition, the experiment results show that by adjusting the injection current of SOA, the BPE can be alleviated effectively.

articleTitle: Arbitrary picosecond pulse shaping in a radially polarized Yb-fiber MOPA beyond 10 W
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous spatial and arbitrary temporal pulse-shaping with a picosecond Yb-doped fiber laser system generating an output power > 10 W. By using a self-developed feed-back control algorithm on a single polarization optical pulse shaper, we obtained arbitrary complex pulse structures in the time domain with high accuracy and at high power level. Meanwhile, the pulse shaping in the spatial domain has been achieved using an in-house S-waveplate to change the linearly polarized fundamental mode into doughnut modes with different polarizations each at a time. This new capability enhances the versatility of ultrashort fiber laser systems for high precision material processing. Directly amplifying the radially polarized doughnut-mode avoids complex beam conversion at the output and provides an efficient route for power-scaling.

articleTitle: A graphene-on-gap modulator with high modulation efficiency
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a high efficient graphene-on-gap modulator (GOGM) by employing the hybrid plasmonic effect, whose modulation efficiency is ~8-folds larger than that of present graphene-on-silicon modulator (GOSM) (~0.1 dB / μm). The proposed modulator has the advantage of short modulation length ~3.6 μm, relatively low insertion loss ~0.32 dB and larger modulation bandwidth ~0.48 THz. Moreover, an efficient taper coupler has been designed to convert the quasi-transverse electric (TE) mode of conventional silicon waveguide to the hybrid plasmonic mode of GOGM, with a high coupling efficiency of 91%. This study may promote the design of high-performance on-chip electro-optical modulator.

articleTitle: DMT for metro applications without optical dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For metro applications, direct detection offers the advantages of low cost and low complexity. Discrete multi-tone (DMT) is a promising format due to its high spectral efficiency, flexibility and tolerance to chromatic dispersion (CD). In this work, single-side-band-DMT (SSB-DMT) and tuneable electrical dispersion compensation double side-band-DMT (TEDC-DSB-DMT) are summarized and compared.

articleTitle: Low repetition rate microsecond square pulse generation in a passively mode-locked Yb-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate that a low repetition rate, all-fiber passively mode-locked Yb-doped fiber laser through nonlinear polarization rotation (NPR). A 1000 m long single-mode fiber (SMF) is inserted into the cavity to lower the repetition rate. The laser operates in dissipative soliton resonance (DSR) region and generates stable square pulses with a 202.3 kHz fundamental repetition rate. When the pump power increases, the pulse duration and output power increase linearly, but the peak power keeps unchanged. The maximum pulse duration is 1.25 μs at the pump power of 540 mW. The maximum average power of output pulses is 3.16 mW, which corresponds to single pulse energy of 15.6 nJ.
