articleTitle: Effect of grating mirrors size on focusing reflectors based on two-dimensional high-contrast sub-wavelength gratings
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present an approach to design focusing reflectors using two-dimensional sub-wavelength gratings (2D SWGs). The effect of the grating reflecting mirrors size on the reflection focusing performance is investigated. The performance parameters considered mainly include focal length, phase change, numerical aperture. Using COMSOL software, the simulation results show that the focal length are affected by the grating reflecting mirrors size. The larger grating mirror (at least the total phase change of 3% angle) has better focusing behavior, this conclusion provides some suggestions for our design and fabrication of reflective convergence grating.

articleTitle: L-band dispersion-managed mode-locked fiber laser incorporating carbon-nanotube-based saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have investigated L-band dispersion-managed mode-locked (DMML) fiber laser incorporating carbon-nanotube saturable absorbers. For the first time, the DMML fiber laser operates at 1595 nm with the net cavity dispersion changing from -0.34 to -0.20 ps<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, showing that the spectral bandwidth can be broadened by 39%.

articleTitle: Twin-core few-mode fiber Bragg gratings inscribed by femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated femtosecond laser inscription of fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) in a twin-core few-mode fiber (TC-FMF) for directional bend sensing. An FBG was selectively inscribed in one core of the TC-FMF by using an 800 nm femtosecond laser through a phase mask. Three resonance peaks at the wavelengths of 1549.05, 1547.65, and 1546.08 nm were observed in the reflection spectrum of the TC-FM FBG, and were generated by the LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode resonance, LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>-LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode cross-coupling resonance, and LP11 mode resonance, respectively.

articleTitle: Random number generation using a spectrum-expanded chaotic signal at 300 Gb/s
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a scheme for fast random number generation with a bandwidth-enhanced chaotic signal generated by injecting the signal of a traditional chaotic external-cavity semiconductor laser (ECSL) into a spectrum expansion module (SE). Our simulation results show that the bandwidth-enhanced chaotic can be generated and its efficient bandwidth can be greatly enhanced up to 70 GHz. Random bits in our scheme are generated by bitwise exclusive-OR(XOR) operation on corresponding bits in samples of the bandwidth-enhanced chaotic signal and its time-delayed signal. An output bit rate of 300 Gb/s is attained by retaining 6 least significant bits (LSBs) per sample at the sampling rate of 50GSa/s.

articleTitle: Effect of haze on the performance of free space optical communication
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the haze attenuation of laser affects the performance of free space optical communication (FSOC). The Haze is regarded as coated particles, which considers haze as the inner and droplet aerosol as the outer core. Based on the coated scattering theory of Christian Mätzler, the scattering model of haze aerosols is established. According to the Meteorological Bureau, the fitting relationship between atmospheric visibility V and PM 2.5 Index is obtained and the relationship between spectral distribution of aerosol particles and PM2.5 Index is derived. When the laser propagates along arbitrary paths, the attenuation coefficient of the laser is calculated by using the mathematical method. According to the different positions of the transmitter and receiver, FSOC can be divided into three situations. Finally, the effect of haze on different situations are discussed.

articleTitle: Research on the application of semiconductor optical amplifier in 100G local area network/data center
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The growing data traffic in the local area networks (LAN) is driving development of the cost-effective transmission systems. In this paper, we investigate the influence of a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) on the transmission system of 60 km standard single-mode fiber (SSMF) in the 1310 nm wavelength-division-multiplexed (WDM) system. We investigate the SOA performance and analyze the receiver sensitivity improvement during the transmission over the link consisting of 100G based LR4 and a pre SOA. It performed that the 4×25 system is operating error-free on all channels without any form of the chromatic dispersion compensation or error correction.

articleTitle: Optical fiber sensing system for temperature and strain simultaneously measurement based on low coherence interferometers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A system based on the Mach-Zehnder low-coherence interferometer for simultaneously measurement in the field of temperature and strain is presented. This system utilizes the principle of the optical path difference modulation and the coherence length modulation in the low coherence interferometer. After frequently testing the interference signal influenced by the temperature and the strain, the sensitivity of the system is obtained. The stability and the multiplexed capability of the system are also investigated.

articleTitle: All-fiber fused-type mode selective coupler with high performance and free of pre-tapering
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper we propose and demonstrate a novel all-fiber fused-type mode selective coupler (MSC) that capable of converting LP01 mode to LP11 mode with high efficiency and purity. Unlike other coupler fabrication techniques for which single mode fiber (or few mode fiber) must be pre-tapered, the advantage of our proposed coupler is that pre-tapering is not required. Two different fibers of the MSC have the same diameter. We achieve LP11 mode with a high modal purity of > 90% and a coupling efficiency of >20%, with a low insertion loss of about 0.3 dB at the wavelength of 1064 nm.

articleTitle: Study on sensing characteristics of phase shifted fiber grating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Phase shifted fiber grating (PSFG) is a kind of important fiber gratings in optical communication, but is seldom used in optical sensing. Based on the coupled mode theory and transfer matrix method, the transmission and reflection spectra of PSFG has been theoretically studied. Then the strain and temperature characteristic of PSFG has been simulated using OptiGrating software. The simulation results show that the strain sensitivity is about 1.216pm/με and the temperature sensitivity is about 0.0124nm/°C. This work is useful for optimizing design of optical sensors based on PSFG.

articleTitle: Offshore verification research on the flexible ATP technology
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We get the sailing opportunities of YW 21 and YW22 ships, and carry out the marine atmospheric laser communication channel test and terminal verification experiment. We develop the experimental equipment including marine atmospheric laser communication terminal and the atmospheric parameter measuring equipment. The stability and tracking data of the communication terminal are obtained, and the optical parameters of the channel are measured. In this paper, the experimental results of the key technology of artificial light assisted ATP are presented.

articleTitle: Intermediate state between dissipative soliton and amplifier similariton in ANDi ultrafast fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We make a theoretical demonstration of the transformation from the dissipative soliton to amplifier similariton in an all-normal dispersion fiber laser for the first time. An intermediate state between the dissipative soliton and amplifier similariton is proposed and we call it the “Dissipative similariton” considering its shaping mechanism and characteristics. Pulse regimes dynamics is thoroughly explored. The chirp evolution together with pulse structures in time and frequency domains can be used to distinguish the three pulse regimes. We think our work can enrich the pulse dynamics in all-normal dispersion fiber lasers and help one to design high-energy ultrashort pulse configurations.

articleTitle: Liquid-core photonic crystal fiber based plasmonic sensor with selective analyte channels
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present and numerically characterize a single liquid-core photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor. The two gold coated liquid analyte channels as big as core are placed near the core for easy excitation of free electrons to produce surface plasmon waves (SPWs). A sufficiently strong SPR is achieved by adjusting the size of the air holes between the core and the liquid analyte channels. The maximum positive refractive index (RI) sensitivity of3800nm/RIU is achieved in the sensing range of 1.45-1.46. The sensor shows a negative RI sensitivity once the RI of the analyte is greater than 1.5.

articleTitle: Mushroom-mesa vertical incidence photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we studied the effect of mushroom-mesa structure on vertical incidence PIN photodiodes based on theory and experiments. A novel mushroom-mesa vertical incidence photodiode was fabricated. The 20-um-diameter mushroom-mesa photodiode with a 0.5-um absorption layer achieved a 3 dB bandwidth of 24.1 GHz, which increased 39.3% compared with PIN photodiodes.

articleTitle: Spectral characteristics of CH4-filled hollow-core fiber Raman laser amplifier
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A 1.5 μm tunable CW single-frequency seed laser is injected into the methane-filled negative curvature hollow-core fiber, and then amplified by stimulated Raman scattering of methane molecule. The Stokes linewidth is measured at the output using a scanning Fabry-Perot interferometer. When the wavelength of the seed laser is tuned to the Stokes transition and the polarization direction of the seed laser and the pump laser is nonorthogonal, the introduction of the seed laser significantly narrows the Stokes linewidth. This paper paves a feasible way to obtain high power· narrow linewidth laser output in gas filled hollow-core fiber by stimulated Raman scattering.

articleTitle: Envelope-based demodulation for temperature sensing with cascaded fiber Fabry-Perot interferometers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A temperature sensor with two cascaded fiber Fabry-Perot interferometers (FPIs) is constructed and demonstrated, which works on envelope-based demodulation and exhibits a high temperature sensitivity. The sensor is fabricated by splicing a short segment of large mode area (LMA) fiber to a short segment of capillary tube fused with a section of single-mode fiber to form a cascaded FPI structure. Experimental results show that the temperature sensitivity achieves up to 249.22 pm/V by using envelope-based demodulation, which is much higher than the one obtained by directly tracing the resonant wavelength in the superposition interference spectrum or the one for a single FPI with air-cavity. Moreover, the proposed sensor is compact with dimension of <;1 mm. All the features make it promising for temperature measuring in many fields.

articleTitle: Coherent communication experiment based on 7-core fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, wavelength division multiplexing and space division multiplexing (WDM-SDM) passive optical access network employing multi-core fiber (MCF) and self-homodyne detection is proposed. 4×56-Gb/s PDM-16QAM-OFDM transmission is realized over 10-km 7-core fiber with simplified digital signal processing.

articleTitle: Burst-mode supercontinuum generation with versatile shapes
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we reported an all-fiber burst-mode supercontinuum (SC) laser source which spanned from 0.8 to 3.2μm. The SC laser was generated within a 50-cm long Germania core fiber. The pump of the SC laser was an amplified nanosecond burst-mode laser pulse train at 1550 nm, which took pulse-pumping to suppress amplified spontaneous emission (ASE). In our experiment, the repetition rate of the burst-mode pulse was set to 570 Hz. Each burst-mode pulse contains 10 pulses with durations of 10 ns and pulse-to-pulse intervals of 10μs. The total SC power was 61.2mW. Versatile burst-mode SC laser was realized in this work.

articleTitle: Research on underwater explosive system based on airborne laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Laser underwater detection technology is widely used in seawater ranging, mine detection, positioning and other fields. This article is for airborne laser underwater exploration submarine technology, proposed a kind of airborne laser underwater exploration submarine system program, the system composition and working process are discussed, the energy link model of trans-atmosphere and seawater is focused on building, including atmospheric attenuation, gas-water boundary attenuation, seawater attenuation, etc. On this basis, the feasibility of energy link is analyzed, through analysis it is feasible to propose an airborne laser underwater exploration system.

articleTitle: Improving the refractive index sensitivity of long period fiber grating with coating ZnO thin film
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Comparing with uncoated LPFGs, ZnO coated LPFG shows obvious improvement of RI sensitivity between the RI range of 1.4 and 1.62. The proposed structure exhibits a very high sensitivity of 5175 nm/RIU in the RI range from 1.444 to 1.448, and the sensitivity could be further improved by optimizing the thickness of the ZnO thin film.

articleTitle: Design of solution pigment concentration detection system based on optical fiber spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A system based on fiber spectrometer was designed to detect the concentration of various artificial pigments contained in the solution. Using this system, the absorbance curves of five kinds of artificial colors of lemon yellow, sunset yellow, carmine, bright blue and amaranth were measured, and the absorption coefficient of each pigment at different wavelengths was calculated. The reliability of the system verifies by detecting the concentration of each pigment in mixed pigments solution, the experimental results show that the relative error is within 5%. Further, the system was used to detect the concentration of artificial pigments in a series of fruit flavor sodas of Coca-Cola company.

articleTitle: High-sensitive torsion sensing based on chiral long-period gratings
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: High-reproducible chiral long-period gratings (CLPGs) are achieved, which are fabricated from normal single mode fibers. To explore torsion sensing application, we investigate the response trend of transmission spectrum versus mechanical twist rate in CLPGs. High torsion sensitivity is achieved, a perfect linear relationship between the resonance wavelength shift and the mechanical twist rate is displayed.

articleTitle: Loss reduction of hybrid single-polarization fiber ring resonator by white light interferometer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By using a white light interferometer to monitor the angular misalignment at a splicing point between a polarization-maintaining fiber and a single-polarization fiber, a low loss hybrid single-polarization fiber ring resonator with a round-trip loss of 0.98dB is fabricated. The misaligned angle at each splicing point is reduced from 10° to 1°, and the average splice loss is reduced by approximately 0.147dB.

articleTitle: Research on calibration of demodulation loss of receiver
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To solve the problem of the deviation of the demodulation threshold which is caused by quoting demodulation loss from the specification, a measuring method based on relationship between E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and Bit error rate (BER) in theory is proposed. Utilizing the inverse-function of BER and the BER measured actually, the E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> in theory corresponding to the measured BER can be calculated. After multi times of measuring and calculating in different bit rate, a serial average data is obtained. And the difference of E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>/N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> between the transmitter and the average which is got from receiver is the demodulation loss, so a curve of demodulation loss versus bit rate can be build. 3 digital baseband equipment were tested, the demodulation loss is different from each other, and the maximum deviation is 1.4dB from the specification. The result proves that using the method discussed above is more accurate than quoting the specification and better for reflecting the individual characteristics.

articleTitle: A novel microfiber refractometric sensor fabricated with tapering-twisting-tapering technique
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a novel microfiber refractive index sensor prepared with tapering-twisting-tapering technique has been proposed and demonstrated for the first time. Experimental results show that the interference intensity of the novel microfiber increases with the increment of pre-tapered length and the intervening twist number. Furthermore, the refractive index sensitivity of this microfiber sensor can reach to ~809 nm/refractive index unit (RIU) in the refractive index ranging from 1.30 to 1.33. Taking advantages of its tiny size, easy preparation and flexible design, the novel microfiber has great potential application in refractive index sensing.

articleTitle: Application research in integrated navigation system of measurement ship based on multiple data fusion technology
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For the problem gyro drift error caused by a long time running of inertial navigation system, Raising data fusion and realtime filtering method, Kalman filter is used to fuse data from modify Global Positioning System(GPS), inertial navigation system(INS), celestial navigation system(CNS), ESGM measurement ship and combined navigation system, and then introducing dynamic real-time fitering method (UKF) to resolve the problem that off-time model can't describe its process changes accurately, test result is uniform with the analysis of higher precision SINS. it proves that Accuracy of Navigation System pf measurement ship can be inproved effectively with above method.

articleTitle: Research on absorption line profile of acetylene gas by changing environmental
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Detection of trace chemicals sensitively and selectively is important for environmental, safety and industrial process monitoring. Based on erbium-doped photonic crystal fibre (ED-PCF) laser intra-cavity absorption spectroscopy detection technology, analyzing the infrared absorption spectrum of acetylene (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) gas. The relationship between the gas concentration and the absorption of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> at the normal temperature is studied. Experimental results show that the self-broadening coefficient and the air collision widening coefficient of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas are (0.12065±0.00784) cm-1/atm and (0.12744±0.00244) cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>/atm in 1532.8nm absorption line, respectively. In addition, with the increase of C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> concentration, the centre wavelength of the absorption peak redshift.

articleTitle: An antenna pattern imprint method for sea based space tracking mission analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The mission analysis for tracking ships are one of the most import works for sea based spacecraft tracking and control. Many constraints such as access interval, tracking site maritime condition, coverage and antenna pattern have to be considered in the analysis. In the past mission analyses, antenna patterns of spacecraft transceivers were commonly simplified as the parameter half cone. However, the simplification sometimes neglects the possible dumb area in the pattern, and it could even cause flash-off of signal and loss of tracking in some missions. The paper proposes an antenna pattern imprint method for sea based space tracking mission analysis. The method provides a visualized constraint for the analysis. The method is convenient and beneficial for the quantification of sea based space tracking mission analysis.

articleTitle: The rising power of random fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report on the demonstration of a 418 W high power random fiber laser, which is the highest power to the best of our knowledge. The random laser is a half-open cavity based on 130 meters long passive fiber with core diameter of 20 μm. It is pumped by 1070 nm Yb-doped fiber laser. The central wavelength of 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> order random laser is 1120 nm. The output power, spectral, and temporal characters are carefully discussed. The results show that such cavity can export random laser effectively. The presented work provides an impactful method to advance the output power of random fiber laser.

articleTitle: Chaos synchronization in semiconductor lasers subject to phase-conjugate feedback
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Chaos synchronization in closed-loop external cavity semiconductor lasers subject to phase-conjugate feedback is investigated theoretically and numerically. We theoretically analysed the injection-locking synchronization condition and numerically confirm it. The simulation results indicate that with introduction of feedback phase difference according to the theoretical synchronization condition, high quality chaos synchronization can be achieved as the conventional optical feedback scenario.

articleTitle: Influence of doping concentration on thermal stability of PMF crossstalk
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We investigate the temperature dependence of CrossTalk (CT) for PANDA Polarization maintaining fiber (PMF). The test temperature ranges from −55 to 85 °C, and the tested fiber was loose wound. The mismatch in thermal expansion coefficient between the boron-doped parts and the core can be varied by controlling the doping concentration in the stress and core regions. The whole temperature CT variation of optimized PMF would be reduced to <2.3dB. This characteristic is important for the real application of PANDA PMFs in temperature-insensitive fiber interferometers, fiber sensors, and optical fiber gyroscopes.

articleTitle: Modal investigation of whispering gallery mode microtube resonators fabricated by laser machining
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrated the modal investigation of whispering gallery mode (WGM) microtube resonators fabricated by laser machining to characterize their dispersion property for Kerr frequency comb generation. We designed and fabricated microtube resonators by CO2 laser machining of fused quartz tubes. The finite element simulations were implemented to determine the quality factor with high accuracy and demonstrate the dispersion of the microtube resonators. The influences of outside diameters and side wall curvature radii of microtube resonators on dispersion are also demonstrated, which is of critical importance to the generation of Kerr frequency combs in a monolithic microresonator.

articleTitle: Multi-channel frequency-tunable optical sinusoidal wave generation using a self-starting optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical sinusoidal wave generation on four channels simultaneously is experimental demonstrated using a self-starting optoelectronic oscillator. The frequency of the sinusoidal wave can be widely tuned from 25 GHz to 200 GHz with 25-GHz spacing. The timing jitter of the microwave signal extracted from the oscillator is measured to be 218 fs.

articleTitle: Thermally robust composite phosphor ceramic makes solid state laser lighting come true
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Solid state laser lighting is a newly emerging technology that combines a blue laser diode (LD) with a yellow-emitting phosphor converter to generate high-brightness white light. Due to high flux irradiation as well as thermal attacks from the incident laser, this technology draws a demanding requirement on the thermal performance of the phosphor converter. In this work, we design a Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-YAG:Ce composite ceramic with a unique microstructure, where yellow-emitting YAG:Ce particles are embedded in a non-luminescent Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> matrix. The composite ceramic exhibits a high thermal conductivity of 18.5 Wm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> and a remarkable improvement in thermal stability (15% improvement at 300 °C). When irradiated under a high power density of 5000 Wcm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>, the output luminous flux increases linearly as the incident current increases from 0.4 to 1.6 A, validating its superior reliability in high-power solid state laser lighting.

articleTitle: Fabrication of microtapered/helical long-period fiber gratings with a CO2 laser fusion splicer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new scheme for fabricating microtapered long-period fiber gratings (LPFGs) and helical LPFGs is proposed and demonstrated successfully by periodically tapering and twisting a standard single-mode fiber, respectively, using a CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser fusion splicer as heater. In comparison to previous fabrication methods, our scheme can significantly improve the quality of the microtapered and helical LPFGs. Considering the simple and flexible fabrication process as well as the high quality of fabricated gratings, we believe that this may offer a simpler and alternative choice to current filters or sensing applications.

articleTitle: Cladding-pumped Erbium-Ytterbium co-doped random fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An Erbium-Ytterbium co-doped random fiber laser (EYRFL) operating at 1550 nm is demonstrated for the first time. The laser cavity consists of a 5-m-long Er/Yb co-doped fiber and a 2-km-long single-mode fiber that provides random distributed feedback. We experimentally achieve 2.14 W of 1550 nm random lasing at 9.62W of 976 nm LD pump power. The laser exhibits a linear output with the slope efficiency as 20.7%. This work provides a promising way to boost the output power of 1.5μm random fiber laser.

articleTitle: Improved practical polarization mode dispersion (PMD) measurement based on fixed analyzer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have researched and compared several practical PMD measurement method, and improved the practical PMD measurement based on fixed analyzer. Using polarization controller results in a more stable system and more accurate result. Algorithms are launched to judge the extreme value points in the spectrum to get a more precise result.

articleTitle: A single-longitudinal-mode, narrow linewidth fiber ring laser stabilized by taper-coupled double-microsphere-cavities
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel fiber ring laser utilizing taper-coupled double-microsphere-cavities (TC-DMC) to stabilize its single-longitudinal-mode operating with a 0.01 nm narrow bandwidth. Fundamental properties including whispery gallery mode (WGM) mode distribution and transmission spectra in the DMC are investigated both theoretically and experimentally. Due to Vernier effect, the WGM spectrum of the DMC has a narrower FWHM which is compressed about 29.3% and the FSR is increased about 5.3%, as compared to the single-microsphere cavity. A 1.5 μm wavelength single-longitudinal-mode fiber ring laser with a bandwidth of 0.01 nm is also demonstrated using the taper-coupled double-microsphere-cavities (TC-DMC) as the all-fiber mode selector.

articleTitle: Design of flexible material self-adaptive deviation-correcting system based on image processing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: To solve the problem of deviation of flexible material in the process of printing and packaging, a self-adaptive deviation-correcting control system was suggested based on a combination of picture processing and fuzzy PID control. This paper has introduced the working principle of deviation-correcting system, the sensor was used to detect the edge of packaging material, the deviation value was obtained by picture processing and analysis, the drive signal was generated accordingly by the deviation-correcting algorithm to realize the control of deviation-correcting device. To realize an identification of packaging material edge, a picture processing algorithm was proposed including the picture preprocessing, edge recognition and so on. Meanwhile a deviation-correcting controller was designed based on the fuzzy PID principle, the self-adaptive adjustment of PID controlling parameter was realized on the basis of fuzzy rule. Finally, a deviation-correcting controlling system was built and the relevant tests were conducted. The system deviation can be controlled within 1mm with a high control precision and ideal steady-state performance. The mentioned deviation-correcting system can meet the demand for running precision of flexible material by the printing and packaging.

articleTitle: Novel frontiers in the stabilization of FD-FWM microcombs
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this contribution, we will review our recent activities in the development of double nested cavity lasers. Several stable operating regimes can be achieved over a wide range of conditions.

articleTitle: The scheduling strategy of network resource in software defined optical network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In order to virtualize the optical resources and support as required, software-defined optical networks (SDON) can dynamically customize the structure and function of the optical network using the software programming method according to the requirements of the users and operators. Each layer in SDON architecture has a lot of core technology. In this paper, we focus on the dynamic scheduling and optimization strategy of SDON network resources, introduce the virtualization technology of network resources and propose a load-balancing virtual mapping algorithm.

articleTitle: Both channel and phase noise blind recover for DDO-OFDM
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Both channel and phase noise blind recover are proposed and demonstrated to recover the orthogonal-frequency-division-multiplexing (OFDM) signal without using any training symbols or pilot subcarriers in direct-detection optical OFDM. The proposed receivers can achieve similar performance compared to conventional OFDM receivers.

articleTitle: Design and experimental characterization of 1×2 silicon optical switch
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design and fabricate a silicon based 1×2 optical switch based on the free-carrier plasma dispersion effect, with a Mach-Zehnder interferometer structure on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) wafer. The experimental result shows that it has an extinction ratio of 21.8 dB at 1546 nm, which meets the requirements of the most applications in optical telecommunication networks.

articleTitle: Low phase noise frequency- and full 360° phase-tunable microwave generation based on an optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Frequency and full 360° phase tunable microwave signal generation based on an optoelectronic oscillator is experimentally demonstrated. Frequency tunable 8-24 GHz and full 360° phase shift are obtained. The single-sideband phase noise of the generated microwave signal is measured to be -122 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset.

articleTitle: The simulation of monolithic vertical integration of VCSEL and RCE photodiode
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we present a monolithic vertical integration of a 850nm wavelength AlGaAs/GaAs-based vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL) and a 810nm wavelength AlGaAs/GaAs-based resonant cavity enhanced photodetector(RCE-PD). The receiving and transmitting of optical signals on two different wavelengths can be realized simultaneously by the single transceiving chip. Simulations show that, the VCSEL can reach a threshold current of 1mA, with a maximum slope efficiency of 0.66W/A, while the RCE PD has a quantum efficiency of 90.24% at the same time. And the two integrated devices are fully decoupled both on the electrical properties and the optical properties. The proposed transceiving chip are focused on improving the performance of optical interconnect applications in data centers.

articleTitle: Broadband and scalable RF switch matrix based on microwave photonics
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel broadband and scalable RF switch matrix based on microwave photonics is proposed and the proof-of-concept experiments are carried out. The experiment results show that the proposed RF switch matrix is with a good linearity, link gain, port isolation and EVM performance.

articleTitle: The air attenuation of laser transmission in sand-dust weather
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The dust concentration and the complex permittivity of wet sand are utilized to study the laser attenuation in sand-dust weather. The relevance of atmospheric visibility and atmospheric humidity to the air attenuation are analyzed. Afterwards, the influence of height to dust concentration and the lase attenuation under different wavelengths are discussed. The stimulation results show that the laser attenuation will decrease with the increasing of atmospheric visibility. Moreover, the increase of atmospheric humidity will result in the increase of laser attenuation. Additionally, the attenuation follows negative exponential distribution when increasing the transmission height and laser wavelength. Particularly, the attenuation gradually approaches to a wavelength related stable value when the transmission height increases to 2.5km.

articleTitle: Gaussian mixture model based approach to fault detection for satellite communication equipment
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of fault detection for satellite communication system, a prediction method based on Gaussian mixture model is proposed. Firstly, the observation sequence is collected by modem as well as frequency conversion equipment. Then feature parameters are extracted after pre-processing. The expectation maximum algorithm is applied to train the Gaussian mixture model. The posterior probabilities of the feature sequence separately relative to the normal and abnormal models are calculated by the maximum a posteriori probability criterion. In order to determine the right working state, the model corresponding to the larger probability is selected. Since the result of the judgment is presented in the form of probability, it is necessary to choose the threshold value after several times. Finally, the performance and average prediction accuracy of the prediction model are tested by simulation.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of the receiving antenna combined by several simple optical lens in Visible Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We researched the performance of the aspheric lens as the receiving antenna of the indoor Visible Light Communication and got the different results with the lens placed in different situations. We use channel gain curves to describe the relationship between the Field-of-View and the optical gain of the receiving antenna. The experiment shows that the aspheric lens can provide a 15dB optical gain and a 36° FOV cooperated with Thorlabs Photodetector PDA100 by placing the curves-surface outwards and focusing accurately. Also, a 10dB optical gain and a 46° FOV achieved by placing the flat-surface outwards and focusing accurately. Furthermore, we researched the performance of the combination of the aspheric and Bi-Concave Spherical lens, aspheric and negative meniscus lens as the receiving antenna which can effectively enlarge the FOV from 36° to 52° with the cost of 5dB optical gain. At last, we researched the Fisheye Lens's performance as receiving antenna and got its channel gain curves.

articleTitle: Multi-soliton in a fiber laser with a microfiber-based topological insulator saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report on the generation of versatile pulse patterns in an erbium-doped fiber laser incorporating a 2D nano-materials, topological insulator (TI): Bi2Te3. By depositing of the TI on a microfiber, an effective saturable absorber (SA) would be created, which has combined the advantages from the strong nonlinear optical response in TI material together with the sufficiently-long-range interaction length in fiber taper. The microfiber-based TI SA operates as both an excellent saturable absorber for mode-locking and a high-nonlinear medium for promoting the formation of versatile pulse patterns in the fiber laser. By adjustment the pump power and polarization state, we can adjusted the number of pulse in one pulse envelope and obtain various of multi-solitons.

articleTitle: Optical fiber based microfluidic gas flowmeter
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A microfluidic gas flowmeter based on optical fiber Fabry-Perot interferometer(FPI) was proposed and demonstrated. The sensor was formed by two embedded optical fibers with a microfluidic gas channel running across the two end faces. The gas flowrate was first tested by monitoring the shift of the resonance wavelength of the FPI. The intensity demodulation method was then applied to investigate thedynamic response of the sensor, by utilizing a tunable laser and a photodiode. The experimental results show that our proposed microfluidic gas flowmeter has high sensitivity and fast response.

articleTitle: Compact visible Q-switching fiber lasers with transition-metal dichalcogenides
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Compact visible pulsed fiber lasers possess various applications. However, fiber-compatible visible-wavelength saturable absorber (SA) is very scare. Recently, transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have attracted widespread attention due to their visible saturable absorption properties. Here, we report our recent advances in compact visible trivalent praseodymium (Pr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>)-doped ZBLAN fiber lasers and TMDs (WS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and MoSe2)-based red passive Q-switching fiber lasers. Our work suggests that TMDs are promising SAs for Q-switching operation in visible spectral region.

articleTitle: Accurate laser linewidth estimation for coherent optical systems using DA-ML carrier phase estimator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an accurate laser linewidth estimation technique based on the decision-aided maximum likelihood carrier phase estimator (DA-ML). Its performance is verified in M-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (MQAM) within a wide range of the laser linewidths and SNR values.

articleTitle: CVD-grown WSe2 for ultrafast erbium-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrated a passively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser by incorporating a microfiber-based tungsten diselenide (WSe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) saturable absorber (SA). We obtained stable mode-locking with pulse duration of 1.2 ps, repetition rate of 2.6 MHz and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 66 dB at maximum pump power of 400 mW. The experimental results show that CVD-grown WSe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> film can serve as a promising SA for ultrafast laser systems.

articleTitle: Service-aware dynamic bandwidth allocation with CoMP in 5G fronthaul network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A service-aware dynamic bandwidth allocation with CoMP is proposed in the heterogeneous 5G fronthaul network. Simulation results show that the throughput and delay performance of users have been improved, and the QoS for high priority users can be guaranteed preferentially.

articleTitle: Low complexity turbo matching coded optical transmission system based on code weight decision
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Weight distribution of code is very important for error correction in the use of Turbo coding program in optical fiber communication. Input sequence need to pass convolutional encoder, Therefore, it is necessary that the weight of the output should be kept as large as possible. Although the interleaver can help to improve the output code weight, the higher the complexity of interleaving, the iterative decoding will be more complex. In consequence, we can judge the weight of the input data before encoding. Invert all bits when the weight of the code is less than a certain value of its length. It can improve the weight of the code through such a simple way and reduce the complexity of the interleaver at the same time.

articleTitle: Mode characteristics for 1.55 μm square microcavity laser monolithically integrated on GaAs substrates
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a 1.55μm square microcavity laser monolithically integrated on GaAs substrates. The mode characteristics of the microcavity laser are numerically investigated by three-dimensional finite difference time domain method. The dependences of the whispering-gallery modes on the width of the output waveguide and the etching depth are discussed. For the cavity with the side length of 12μm and the output waveguide of 1μm, it is easy to excite whispering-gallery modes around 1.55μm. The mode wavelength is 1542.88nm and the mode Q factor is 2389.23. The Q factor degrades rapidly with the waveguide width increasing and increases with the increasing of the etching depth.

articleTitle: Advances on integrated microwave photonics
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Integrated microwave photonics has attracted a lot of attentions and makes significant improvement in last 10 years. We have proposed and demonstrated several schemes about microwave photonics including waveform generation, signal processing and energy-efficient micro-heaters. Our schemes are all fabricated on silicon-on-insulator chips and have advantages of compactness and capability to integrate with electronics.

articleTitle: Research on ship-shore optical communication mode
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The current ship-shore communication is microwave communication, which is limited by transmission bandwidth and speed. So it is hard to satisfy the requirement of high-speed and stupendous-capacity in future. Within researching the development trend of optical communication, a communication mode based on optical communication is proposed to solve the problem. And considering the specialty of ship-shore communication, the key technologies are analyzed to realize the mode.

articleTitle: High-rate and low-jitter optical pulse generation based on an optoelectronic oscillator using a cascaded polarization modulator and phase modulator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel optical pulse generator with high-rate and low-jitter is proposed based on the optoelectronic oscillator using a cascaded polarization modulator and phase modulator. Optical pulses with 10 GHz repetition rate and 29 ps width are demonstrated. According to the single-sideband phase noise of the generated microwave signal, 169 fs time jitter of the generated pulses in the 100 Hz to 1 MHz frequency range can be calculated.

articleTitle: Research on big datagram outburst transmission in space TT&C network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Due to the unique data structure, the big datagram is prone to packet loss during the network outburst transmission process, especially in the space TT&C (Tracking, Telemetry and Communication) network which is very strict in real time. This paper focuses on the analysis of the transmission mechanism of big datagram, expatiates its fragmentation, reorganization and Re-fragmentation mechanism. The trials of data sending and receiving are conducted to test the transmission performance and the influence of high priority queue on low priority queue by setting up the test environment. Finally, to defeat the packet loss of big datagram, some solutions have been proposed.

articleTitle: Splicing and end facet optimization of large-mode-area photonic crystal fiber for high power application
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In recent years, there is a very fast development in high power fiber laser technology. However, problems like strong nonlinear effect, thermal injury at the fiber end facet and so on arise with increase of the laser power. One of the promising methods is to use rare earth-doped photonic crystal fiber (PCF) with a large mode area as gain medium, but the commonly used free-space coupling method limits efficiency, flexibility and stability of fiber lasers. Here we use a kind of double-clad large-mode-area PCF of 500 μm outer diameter to splice with the traditional solid fiber and achieved a high power coupling ratio up to 72%. We also optimize the end facet quality of the PCF at the output port to obtain a good output.

articleTitle: MoS2 for self-started mode-locked fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we reported a simple and compact all-fiber erbium-doped femtosecond laser mode-locked by fiber-taper molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) saturable absorber (SA). The SA was prepared by magnetron-sputtering deposition (MSD) method, directly growing MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film and then gold film on the microfiber. Based on this SA, the oscillator operated in soliton state, and delivered 478 fs pulses with 6.2 nm bandwidth and 24.7 MHz repetition frequency. Experimental results showed that MSD grown fiber-taper MoS2 can develop into promising photonic devices for ultrafast photonics.

articleTitle: Multiplexed fiber-optic methane sensor system with auxiliary weak fiber Bragg gratings based on OTDR measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a multiplexed fiber-optic methane sensor system to monitor the concentration of methane, which is realized by setting auxiliary weak fiber Bragg gratings (FBGs) around gas cells, and using an optical time domain reflectometry (OTDR) to measure the reflectivity. With the assistance of the weak FBGs, the methane concentration variations were successfully monitored with a detection sensitivity below 0.05 vol. %.

articleTitle: Research on fiber nonlinear coefficient
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We make some measurement research based on CW SPM method, and obtain the non-linear coefficient for the novel ultra low loss& large effective area single mode fiber. And we also discussed the measure uncertainty and non-linear coefficient influence factor.

Author Keywords: ultra low loss& large effective area fiber

articleTitle: Enhanced Stokes Space based mode division de-multiplexing for hybrid modulated MDM-QPSK&16QAM signals
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose an enhanced Stokes Space based mode division de-multiplexing algorithm by using S0 based layered fitting (SLF) method, which can realize QPSK&16QAM hybrid modulation format de-multiplexing in few mode transmissions. The effectiveness of this method is substantiated through numerical simulations under mode division multiplexed transmission, where the modulation format carried by each mode is different.

articleTitle: Virtual network embedding based on restrictive selection and optimization theory
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: One main challenge in network virtualization is virtual network embedding (VNE). VNE is NP-hard. Previous VNE algorithms in the literature are mostly heuristic, while the remaining algorithms are exact. To make a trade-off between the heuristic and the exact, this paper proposes the algorithm VNE-RSOT, based on restrictive selection and optimization theory, to solve the VNE problem. The restrictive selection contributes to largely cutting down on the number of integer variables, adopted in the following optimization theory approach. The VNE-RSOT aims to minimize the substrate resource cost. A simulation against several state-of-art heuristic algorithms is made. Numerical results reveal that virtual network request (VNR) acceptance ratio of VNE-RSOT is, at least, 10% higher than the best-behaved heuristic. The execution time is also plotted to emphasize the efficiency of VNE-RSOT.

articleTitle: A novel switchable microwave photonic filter
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel switchable microwave photonic filter (MPF) based on a second-order Lyot loop and an optical phase modulator (PM) is presented and experimentally demonstrated. A broadband light emitted from a broadband optical source (BOS) is sliced by a second-order Lyot loop which acts as a spectrum slicer, then, is modulated by an optical PM and delayed by a dispersive medium. By doing this, a switchable microwave photonic filter free the baseband resonance is achieved, the radio frequency (RF) responses show three different passband states, which are single passband state, dual-passband state and triple-passband state, respectively. The proposed switchable MPF exhibits a high rejection ratio, which is larger than 30 dB.

articleTitle: Single bandpass microwave photonic filter based on weak optical injection
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Strong optical injection into a distributed feedback (DFB) semiconductor is a method to realize a single bandpass microwave photonic filter (MPF). But the out of band suppression ratio (OSSR) is limited by the four wave mixing (FWM) effect, and the 3 dB bandwidth is too large for microwave signals. To improve the OSSR and narrow the 3 dB bandwidth of the MPF, a novel single bandpss MPF based on weak optical injection is proposed and demonstrated in this paper. Experiment results shown that reduce the optical injection power can eliminate the FWM effect and improve the OSSR and narrow the 3 dB bandwidth of the MPF. In addition, reduce the power of a microwave sinusoidal signal which come from the vector network analyser (VNA) can also narrow the 3 dB bandwidth of the MPF.

articleTitle: Ultrasensitive refractive index sensor based on graphene coated hollow core fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-quality nanolayer graphene (NLG) coated hollow core fiber (HCF) platform has been demonstrated for accurate monitoring of refractive index (RI) changes so far mainly operate in liquids but not in air. The NLG with high index is deposited on the outer surface of the HCF, and an enhanced anti-resonant reflecting guidance is formed, which induces sharp periodic lossy dips in the transmission spectrum. A cute experiment conducted interrogating the transmission intensity of the lossy dip demonstrates a high resolution of 2.73×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> RIU and a sensitivity of -365.9 dB/RIU, which is two or three times higher than that of intensity-modulated RI sensors reported previously. We believe that this configuration opens research directions for highly sensitive sensing in researches of chemistry, medicine, and biology.

articleTitle: High radio-frequency phase-coded waveform generation based on dispersion-compensated optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: High radio-frequency phase-coded waveform generation based on dispersion-compensated optoelectronic oscillator (DCOEO) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The carrier frequency range of the generated phase-coded microwave, which exactly varies from 4 GHz to 45 GHz, can cover Ka band for Radar applications.

articleTitle: Optimized design for beat-length stability of rhomb lattice holey birefringence fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The impact of lateral deformation on dispersion characteristics of birefringence and polarization beat-length in holey fiber with rhomb lattice was simulated by full-vector finite difference beam propagation method. It is found that proper lateral deformation in this fiber can effectively suppress the nonlinear change of birefringence with wavelength. The expanded linear range can make the polarization beat-length stable in wider wavelength band. By optimization, the relative fluctuation of beat-length value is less than 2.67% over wavelength range from 1.1 μm to 1.9μm. This fiber is suitable for making wideband fiber-optic wave-plate covering both 1310nm and 1550nm wavelength windows.

articleTitle: A differential pressure principle based mine wind velocity sensor using fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A design of mine wind velocity sensor is reported, which is based on differential pressure principle and adopts differential sensitive architecture composed of a bellows, an equal-strength beam and two fiber Bragg gratings(FBG). Furthermore, an algorithm is introduced for temperature compensation. Through these methods the cross sensitivity of temperature is effectively eliminated. The relation between the wavelength difference of the two FBGs and the wind velocity is derived, meanwhile the hydraulic simulation test gets the sensitivity of the sensitive structure, 0.703pm/Pa, which is in good agreement with the theoretical value. The result of the wind tunnel tests shows that the measurement error of the sensor is within 0.3m/s in the range of 0.2-20m/s.

articleTitle: X-band optically steered phased array antenna with ultra-fast beam scanning
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A photonic-based phased array antenna (PAA) with ultra-fast beam scan is proposed and experimentally demonstrated using dispersion-based true time delay lines. The ultra-fast angle scan is realized using an ultra-fast wavelength-swept laser source which is constructed by a gated multi-wavelength laser (MWL) and a dispersion compensation fiber (DCF). The wavelength switching time is about several nanoseconds. In the results, we also successfully realized an ultra-fast angle scan from 0 to 43° within 12.48 ns.

articleTitle: Study on transmission performance of optical OOK and PSK modulation formats
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By solving Schrodinger equation in standard Split-Step Fourier Transform (SSFT) method, the NRZ, 33%RZ, 50%RZ, CSRZ, DPSK, 33%RZ-DPSK, 50%RZ-DPSK and CSRZ-DPSK were simulated in 40G bit/s single channel transmission system with the influence of dispersion, nonlinearity and polarization mode dispersion. The simulation results show that CSRZ has better performance than the other modulation formats in the OOK formats, and in PSK formats, the performance of CSRZ-DPSK is the best in these modulation formats concerning in this paper.

articleTitle: Two-dimension encryption OFDM-PON based on dynamic chaos-iteration
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a two-dimension encryption orthogonal frequency division multiplexing passive optical network (OFDM-PON) based on dynamic chaos-iteration. The correlation monitoring method is adopted to achieve dynamic key distribution between OLT and ONUs. It is shown that key space can be larger than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">86</sup>, which would be against exhaustive attack effectively. We experimentally demonstrate a 13.3Gb/s encrypted 64 QAM-mapping OFDM signal transmission over 25km standard single-mode fibre in an OFDM-PON and successfully decrypt it at the receiver.

articleTitle: Performance improvement of Brillouin based distributed fiber sensors employing wavelength diversity techniques (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The sensing performance in Brillouin-based distributed fiber sensors is ultimately depends on the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the received signal. In order to enhance the SNR, thus improve the sensing performance, several wavelength diversity techniques have been proposed. This paper presents the current wavelength diversity techniques employed in both Brillouin optical time-domain reflectometry (BOTDR) and Brillouin optical time-domain analysis (BOTDA) systems. So far, the best SNR improvement in BOTDR system is 4.85 dB with a 25 km sensing fiber, whereas, 4.8 dB in BOTDA system with a 50 km sensing fiber.

articleTitle: Coexistence of polarization domains and polarization vector solitons in fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally observed the coexistence of polarization domains and polarization locked vector solitons in an Er-doped fiber laser with microfiber-based graphene as a saturable absorber. Taking advantage of the highly nonlinear effect and saturable absorption effect of the microfiber-based graphene saturable absorber, we have obtained polarization domains and their splitting into regularly or irregularly distributed multiple domains under relatively high pump power; at lower pump power and by carefully adjusting the orientation of the intra-cavity polarization controllers, we have also observed polarization locked vector pulses and their disordered soliton bunch or harmonic mode locking.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of GaAsP/Si dual-junction solar cells
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The GaAsP/Si dual-junction solar cells have been systematically investigated in our paper by using AMPS (Analysis of Microelectronic and Photonic Structures). Based on the optimized results of single-junction solar cells, we propose a promising method to improve the properties of the dual-junction solar cell. And the monolithic GaAs<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>/Si dual-junction solar cells with various As compositions (x=0.65, 0.75, 0.85) and base thicknesses (t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>=0.05~2.5um) were analyzed. The remarkable conversion efficiency of 35.8% has been obtained for the GaAs<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.75</sub>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.25</sub>/Si dual-junction solar cells, which is higher than previously reported results. Our method and results will provide a significant guidance for the design and manufacture of Si-based dual-junction solar cells.

articleTitle: A precision edge filter interrogation system for mine Fiber Bragg Grating micro-seismic sensors
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The edge filter approach using a distributed feedback laser diode is well suited for interrogating Fiber Bragg Grating micro-seismic sensors. This paper presents the design and implementation of a novel precision edge filter interrogation system based on digital signal processing technology. The experimental study of the temperature tuning characteristics, system composition, and operating principle are introduced in detail. The results show that the system achieves a bandwidth range from 0.5 Hz to 450 Hz. The working-point control accuracy reaches up to 0.1 %, while the time synchronization precision is about 0.6 us. It is expected to be applied in distributed fiber optic micro-seismic system for underground coal mines.

articleTitle: Open-cavity Fabry-Perot interferometer pressure and temperature fiber sensor based on photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a cascaded-cavities Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI) for simultaneous measurement of pressure and temperature based on photonic crystal fiber. The sensor is composed of cascaded air-cavity and silica-cavity. The air-cavity and silica-cavity are both sensitive to temperature and pressure because of the thermo-optic coefficient and Young's modulus. We can obtain the pressure sensitivity and the temperature sensitivity of each cavity by band-pass filtering of the sensor spectrum in the frequency domain. Therefore the proposed sensor can simultaneously measure the pressure and temperature without pressure-temperature cross-talk. The proposed sensor has a compact and all-fiber structure, while the fabrication process of the cascaded FPI sensor is easy with just a few steps of splicing and cleaving.

articleTitle: Refractive index sensor based on liquid-filled defect hollow core Bragg fiber for high index sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a refractive index (RI) sensor based on a liquid-filled defect hollow core Bragg fiber (DHCBF) for high index sensing, in which a resonant wavelength resulted from the transverse resonant coupling effect between core modes and defect modes is utilized as the characteristic wavelength. The linearity and sensitivity strongly depend on structural parameters of defect layer. Accordingly, we numerically demonstrate a high linearity RI sensor with a high sensitivity of 753nm/RIU in the large range of 1.477 to 1.645, by optimally designing the defect layer in a liquid-filled DHCBF. The sensitivity of 532nm/RIU with slightly higher linearity is still can be achieved even when the cladding material dispersion is included.

articleTitle: A simple all-optical wavelength converter based on cascaded highly nonlinear fibers with high conversion-efficiency
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In all-optical wavelength converters based on highly nonlinear fiber (HNLF), the longer fibers always have lower Stimulated Brillouin Scattering (SBS) threshold power. In the paper, we proposed an all-optical wavelength converter with increasing SBS threshold by cascading two different HNLFs. We experimentally achieved -8-dB conversion efficiency and good converted signals with negligible power penalties.

articleTitle: Luminescence properties of novel single-phase (Sr1−xMnx)3(PO4)2: Eu2+ phosphor for white light emitting diodes
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A series of phosphors (Sr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>Mn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>(PO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>:Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> (x=0−0.1) were synthesized via a high-temperature solid-state reaction. The photoluminescence properties were systematically analyzed. articleTitle: Soliton explosions in a fiber laser mode-locked by nonlinear polarization evolution
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report on the first observation, to the best of our knowledge, of soliton explosion in an ultrafast fiber laser mode-locked by nonlinear polarization evolution. Different from previous experimental observations in passively mode-locked lasers, the soliton explosions continue thousands roundtrips.

articleTitle: Sensitivity-enhanced Sagnac interferometer temperature sensor based on Vernier effect with the help of Fabry-Perot interferometer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A sensitivity-enhanced temperature sensor based on Vernier-effect was demonstrated. Vernier-effect is achieved by a cascaded configuration with a fiber Sagnac interferometer (FSI) and a Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI). FSI, which consists of a certain length of polarization maintaining fiber, is for temperature sensing, while. FPI acts as a filter due the temperature insensitivity. Experimental results show that the temperature sens or has a high sensitivity of -29 nm/°C and the enhancement factor is about 10.3.

articleTitle: All-fiber polarization maintaining erbium-doped fiber laser based on nonlinear amplifying loop mirror
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, all-fiber based all polarization maintaining erbium-doped fiber lasers based on nonlinear amplifying loop mirror (NALM), including both figure-of-8 and figure-of-9 configurations are demonstrated. The figure-of-8 oscillator generates 1.6 ps chirped pulses at 1550 nm with a pulse energy of 0.8 nJ and a repetition rate of 12 MHz. The figure-of-9 oscillator generates 420 fs pulses at 1550 nm with a pulse energy of 0.2nJ and a repetition rate of 52.5 MHz. Both configurations have the advantages of self-starting and long term operation.

articleTitle: Partitioned frequency domain equalization for 6-LP mode multiplexed systems with few mode fibers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Mode division multiplexed(MDM) in few mode fibers has got attraction due to its potential to achieve ultra-high capacity beyond the nonlinear Shannon limit of the single mode fiber. However, the effect of dispersion, mode coupling and differential group delay on optical signals cannot be ignored, thus equalizing these impairments are required in MDM system. In this paper, a partitioned modified frequency domain least mean square(PFDLMS) algorithm is proposed for the digital dispersion equalizer of polarization division multiplexing(PDM)-MDM coherent system. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can improve the convergence speed and get a great equalization performance.

articleTitle: Investigation of amplification characteristic for DPSK signal in SOA
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The amplification characteristics of DPSK signal in semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) is numerically simulated and experimentally demonstrated for the first time. The results show that the bit pattern effect (BPE) of the DPSK signal is induced by SOA. According to the results, when pulsewidth of the signal is comparable to the gain recovery time of SOA, the BPE is severe. And when the pulsewidth of the signal becomes much larger or shorter than the gain recovery time of SOA, the BPE is alleviated. In addition, the experiment results show that by adjusting the injection current of SOA, the BPE can be alleviated effectively.

articleTitle: A fast offset phase calibration method
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The phase correction algorithm of dual channel mono-pulse radar is studied in this paper. The angle error voltage of the tracking receiver is represented by a complex number. The expression of the relation between the corrected phase and the corrected slope and the error voltage is derived, and a fast phase detection method is proposed. phase detection rate of this method is significantly faster than the automatic phase calibration of the equipment itself for the case of without the boresight tower. Moreover, the method presented here has higher accuracy.

articleTitle: The study of cross interference experiments of laser methane sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on Tunable Diode Laser Absorption Spectroscopy (TDLAS) and the feature of Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Laser (VCSEL) which wavelength scanning range up to several nanometers, the methane sensor system was designed. To verify the characteristic of anti-cross interference, we made some spectroscopy stimulation and experiments to analyze the affects to the methane measurement results of the gas of H2O, CO and CO2. The results prove that the laser methane sensor has the characteristics such as high stability, resistance to gas cross interference etc.

articleTitle: Magnetic field sensor based on phase-shifted fiber Bragg grating with magnetic fluid
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A magnetic field sensor based on a novel phase-shifted fiber Bragg grating with magnetic fluid is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. It is fabricated by cleaving a uniform fiber Bragg grating at the center point, introducing a micrometre gap as a phase-shift and then filling the gap with magnetic fluid. External applied magnetic field changes refractive index of the magnetic fluid, leading to a wavelength shift of the phase-shifted induced transmission peak. By detecting transmission peak wavelength shift with magnetic field intensity, optical measurement of magnetic field is realized. Experimental results show a linear response of wavelength shift to magnetic field intensity with a high sensitivity of 2.4 pm/Oe in the testing magnetic field intensity range from 0 to 120 Oe.

articleTitle: Optical fiber sensor based on concave cone and long period fiber grating cascaded
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical fiber sensor based on concave cone and long period fiber grating (LPG) is proposed, and the experimental curve and temperature are experimentally demonstrated. The sensor head consists of a combination of concave cone and long-period fiber grating. The experimental results show that the interference peaks of the resonant wavelengths of the concave cone and the long-period fiber grating have different responses to the curvature and the temperature. Therefore, the measurement of the curvature and temperature can be obtained by using the concave cone and the long-period fiber grating cascade.

articleTitle: Reduction of high-frequency laser noise in resonant fiber optic gyroscope with a phase-modulated feedback loop
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The resonant fiber-optic gyroscope (RFOG) based on the Sagnac effect is a high-accuracy rotation sensor. The intermodulation error due to the laser noise at even harmonics of the modulation frequency deteriorates the performance of the RFOG. Aiming at the suppression of high-frequency laser noise, a phase-modulated feedback loop is developed and analyzed. The parameters of the servo loop is optimized to enhance the performance of the gyroscope.

articleTitle: Miniature optical fiber sensor based on polypyrrole for detection of VOCs
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
