abstract: A volatile organic compounds (VOCs) sensor based on intrinsic Fabry-Perot interferometer (IFPI) coated with polypyrrole thin film was proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The IFPI consists a section of hollow-core fiber (HCF) sandwiched between two single mode fiber. The polypyrrole is formed chemically via interfacial polymerization technique and coated directly onto the fiber. As the isopropanol vapor got absorbed by the film, the reflection spectrum of IFPI changes due to the refractive index (RI) variation of the film. The proposed sensor achieves a sensitivity of 0.0423 dB/ppm with a wide concentration range of isopropanol vapor from 65 to 455 ppm.

articleTitle: 1-to-49 Optical multicasting of PDM OFDM signal based on dual-stage multi-pump FWM scheme
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a dual-stage multi-pump FWM scheme for all-optical signal multicasting in HNLF. Based on the scheme, we experimentally demonstrate 25GHz-spaced l-to-49 multicasting of PDM OFDM signal using 6 pumps. All replicas exhibit performance above 7% FEC threshold with Q-factor margin of no less than 1dB. To the best our knowledge, this is the largest reported replica count in the context of all-optical multicasting of PDM OFDM signals.

articleTitle: A TE/TM independent polarizer based on graphene interferometer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We proposed a versatile polarizer independent with the polarization of the incident light by coating the graphene on the silicon waveguide. The proposed polarizer works at two operation states: TE-pass state and TM-pass state, where the variation of mode effective index is different for the two states. Therefore it is able to combine TE-pass and TM-pass polarizer into one single component. The proposed device owns a compact size of 69.65μm*2μm, high extinction ratio 19.15dB for TE-pass polarizer and 20.68dB for TM-pass polarizer, respectively. Furthermore, this device exhibits a wide working bandwidth from 1500nm to 1800nm.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of photodiode array electrodes
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We designed and optimized a high-speed, low-loss electrodes applied to photodiode array (PDA) using simulating software HFSS. Optimized and un-optimized electrodes were fabricated and tested. A 1.1dB reduce of the insertion loss at 40GHz was achieved by the optimization. Meanwhile, photodiode array implementing the optimized electrodes has a 6.6GHz higher 3dB-bandwidth comparing to the photodiode with un-optimized electrodes.

articleTitle: Self-started stable pulsing operation of random fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Unlike traditional fiber laser with defined resonant cavity, random fiber laser (RFL), whose operation is based on distributed gain and feedback via Rayleigh scattering and stimulated Raman scattering in long passive fiber, has fundamental scientific challenges in pulsing operation for its remarkable cavity-free feature. Here, we propose and experimentally realize the passively spatiotemporal gain modulation induced self-started stable pulsing operation of counter-pumped RFL. Thanks to the good temporal stability of employed pumping amplified spontaneous emission source and the superiority of this pulse generation scheme, stable and regular pulse train can be obtained. Furthermore, the pump hysteresis and bistability phenomena with the generation of high order Stokes light is presented and the dynamics of pulsing operation is discussed. This work extends our comprehension of temporal property of RFL and provides an effective novel avenue for the exploration of pulsed RFL with structural simplicity, low cost and stable output.

articleTitle: Design of super sensitive CMOS image sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Aiming at the shortcomings of low pixel filling rate of CMOS sensor, a gold film optoelectronic device suitable for a given wavelength is designed by using the optical signal of the pixel ineffective region and the super - transmissive effect based on the metal surface plasma. A series of regular periodic centers through holes can be used to direct the surface plasmonic surface excited by the surface of the gold film through the central pores of the structure by etching a 100 nm thick gold film surface. The gold film structure is close to the surface of the CMOS sensor, in which the structure of the hole corresponds to the effective area of the pixel, the external structure corresponds to the invalid area of the pixel. With this method, the absorption efficiency of the CMOS sensor can be increased to 1.70 times. The device can effectively improve the CMOS sensor light absorption efficiency, can compensate for the low CMOS sensor filling rate shortcomings.

articleTitle: Miniature pH sensor based on thin-core fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A miniature pH sensor by using a tapered thin-core optical fiber based Mach-Zehnder interferometer coated with a pH sensitive film is demonstrated. Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and polyacrylic acid (PAA) were used to form a membrane structure on the taper by laminating self-assembly technique. By measuring wavelength change of the interference pattern or optical intensity, we achieved high sensitivity pH value measurement up to 2.06 nm/pH unit. The proposed sensor has small size, simple structure, good stability and a relatively short response time less than 52 s.

articleTitle: Equalization algorithm based on CMA and SVM for carrierless amplitude phase modulation in optical access networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An equalization algorithm is proposed for carrier-less amplitude and phase (CAP) modulation system, which is regarded as a good candidate for short range optical communications, like electrical power optical fiber communication, optical access network. The constant module algorithm (CMA) combined with support vector machine (SVM) performs the equalization function. The simulation system was setup for both single-band 16-CAP signal at 10Gbps and multi-band M-CAP (4-CAP, 16-CAP, 64-CAP) signal at 100Gbps. After the CMA-SVM equalization, the impaired CAP signals are compensated effectively. The phase rotation is recovered and the centralization of each constellation points is improved obviously, which demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed equalization algorithm.

articleTitle: Magnetic field sensor based on twisted fiber and magnetic fluid
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A magnetic field sensor based on twisted single mode fiber and magnetic fluid (MF) is proposed and demonstrated. The sensor consists of two twisted points on a single mode fiber introduced by flame-heated and rotation treatment. Cladding modes are excited at the first twisted point and part of them are coupled back to the fiber core at the second twisted point, forming an inline Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Then the structure was inserted into a MF-filled capillary for magnetic field sensing. Owing to the refractive index tunable characteristic of the MF, the destructive interference wavelength will shift as the magnetic field intensity varies. Experimental result shows that a sensitivity of 55.5pm/Oe is achieved for static magnetic field measurement ranging from 20-120 Oe.

articleTitle: High-order few-mode-fiber Raman amplifier for low noise mode-division-multiplexed optical communication
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate, for the first time, a second-order few-mode distributed Raman amplifier with 4 dB mode-equalized gain. The noise figure improvement of the LPoi andLPn modes are respectively 1.2 dB and 1.1 dB compared with first-order Raman amplification scheme. We also use optical time-domain reflectometer (OTDR) to measure the signal evolutions, and the results confirm the low noise amplification for the second-order pumping configuration.

articleTitle: Vortex-mode optofluidic manipulation based on hybrid photothermal waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Photothermal manipulation has been proven as an effective strategy to trap and rotate mesoscopic particles, whose features are scales ranging from tens of nanometers to hundreds of micrometers. In particular, the extraordinary ability of highly-efficient non-contact photothermal manipulation based on fiber waveguide has stimulated a number of breakthroughs in lab-on-a-chip techniques and research endeavours. In this report, we have developed a new vortex-mode optofluidic technique for achieving controllable convection and multi-particle manipulation by photothermal waveguide. The optofludic vortex can trap and rotate mesoscopic particles in the vortex center due to strong confinement and torque. In addition, based on the convenience and the flexibility of fiber waveguide, multiple vortexes can be integrated on an vortex array in a small scale chip, which will enable simultaneously multiple experimental operations in an elaborate lab-on-a-chip system. As an optofluidic “workshop” with above advantages, the vortex-mode optofluidic system is expected to have good prospects in several frontier field of nanoscience.

articleTitle: A high SMSR dual-wavelength linear-cavity Er-doped laser based on AWG as a comber filter and demultiplexer
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel high SMSR dual-wavelength erbium-doped fiber laser operating in C-band is proposed and successfully demonstrated. Based on Arrayed-Waveguide Gratings (A WGs) as a comber filter and demultiplexer, the fiber laser retrieve the optical side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of 53dB and the output powers of-10.45dBm and-10.20dBm at the wavelengths 1554.87nm and 1555.65nm, respectively. The mode spacing of the dual-wavelength fiber laser is nearly 0.8 nm. The laser can operate in stable narrow-line-width with single- and dual-wavelength output at room temperature.

articleTitle: A sensing system for simultaneous measurement of temperature and transversal loading based on a fiber-ring microwave photonic filter
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a fiber-optic sensing system for simultaneous measurement of temperature and transversal loading based on a fiber-ring microwave photonic filter (MPF) has been proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The temperature variation will induce the central frequency shift of the MPF's passband, while the micro-bend loss induced by transversal loading will cause the change of extinction ratio of the MPF. Hence, by tracking the central frequency and extinction ratio of the passbands, temperature and transversal loading can be monitored respectively. The proposed sensing system enjoys high sensitivity, remoting sensing, good multiplexing capacity, thus shows a good prospect in practical applications.

articleTitle: Research on the power combining efficiency of a shipborne X-band transmitter
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A power combining solution using magic-T is presented to apply in a shipborne X-band transmitter. According to scatter parameter theory, the factors that have influence on combining efficiency are analyzed; the combining efficiency and max output power are calculated. The results show that: (1) the magic-T has the advantage of small size, simple structure, good heat dissipation performance, so that it suits the shipborne situation well. (2) The combining efficiency of magic-T depends mostly on the insertion loss, and the amplitude and phase of input signal. (3) The 1kW output can be satisfied using the power combining solution presented.

articleTitle: Polarization-fluctuation induced drift in resonant fiber optic gyro using an air-core photonic-bandgap fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We present an analytical model of the drift in the air-core photonic-bandgap fiber (PBF) resonator optic gyroscope caused by temperature-driven polarization instability. Air-core PBF resonator based on micro-optical structure has been demonstrated and the finesse of the resonator is 7.5. Experimental results show that the gyro bias stability still seriously affected by the thermally induced polarization instability. By carefully controlling the temperature, a bias stability of 0.0034°/s has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Effects of a minute femtosecond pulse seed on continuous wave pumped supercontinuum generation
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We numerically investigate the effects of a minute femtosecond pulse seed on continuous wave pumped supercontinuum generation when the frequency shift of the seed varies.

articleTitle: Characteristics of high-order linearly chirped waveguide Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, characteristics of high-order linearly chirped waveguide Bragg gratings (LCWBGs) are studied. The influence of saturation coefficient and grating order on the reflection spectrum (central wavelength, chirp coefficient, maximum reflectivity and total reflection bandwidth) of high-order LCWBGs is analyzed. LCWBGs with different grating orders have different optimal saturation coefficients. With the increase of saturation coefficient, chirp coefficient and total reflection bandwidth are almost unchanged, central wavelength moves to longer wavelength. Under optimal saturation coefficient, chirp coefficient, total reflection bandwidth and maximum reflectivity are smaller with the increase of grating order.

Author Keywords: high-order linearly chirped waveguide Bragg gratings

articleTitle: Technique to eliminate birefringence in PLC-based direct D(Q)PSK receiver and array waveguide grating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We review our contribution in the half-wave plate based technique to eliminate birefringence in PLC-based direct D(Q)PSK receiver and arrayed waveguide grating (AWG). In a direct DPSK receiver, a half-wave plate and heating electrodes are added on the arm waveguides of the DLI, to eliminate the PDFS of the delay-line interferometer (DLI). By applying a proper heating current, a residual PDFS of practically zero at 1550 nm and within ±125 MHz was achieved over the full C-band. In the AWG embedded with a half-wave plate, a strategy using optically asymmetrical slab waveguides is proposed. For the exemplary case that the half-wave plate is not embedded in the middle of AWG, the thermo-optic effect is utilized to adjust the birefringence of the slab waveguides and realize optical asymmetry of them; thereby the residual polarization sensitivity is eliminated.

articleTitle: Modulation and performance tradeoffs for short-range non-line-of-sight ultraviolet communication
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The non-line-of-sight ultraviolet single-scatter approximate model is usually used to study the channel characteristics and system performance due to its simplification. In this paper, a performance evaluation system based on the approximate model is established, which includes four aspects, namely, packet error rate, average transmitting power, bandwidth utilizing efficiency and data transmission rate. Under the condition that Gaussian noise distribution is considered in channel model, the performance of different modulation schemes is evaluated. Finally, give the performance metrics that the system can achieve within 100 meters.

articleTitle: High capacity optical transmission technologies in multi-core fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose high capacity transmission technologies based on multi-core fiber (MCF) with both coherent and direct detections. In the coherent detection system, we experimentally demonstrate 560 Tb/s coherent optical dual-polarization DFT-S OFDM 32QAM signal transmission over 10-km single-mode 7-core fiber.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of efficient topology reconstruction in optical switching based data center network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We review our previously proposed topology reconstruction mechanism in the small world topology based optical data center network (DCN). We also present some recent experimental demonstration results, which verified that the topology reconstruction can reduce the number of hotspots and thus further accelerate data analysis jobs in DCN.

articleTitle: A single-longitudinal-mode, narrow bandwidth fiber laser based on an ultra-high roundness microsphere cavity
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes a single-longitudinal-mode, narrow bandwidth fiber laser with double-ring cavity, using an ultra-high roundness microsphere cavity as the single-longitudinal-mode selector. By improving the heating technology and surface cleaning process, microsphere cavities with high Q factor are obtained. Through optimizing the polarization of incident light and the diameter of tapered fiber, Whispering Gallery Mode (WGM) resonance spectrum with a high coupling efficiency of 99.5%, a 3 dB bandwidth of 1 pm and a side mode-suppression-ratio of 14.5 dB is obtained. The proposed fiber laser produces narrow bandwidth laser spectrum with a 3 dB bandwidth of 0.01nm and a high stability without mode-hopping. The proposed fiber laser is of great significance in optical communication and sensing systems.

articleTitle: Pulse width compression of supercontinuum based on free space OTDM system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a pulse width compression scheme for optical time division multiplexing (OTDM) system based on supercontinuum (SC) is proposed. After injecting a high power narrow line-width pulse width laser into high nonlinear fiber (HNLF), the pulse width has been obviously narrowed. This demonstration suggests that the pulse width compression effect of SC could be used in free-space OTDM system.

articleTitle: An integrated triple-wavelength tunable filter based on Lithium Niobate
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The performance of an integrated triple wavelength tunable filter based on the electro-optic effect in Lithium Niobate is proposed and analyzed. The filter contains four Bragg waveguide gratings, which separated by three waveguides and three pairs of electrodes. Three pairs of electrodes on both side of three waveguides is used to tune the phase shift caused by the waveguides. As a result, the wavelength and wavelength spacing of the filter is tunable.

articleTitle: Study on the rate equation of semiconductor laser in LiDAR detection system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: LiDAR(Light Detection And Ranging) is an important sensor in the environmental perception of self-driving cars. This article mainly aims at the existing unmanned application environment, design a feasible LiDAR(Light Detection And Ranging) for low-speed short-range barge truck, and definition of parameters on laser radar on the whole measurement range: 100m, accuracy: 3cm, data acquisition frequency is 2kHz and operating wavelength: 1053nm operating temperature: 10° to 50 °C. Try to improve the performance of the semiconductor laser response characteristics of the laser, the analysis on the factors influencing the dynamic response, to give full play to its advantages in performance and minimize the impact of unfavorable factors, make semiconductor lasers work best.

articleTitle: The Mach-Zehnder modulator based on bi-layer graphene-silicon-waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate that by inserting bi-layer graphene inside silicon waveguide, the modulation ability of the overall waveguide can be greatly enhanced. A Mach-Zehnder modulator based on this structure is proposed and the calculated results show the modulator exhibits an excellent performance in terms of small footprint (35 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and high extinction ration (31 dB). Besides, it requires low applied voltage and can be compatible with CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Thulium-doped mode-locked fiber laser incorporating carbon-nanotube-based saturable absorber with ring pattern
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have demonstrated a thulium-doped mode-locked fiber laser incorporating carbon-nanotube-based saturable absorber (CNT-SA) with ring pattern for the first time. The mode-locking operation can be maintained an intracavity average power of 37.8 mW, indicating that CNT with ring pattern can enhance the thermal damage threshold of SAs near 2 μm.

articleTitle: Enhanced ultraviolet photoluminescence in Gd3+-doped Silica glass
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Photoluminescence (PL) of Gd-doped silica in the ultraviolet (UV) is investigated. The strong emission detected at 314 nm is assigned to the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7/2</sub> to <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7/2</sub> transition under excitation of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>D<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">J</sub>, <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">J</sub>, and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">J</sub> energy levels of the Gd<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>. After glass densified by rapid thermal treatment (RTT), significant enhanced luminescence and decreased loss covering the UV band are observed.

articleTitle: Slot-waveguide fibers for ultra-low volume optofluidic sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A brand new design of slot waveguide is proposed using a subwavelength hollow-core fiber, which enables light to be confined in an extremely small hollow-core with long interaction length. The slot-waveguide fibers (SWFs) have specific advantages in ultra-low volume optofluidic sensing compared with other waveguide structures. The guiding properties and optimization of the design to maximize its sensitive have also been investigated.

articleTitle: A method for ship-borne mono-pulse radar amplitude-phase fast-calibration
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the theory and design of mono-pulse radar amplitude-phase calibration based on AD sampling are introduced. The methods of mono-pulse radar amplitude-phase calibration are analyzed. According to the theory, a fast-calibrating method that is based on simulator calibration is designed. By testing this fast-calibrating method, the experiment results show that the method is effective and convenient.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and wavelength tunable optical passband filter with tunable attenuation based on transmission liquid crystal technology
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An optical passband filter based on transmission liquid crystal technology is proposed and demonstrated. The bandwidth, wavelength and attenuation can be tuned by controlling the voltage applied on the liquid crystal chips. The insertion loss is <3dB, bandwidth tunable range is from 50GHz to 5000GHz, attenuation range is from 0 to 15dB. The filter can meet the technical requirements of CDCF ROADM.

articleTitle: Demonstration of stimulated emission in CsPbBrs nanocrystals integrating silica microsphere structure
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Here we report an active microresonator by integrating a thin layer of all-inorganic CsPbBr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> nanocrystals (NCs) to a silica microsphere. We also demonstrate the transition from spontaneous emission to stimulated emission (SE) of CsPbBr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> with varying pump power. Further lasing is expected by improving the fabrication technology. Our configuration may provide a route to low threshold and compact lasers, and find applications in sensing.

articleTitle: 2×2 multimode optical switch for large-capacity on-chip optical interconnect
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a silicon 2×2 optical switch which can simultaneous manipulate wavelength division multiplexing and mode division multiplexing signals. It is composed of broadband mode multiplexers, demultiplexers and single mode optical switch elements. For demonstration, we design and fabricate a prototype device using asymmetric directional coupler and Mach-Zehnder optical switch elements which can manipulate four modes and multi-wavelengths from 1525 nm to 1565 nm. The optical crosstalk is less than 18.9 dB and the 10%-90% switching time is ~19 μs. This device can be a key component for constructing simultaneous WDM and MDM optical networks to further increase the communication capacity.

articleTitle: Tunable narrow linewidth 1.5 μm fiber laser using a π phase-shifted FBG
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Here we demonstrate, to the best of our knowledge, a tunable 1.5 μm narrow linewidth fiber ring laser using a temperature tuning π-phase shifted fiber Bragg grating (π-PSFBG) for the first time. The π-PSFBG is employed as both a narrow band filter and a wavelength tuning component by a thermo electric cooler (TEC). The tuning range of the laser is 1.29 nm with the precision of 14 pm/°C, and the maximum output power is 1.1 W with a linewidth of 2.57pm, and the slope efficiency is about 12.2%.

articleTitle: Design of 2×2 silicon TE-polarization Digital Optical Switch (DOS) based on adiabatic coupler
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and numerically simulate a 2×2 Digital Optical Switch (DOS) based on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) adiabatic coupler for TE polarizations at 1550nm. The simulation results acquired by Beam-Propagation-Method (BPM) reveal that the cross-talk (CT) levels are below -27dB over a broadband of 60nm. Small simulated insertion-losses (ILs) below 0.1dB are obtained between the wavelengths 1520nm to 1580nm for both two switching states.

articleTitle: Linearly-polarized narrow-linewidth random fiber laser seeded fiber MOPA
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose and experimentally investigate a linearly-polarized narrow linewidth random fiber laser (RFL) operating at 1080 nm and boost the output power to kilowatt-level with near-diffraction-limited beam quality by a master-oscillation-power-amplifier (MOPA) configuration. The RFL based on half-opened cavity generates 0.71 W seed laser with 88 pm full width at half-maximum (FWHM) linewidth and 22.5 dB polarization extinction ratio (PER) for power scaling. Two stage fiber amplifier enhances the seed laser to maximal 1.01 kW with a PER value of 17 dB and a beam quality of Mx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=1.15 and My<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=1.13. The FWHM linewidth of amplified random laser broadens linearly as a function of output power with a coefficient of about 0.1237 pm/ W. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of linearly-polarized narrow linewidth RFL with even kilowatt-level near-diffraction-limited output.

articleTitle: Study on absolute distance measurement based on a mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The absolute distance measurement system based on phase shift and synthetic wavelength is developed. The repetition frequency of 250 MHz and corresponding forth harmonic frequency of a mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser are used in measurement. The synthetic wavelength in introduced to enlarge the measuring ambiguity range of the system. Moreover, the repetition frequency is modulated by an acoustic optical modulator so that the large-scale and high-precision measurement is realized. The experimental results show the proposed system owns a micro-grade measurement uncertainty in a range up to 100 m. The difference between the measurement and actual distance agrees well.

articleTitle: Research on the phase shift characteristic of angle tuning F-P etalon
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Based on the optical characteristics of the solid F-P etalon, the sensitivity to the angle and transmission is discussed. By slightly changing the angle of the incident light, the transmittance waveform of the etalon has a significant phase shift, and which become more and more rapidly with the increase of the angle. Through the stability analysis of transmission waveform in different regions, it can be seen that the solid F-P etalon exhibits higher sensitivity in the peak-valley region.

articleTitle: MDNS based automatic discovery method in optical NMS
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The optical network management system is very important for optical equipment monitoring and managing, the timeliness and accuracy are very critical parameters. Automatic discovery of network nodes is the embodiment of automation of network management system. However, most of the traditional automatic discovery method is based on the ICMP protocol, which is to ping all the IP addresses in local area network one by one, but it effects efficiency greatly consuming costing too much time. This paper proposes an automatic discovery method based on MDNS protocol in designed optical NMS, sending multicast message to all IP addresses in LAN, then the IP addresses with response are valid address. So in this way we can detect IP node and supported services more rapidly, brings about a vast improvement in the efficiency of optical network management system.

articleTitle: Burst-mode supercontinuum generation with versatile shapes
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: fibre optic sensors; optical modulation; fibre lasers; optical fibre networks; optical fibre polarisation; laser cavity resonators; Bragg gratings; optical fibre fabrication; laser beams; optical pumping.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of adaptive digital pre-distortion with partial transmit sequence algorithm for DMT modulation in high speed optical interconnection
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An 117 Gbit/s short range high speed optical interconnection using DMT modulation and adaptive DPD-PTS algorithm is proposed. By comparison with the traditional DPD algorithm, the simulation results show that the DPD-PTS used in the proposed scheme may achieve higher performance without complex equalization algorithm and dispersion compensation, and thus 117 Gbit/s DMT signal can be transmitted over 20-km SSMF.

articleTitle: Ultraviolet-extended flat SC generation in seven-core photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An ultraviolet-extended broadband supercontinuum (SC) generation down to 350 nm wavelength is obtained by pumping a piece of uniform seven-core photonic crystal fiber with a tunable femtosecond laser at 800 nm, which extends the shortest wavelength in SC generation in seven-core PCF to date. High spectral flatness (10 dB) has been achieved in the entire visible window.

articleTitle: A broadband and tunable absorber with non-volatile floating-gate graphene structure
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A broadband and tunable absorber with nearly zero static power consumption is proposed based on non-volatile floating-gate graphene structure. Such absorber has almost no static power consumption benefited from the non-volatile design. In such design, the central graphene can capture the tunneled electrons under the positive applied voltage, but cannot release these electrons after removing the voltage since it is electrically isolated from the external electrodes. Therefore, no extra power is needed to sustain the conductivity of graphene. Moreover, our proposed absorber exhibits an extremely strong absorption capacity. Even taking the strict condition for the bandwidth where all the absorptivity inside the bandwidth are larger than 90% as criterion, the proposed absorber provides more than 60 GHz absorption bandwidth which is twice larger than previous results. Furthermore, the proposed absorber shows high tolerance against large incidence angle (60°), different polarizations. The results may promote various future non-volatile absorber designs.

articleTitle: Block interleaved frequency division multiple access for visible light communications
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a power efficient multiple access scheme for visible light communications (VLC) based on the block interleaved frequency division multiple access (B-IFDMA), which provides large frequency-diversity, flexible bandwidth allocation, low complexity of channel equalization and user separation. The impact of the number of subcarrier per block on the transmission performance under wireless optical channel is investigated.

articleTitle: Fast detection for newcastle disease virus by using 81° tilted fiber grating immunosensor
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A type of newcastle disease virus (NDV) immunosensor based on 81° tiled fiber grating (81° TFG) was proposed. Staphylococcus aureus Protein A (SPA) was used to modify the surface of 81° TFG, then highly purified NDV monoclonal antibodies (MAbs) were immobilized on 81° TFG surface through SPA molecules. The experimental results show that, the immunosensor has a lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.1~0.2ng/mL to NDV and become saturated at ~1.0ng/mL, and has good linearity with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of ~0.982 and sensitivity of ~342pm/(ng/mL) in the concentration range of 0~1.0ng/mL.

articleTitle: Error analysis for the moon's gravity field inversion based on satellite gradiometr
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The traditional method uses the least squares method to evaluate the effect of satellite load noise on the recovery accuracy of the lunar gravity field, which means large number of complex calculations are needed. In order to recover the lunar gravity field more accurately and simply, the article establishes an expression of the noise power spectrum and analysis the errors from the accuracy of the satellite gravity gradient measurement, the orbital height and the period of running time on the recovery of the moon gravity field, And finally gives a reasonable indexes design of the lunar gravity gradiometry. The results show that the accuracy of the recovery of the lunar gravity field increases with the increase of the gradient measurement accuracy (10,5,1 and 0.1mE / Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>), the decrease of the satellite orbit height (250, 200, 150 and 100km) and the running period (1month, 3months and 6months).

articleTitle: Ultrahigh-resolution wavelength scanning system with FBG Fabry-Perot interferometer for displacement sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A wavelength scanning system with ultrahigh-resolution is proposed and demonstrated for displacement sensing. Light from a linewidth-narrowed and frequency-stabilized laser is put into an electro-optic modulator (EOM) which is connected to a microwave source (MS), and the frequency of the radio frequency (RF) signal output from the MS is set to scan from 2.3 GHz to 6.5 GHz with a high resolution covering the free spectrum range (FSR) of a fiber Bragg grating Fabry-Perot interferometer (FBG-FPI), thus the laser output from EOM scans with the same resolution to RF signal within certain wavelength range. The laser is injected into the FBG-FPI yielding extremely narrow transmission peaks within the FBG reflection wavelength range. Experimental results show that the longitudinal modes caused in the FPI cavity which is invisible to normal commercial optical spectrum analyzer (OSA) can be measured accurately and displacement measuring with nanometer resolution can be expected by using this system.

articleTitle: Research on radiation-hard EDFA used in space optical communications
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The damage characteristics of two rare-earth-doped fibers irradiated by electron accelerator and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co radiation source have been investigated, and the radiation sensitivity properties of the key components in EDFA have been compared. And moreover, a study on passive-transmission and radiation-hard EDFA based on modified erbium-doped fiber based on Cerium and hydrogen loading was carried out. The EDFA with improvement radiation-hard properties exhibits a transmission loss decrease by 0.35 dB under a total dose of 70 krad (Si) under the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co radiation.

articleTitle: Testing of single event effect on several commercial chips of optical transceivers based on heavy ions and pulse laser methods
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Single event effect susceptibility of industrial MCUs and key drive chips of several commercial transceivers are studied based on heavy ions and pulse laser methods. Based on the testing results, the performance of receive chips are better than transmit chips or transceiver chips, and the threshold values of transmit chips or transceiver chips are between 30 and 37MeV.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg. However, the MCUs are very sensitive to single event effect, and the threshold value of SEL is lower than 12.6 MeV.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg. And finally, we provided two aspects of hardware and software to improve reliability for optical transceivers, which can be referenced by satellite system designation for various space missions.

articleTitle: Regional fault-tolerant restoration in fiber communication based on SDN
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A regional fault-tolerant restoration mechanism based on SDN is proposed for fiber communication networks. Simulation results show that this mechanism has shorter recovery time and lower restoration failure rate than other mechanism because of avoiding the occurrence of regional faults.

articleTitle: Dislocated Fabry-Perot fiber cavity for strain measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a Fabry-Perot (FP) fiber cavity for strain measurement. The cavity is fabricated by fusion splicing two etched single-mode fibers (SMFs) with core offset in X axis. It is found that the strain sensitivity can be increased from 1.67 to 3.14 pm/με by adopting offset splicing. Such FP cavity is of low cost, compact in size, simple in structure and easy in fabrication, and has high potential in strain sensing.

articleTitle: Low-loss and low-crosstalk hybrid WDM-PDM (de)multiplexer based on a microring-resonator array
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A high-performance hybrid multiplexer for wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) and polarization-division multiplexing (PDM) is proposed and realized by combining a polarization-splitter-rotator (PSR) and a microring resonator (MRR) array. A 16-channel hybrid multiplexer with eight wavelength-channels and dual polarizations is demonstrated as an example. Any MRR works bi-directionally and provides two drop ports. The MRR array enables a box-like response for WDM filtering with a channel spacing of 400 GHz. The 3dB-bandwidth is as large as 2nm and the channel crosstalk is less than −25dB. The on-chip loss for the present 16-channel hybrid (de)multiplexer is ∼3dB only.

articleTitle: Dual pulse bound states in a dispersion-managed mode-locked all-fiber laser with 101.75MHz repetition rate using 45° tilted fiber grating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a dispersion managed Erbium doped all-fiber laser with 101.75MHz repetition rate using 45°TFG to realize mode locking based on nonlinear polarization rotation technique. In our experiment, stable dual-pulse tightly bound states were observed under the pump power of505mW.

articleTitle: Highly birefringence of squeezed holey fiber with round lattice
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A holey fiber with round lattice is squeezed into a hotkey fiber with elliptical lattice and the results show that the squeezed fiber's birefringence is up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> in 1.5 ~ 2.0μm wavelength range. Because of the 360 degree symmetry of the holey fiber with round lattice, it does not require deliberately to adjust the direction of extrusion when the fiber is squeezed. Thus the difficulty of fabricating fiber with higher birefringence has been reduced.

articleTitle: Polarization analyzer based on rotational Doppler Effect
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A polarization analyzer is presented by polarization-mode-frequency mapping. The two orthogonal circularly polarized components of light are converted to two orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes by a q-plate, and then the OAM modes are mapping to two frequencies by using rotational Doppler Effect. The polarization of light can be retrieved by Fourier transform of the signal collected by a photodetector.

articleTitle: Method of spectrum correction in ethylene detection based on TDLAS
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Ethylene is one of the important signature gases in spontaneous combustion forecasting of coal goaf area. It is very important to detect the concentration of ethylene accurately. However, the absorption spectrum of the other interfering gases is always in the ethylene spectrum during the ethylene detecting, which has a great impact on the ethylene's accuracy. In this paper, a spectral correction method is presented to extract pure ethylene spectra. The experiments show that the detection accuracy is improved by nearly 10 times by using this method, so realized the high accuracy detection of ethylene.

articleTitle: Low-cost refractive index sensor based on tadpole structure fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A tadpole-shape fiber sensor, with S-bend fiber cascading spherical shape, has been proposed and experimentally realized in this work. In our experiments, the output spectrum of the proposed sensor was found to be shifted with the changing of the refractive index and the temperature. Experiments results showed that the highest sensitivity of the refractive index was up to -114.845nm/RIU with a wide range from 1.347 to 1.458. Meanwhile, the temperature sensitivity of the sensor was measured to be 0.15nm/<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C with the range from 20 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C to 80 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C. The proposed sensor has the merits of compactness, high sensitivity, wide sensing range and low-cost.

articleTitle: Spectral-compressed fiber laser source for broadband-CARS microspectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A fiber laser source based on a spectral-compressed dissipative soliton oscillator for broadband coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (BCARS) microspectroscopy is reported. The high-power narrowband picosecond pump pulses for BCARS are obtained by spectral compression in a cascaded fiber amplifier. BCARS signal with high spectral resolution is demonstrated by this fiber source.

articleTitle: A new turbulence introduced single scattering model for non-line-of-sight ultraviolet communication
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The long-distance ultraviolet communication has to take the influence of atmosphere turbulence into consideration. This paper proposed a new turbulent channel combined with single scattering model for ultraviolet communication, where the variation of refractive-index structure parameter is introduced. The calculating results of new model is closer to the experimental results compared to that of the original model.

articleTitle: Mode-locked thulium-doped fiber laser with WSe2 based evanescent field interaction
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report, for the first time to our knowledge, the usage of CVD-grown few-layer WSe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> as a saturable absorber for the mode locking of a thulium-doped fiber laser. The WSe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> saturable absorber was deposited on the waist of the tapered fiber. By employing the WSe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> saturable absorber, we demonstrate a passively mode-locked fiber laser operating at 1863.96 nm with a 3 dB spectral bandwidth of 2.89 nm. The fundamental repetition rate was 11.357 MHz with a signal-to-noise ratio of 85 dB.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of multi-domain optical network federator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Aiming at providing united control of multi-domain optical networks orchestration, we design the Federated Platform based on Open Network Operating System (ONOS). Our implementation includes adding and extending modules in ONOS to provide the global view of multi-domain networks and support cross-domain end-to-end services by communicating with the individual domain controllers through RESTCONF protocol. It illustrates the feasibility of the proposed architecture through analyzing the construction of the platform and the functional testing data.

articleTitle: Cost-effective MDM-WDM ROADM scheme based on wavelength reuse
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel cost-effective mode division multiplexing and wavelength division multiplexing (MDM-WDM) reconfigurable optical Add/Drop multiplexer (ROADM) scheme based on wavelength reuse and experimentally demonstrate its feasibility. The proposed scheme could reduce system cost and simplify the wavelength management.

articleTitle: Layered PAM-DHT system for improving effective data transmission
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel system considering layered Pulse Amplitude Modulation with Discrete Hartley Transform (PAM-DHT), in order to improve Effective Data Transmission Efficiency (EDTE) by modulating both odd and even subcarriers. This system is suitable for the optical communication employing Intensity Modulation with Direct Detection (IM/DD). At the transmitter side of this system, signals are divided into different layers for DHT modulation, and then combined for simultaneous transmission. An iterative architecture is utilized to recovery layered signals at the receiver side. Our layered PAM-DHT system does not require Hermitian symmetry because the data modulated by PAM is real. In this way, more subcarriers can be used to transmit effective data simultaneously. In contrast to conventional PAM with Discrete Multitene Transform (PAM-DMT) and single-layer PAM-DHT, our layered PAM-DHT system, which has the similar Bit Error Rate (BER), obtains the EDTE almost 4 times and 2 times improved, respectively. The proposed system also has a lower BER under the same EDTE.

articleTitle: Analysis for transmission performance of ultra-long haul optical fiber link considering quintic nonlinear effect
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, the optical transmission equation of fiber considering fourth-order dispersion and quintic nonlinearity is proposed. Simulation software of ultra-long haul transmission is developed by discretizing the equation with symmetric spilt-step Fourier method. Unrepeatered optical transmission system of 40Gb/s signal centred at 1550nm is designed. The results of numerical analysis show that the quintic nonlinearity with coefficient of 1W~<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/km will result in significant transmission impairments, and Q factor of the system is reduced by 1.9 at distance of 120km. When the optical transmitter power increases from 0.01 W to 0.5W, the average Q factor is declined by 32.5. Therefore, the influence of quintic nonlinearity needs to be considered in the system with high power.

articleTitle: Supercontinuum generation with a repetition rate over 100MHz based on a picosecond pulse from a normal dispersion fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-fiber supercontinuum (SC) source with a repetition rate of over 100 MHz is experimentally demonstrated for the first time. The SC is generated by introducing the pulse output from a normal dispersion fiber laser into high nonlinearity fibers (HNLFs). An erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) and single segment single mode fiber (SMF) are used to compress the pulsewidth to increase pulse peak power. Finally, we can successfully obtain a SC with 10 dB bandwidth of over 500nm. In particular, the spectrum at the C-band is flat with a power fluctuation of less than 3 dB. All those features verify the SC an excellent local oscillator source for linear optical sampling application.

articleTitle: Silicon PAM-4 optical modulator driven by two binary electrical signals with different peak-to-peak voltages
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a silicon PAM-4 optical modulator, which is based on a symmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Two uncorrelated binary electrical signals with different peak-to-peak voltages are applied to the phase shifters of the silicon optical modulator. Accordingly, two different phase shifts are generated in the two arms. After the permutation, there are totally four phase differences between the two arms and the output optical power has four levels. The device can work at 32 Gbaud in the wavelength range from 1525 nm to 1565 nm, which is promising for the next-generation high-speed silicon optical link.

articleTitle: Filtering algorithm research in trace C2H2 detection based on TDLAS
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Real-time and accurate detection of the flammable gas concentration is the key issue in spontaneous combustion prediction. A modified tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) technology has been used in this paper to achieve in-situ detection of trace Acetylene concentration. Noises and interference fringes are eliminated by wavelet adaptive threshold filtering, and then Kalman filtering has been used to smooth the estimated gas concentration. It is demonstrated that the sensitivity is improved from 2 to 0.5 ppm by wavelet denoising and Kalman filtering. The fluctuation of estimated concentration can be suppressed to 1/4 of the original value.

articleTitle: 1310 nm V-cavity semiconductor laser with 38×100GHz tuning range
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A 1310 nm InGaAlAs/InP V-cavity laser (VCL) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The laser is ultra-compact with a device size of only 520μm×300μm. Measurement result shows that 38×100GHz tuning range with above 30dB side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) is achieved.

articleTitle: Resource-efficient content adjustment in real time in elastic optical datacenter networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We investigate the problem of content adjustment in real time according to the usage of storage and spectrum resources in elastic optical datacenter networks. A novel resource-efficient content adjustment (RECA) scheme is proposed to minimize spectrum consumption, content synchronization cost, and blocking probability.

articleTitle: Microwave photonics for high performance sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The attractive use of microwave photonic (MWP) technologies brings about immense benefits to the field of optical sensing. Recent new developments in microwave photonic signal processing techniques that have high potentialities to be used in a variety of sensing applications are presented in the paper, including exploring the use of finite impulse response MWP filters for distributed sensing applications, employing single passband MWP filtering techniques to increase measurement range, and the realization of optoelectronic oscillators for enhanced sensing resolution.

articleTitle: Study on characteristics of random phase-shifted fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A random phase-shifted fiber Bragg grating has been theoretically analysed by the transfer matrix method. Numerical predictions of the effects of phase-shifted points on the reflection spectra of such a grating are calculated. This fiber Bragg grating with 10 random phase-shifted points distributed has been fabricated. These predictions are compared with experimentally measured spectra of the random phase-shifted fiber Bragg gratings. A good agreement between the theoretical predictions and the experimental results was obtained.

articleTitle: Highly polarized multiwavelength Er-doped fibre laser using all fibre Lyot filter
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A multiwavelength Er-doped fibre ring laser system using all fibre Lyot filter and highly nonlinear fibre was experimentally demonstrated, with degree of polarization up to 99.9% and 50 channels output.

articleTitle: Design of temperature sensor based on silicon microring resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A silicon microring-resonator-based temperature sensor which consists of a microring resonator and two straight waveguide at both sides studied. Detailed analysis and simulation are presented and a proof of concept structure is optimized to demonstrate a resonator with resonance wavelength variation about 100.73 pm/K within 50 K temperature range. Two novel methods of tuning the temperature sensor by changing the effective index and the round-trip amplitude transmission factor are proposed and optimized.

articleTitle: Pulse width tunable passively Q-switched fiber laser with graphene saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A pulse width tunable passively Q-switched fiber laser is demonstrated by using a graphene saturable absorber (GSA) with graphene-covered-microfiber (GCM) structure. Due to the cross absorption modulation (XAM) effect in graphene, the modulation depth of the GSA could be varied from 3.22% to 2.16%%, which results in that the output pulse width and the repetition rate of the laser could be varied from 3.5 to 7.5 μs, and from 34.5 to 48.8 KHz, respectively, with fixed pump power.

articleTitle: A new method of photoelectric deviation measurement
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a method for detecting the photoelectric deviation of radar system based on tracking the Change 3 lander is presented. In this method, the accurate position of the lander is calibrated by using the relative position relationship between the Chang'e 3 lander and the feature points in the lunar surface image. Then the miss distance is obtained by calculating the relative position of the center of the optical axis of the lander on calibration TV, and finally the photoelectric deviation is obtained. The proposed method needs less staff and low cost.

articleTitle: Erbium doped fiber lasers based on 45° tilted fiber gratings
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: 45° tilted fiber grating (TFG) possesses a series of merits, such as strong polarization dependant loss (PDL), low insertion loss, superior compatibility, and compactness. One of the most prominent features of such polarizing device is the all-fiber structure. This polarizing element plays an important role in all-fiber integrated systems which have been widely investigated in the last two decades. In this report, we reviewed the recent development in single wavelength, multiple wavelength, Q-switched, and mode locked fiber lasers based on the 45°TFG as in-fiber polarizer.

articleTitle: Multi-tenant fairness in data center networks with flexi-grid optical networking
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we set up a model of multi-tenant fairness in data center networks with flexi-grid optical networking and define the fair sharing degree (FSD) as an effective measurement of fairness. A novel max fairness (MF) scheme is proposed to ensure the fairness and minimum bandwidth of tenants. Numeric results demonstrate that the MF scheme achieves 67%-88% FSD reduction and a better stability of FSD.

articleTitle: Block decision-aided laser phase noise estimation for coherent optical OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a block decision-aided (BL-DA) laser phase noise (LPN) estimation algorithm for coherent optical OFDM (CO-OFDM) systems. The OFDM symbols are divided into several blocks and the LPN estimation and compensation procedure is performed based on the decisions between these blocks. The proposed BL-DA algorithm can be applied for higher LPN estimation while at the same time ensuring a better estimation performance. Simulations are carried out in a 70.6 Gbit/s 16-QAM CO-OFDM system to verify the feasibility and efficiency of the BL-DA algorithm.

articleTitle: Low-loss coupling by injecting tapered solid-core fibers into the hollow-core of anti-resonant fibers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Anti-resonant hollow-core fibers (AR-HCFs) have attracted intensive attention. In order to realize low-loss coupling between anti-resonant hollow-core fibers and solid-core fibers, tapered solid-core fibers are injected into the hollow-core of AR-HCFs. For the ice-cream type anti-resonant hollow-core fibers whose mode field diameter are about 35μm, the coupling efficiency is over 85% when the tapered diameters are around 35~42μm, and the all-fiber structure is the tapered single-mode fibers (HI-1060) injecting into the hollow-core of AR-HCFs and the multi-mode fibers abutted on another end of AR-HCFs as output end. The experimental results show that the maximum coupling efficiency is 74.59%, which provides a feasible low-loss coupling scheme for AR-HCFs with large mode field diameters.

articleTitle: Study of narrow pulse driver circuit with adjustable width and amplitude
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A narrow pulse driver circuit was studied in this paper. we proposed and demonstrated a method combining the analog circuit and the digital circuit. By analyzing the working principle of transistor, we selected the HEMT transistor as a high-speed switch. It can supply voltage pulse or current pulse according to different applications. The generation of trigger signal, controls of the pulse width and amplitude were highly integrated on one circuit board. Experimental results show that the width of pulse can be tuned from 1.95 ns to 800 ns with the pulse amplitude from 0 to 5V.

articleTitle: A vertical integrated optoelectronic chip for optical interconnect
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an integrated optoelectronic chip, which can transmit optical signal at 849.2nm and receive optical signal at 803nm, is proposed. It is constructed by integrating a VCSEL unit above a PIN-PD unit. Analysis show that, the VCSEL unit has a threshold current around 1mA and a maximum output power around 1.2mW at 849.2nm, the PIN-PD unit has a highest absorption quantum efficiency above 70% at 803nm and a absorption range of 11nm where absorption quantum efficiency is higher than 60%. It can be applied to further improve the performance of optical interconnect system.

articleTitle: Key technologies of EPON communication network for new intelligent substation
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Traditional intelligent substation communication network has the problem in large transmission delay and delay jitter. This paper studied service isolation and low delay technology as the key technologies of EPON communication network for new intelligent substation. We built the experimental network and tested the performances of various services under different load conditions, the results verified the effectiveness of this new communication network.

articleTitle: Long cavity passive harmonic mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a passive harmonic mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser with long cavity based on nonlinear polarization rotation (NPR). The total cavity length is 696 m, which can be achieved by incorporating a 650 m long single mode fiber (SMF). The fiber laser produces 6.1 ps, 6.49 nJ mode-locked pulse at a fundamental repetition rate of 306.4 kHz. And from 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> to 16<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order passive harmonic mode-locked pulse trains have been experimentally observed.

articleTitle: An enhanced differential carrier phase extraction method for wideband signal in CEI
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, an enhanced differential carrier phase extraction method for carrier-suppressed wideband signal in CEI measurement is proposed. Based on Costas loop, after orthogonal transformation, low-pass filtering and phase detection, the differential carrier phase of the received signal of the two measuring stations can be obtained directly. It is more efficient comparing with the traditional method, which extracts the carriers respectively and then differentiate their phase. At the same time, its working frequency is the frequency of carrier, and will not lead to the phase ambiguity caused by doubling frequency, phase ambiguity solution is not needed. For the ambiguity of anti-tangent phase detector, correct differential carrier phase can be obtained under the constraint of the priori delay model. The Monte Carlo simulation results show that the method has a small error and stable performance in different SNR.

articleTitle: Numerical study of bound states solitons in a dispersion-managed fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a detailed characterization of the bound states solitons in a dispersion-managed fiber laser with respect to the dynamics of time domain separation and phase difference. The theoretical results reveal that the bound states solitons in a nonlinear system have two equilibria, and different initial conditions would induce the pulse separation and phase difference to distinct fixed points. Moreover, bound states solitons have opposite evolution direction in phase plane in different equilibria. Interesting, the behaviour of bound states solitons like a damped oscillator when the initial separation is suitable.

articleTitle: Study of multispectral polarization visible light propagation properties under smog conditions
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Polarization imaging technology has shown great advantages in military reconnaissance, vegetation remote sensing and aerosol detection, and the study of the properties of the polarized light transmission can better promote the development of technology. In this paper, according to the characteristics of multi-spectral polarized light transmission in smog environment, an experimental test device of multiple spectral bands of visible light is built in the smog simulation environment, experiments show that when the wavelength changes between 0.5–0.73um, the polarized light of the circularly polarized light is larger than that of the linearly polarized light, and the linearly polarized light exhibits better polarization characteristics in the other wavelengths of the visible light.

articleTitle: High resolution ISAR imaging using homotopic non-convex regularization
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel high-resolution inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging method using homotopic non-convex regularization technique is proposed in this paper. Compared with existing compressive sensing (CS) based imaging methods, the proposed method can deal well with off-grid scatterers in the imaging scene, besides it has low computational complexity, therefore has potential to be applied in practice. Experimental results with B727 data show the effectiveness of related analysis.

articleTitle: Terahertz polarization splitter based on partial coupling in dual slotted core polymer fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A terahertz (THz) polarization splitter based on asymmetric dual slotted core polymer fiber is proposed and numerically investigated. The dual slotted core composed of subwavelength-scale air slots that are independently suspended within the fiber, not only allows for single-mode propagation for the two orthogonal polarization modes with low absorption losses, but also enables them to couple with each other. The transmission modes, splitting lengths, and pertinent performance parameters are numerically investigated at a center-frequency of 1.0 THz, which shows a short splitting length of ~1 cm, an ultra-low transmission loss of 0.4 dB, a bandwidth of 0.18 THz and extinction ratios (ER) of -17.66 dB for X polarization mode and -90.66 dB for Y polarization mode.

articleTitle: Collaborative video distribution in storage-limited passive optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the development of passive optical networks (PONs), to cache videos on optical network units (ONUs) is now considering as an efficient scheme for better-quality video service provision. In this paper, we study the problem of collaborative video distribution among ONUs under the limited storage capacity of each ONU with the aim to maximize the video hit ratio of ONUs (VHRO). Two scenarios will be specifically studied: (1) the videos stored by each ONU can be delivered to all peer ONUs without bandwidth limitation; (2) the bandwidth used to receive videos from peer ONUs is limited for each ONU. Under the first scenario, we show that the maximum VHRO for a special case of the problem can be approximately calculated, and the general case of the problem can be transformed into a multiple knapsacks problem. Under the second scenario, we propose an efficient heuristic algorithm to solve the problem. The efficiency of the work is finally validated by simulation.

articleTitle: Polarization mode dispersion monitoring based on auxiliary optical signal gain
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a novel polarization mode dispersion (PMD) monitoring method by adding auxiliary optical signal is presented. Based on four-wave mixing (FWM), the PMD can be monitored in all-optical domain by measuring the power of the idler wave. With the help of auxiliary signal, the change trend of idler wave power with PMD will be enlarged, which expands the scope of monitoring and improves the monitoring sensitivity. When the PMD varies from Ops to 50ps, by analyzing the simulation results of 4 channels RZ-TDM signal with the transmission rate of 40Gbit/s, it is concluded that the signal power requirement of the new device is low, and the accumulated chromatic dispersion (CD) has little effect on the monitoring performance. It is suitable for PMD monitoring of different duty cycle signals with higher speed and more complex modulation formats.

articleTitle: Linearization of phase modulation link using stimulated brillouin scattering
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a linearization technique to modify the nonlinear transfer function of a phase modulation link. The phase modulation signal is converted into intensity modulation signal, and the phase of the optical carrier band is shifted. Eventually the third-order intermodulation distortion (IMD3) components produced by different optical spectrum components have opposite phase, with destructive combination in electronic domain, the IMD3 will be eliminated. Theoretical analysis is given and an experiment is conducted, results show that the spurious dynamic range is 106.7 dBHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sup> for the linearized link, as compared with the link without linearization, an enhancement of 10.4 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: A new type vertically integrated device for optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A vertically integrated device composed of Vertical-Cavity Surface-Emitting Laser (VCSEL) unit and Resonant Cavity Enhanced Photodiode (RCE-PD) unit is proposed, which has huge potential application perspectives for optical interconnects. The performance of the integrated device and the interaction of its two composing units are analyzed based on different structure optimization. As optimized, its two units can be functionally decoupled from each other. For VCSEL unit, the threshold current is 1.25 mA and the slope efficiency is 0.89W/A. For RCE-PD unit, the quantum efficiency is up to 90.5%.

articleTitle: Design of the microwave photonic filter with rectangular response
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a method to design and implement the microwave photonic filter with rectangular response by using the frequency comb, spatial light modulator-based spectrum shaper and dispersive element. Numerical results are presented to verify the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: In-fiber grating based optical signal processors
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In-fiber gratings provide a perfect platform for directly processing optical signals in optical fiber with ultra fast speed. Their spectral profile and dispersion profile can tailored to realise various functionalities in different applications. This paper will focus on the discussion of our past and recent development on fiber grating devices that are used for optical signal processing.

articleTitle: Research on mechanism and structure of all-fiber weak magnetic field atomic sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, combined with the high-sensitivity weak magnetic field measurement technique of atomic magnetometer structure and the high precision measurement advantage of optical fiber sensing technology, an all-fiber weak magnetic sensor (AFWMS) structure is proposed and studied deeply. The sensing principle of measuring the weak magnetic field by using the atomic magnetometer structure is analyzed. A sensor model for the weak magnetic field was stablished.

articleTitle: Trace gas sensing based on Min-IR CW broadly tunable Cr:ZnSe laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Recent progress in development of broadly tunable Cr:ZnSe lasers for trace gas detection is reported. With an intracavity CaF2 prism, the CW Cr:ZnSe laser was tuned within a total wavelength range of 427 nm from 2164 nm to 2591 nm. And, the applied research about trace gas sensing based on Mid-IR broadly tunable Cr:ZnSe lasers has been discussed in this paper, which indicated that a single-frequency broadly tunable Cr:ZnSe laser is a promising source for the applications on the trace gas sensing.

articleTitle: Broadband ytterbium-doped femtosecond fiber laser around 980 nm
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report a broadband ytterbium-doped femtosecond fiber laser around 980nm. The cavity is based on the all-normal dispersion (ANDi) configuration, including a diffraction-grating which plays a crucial role as a narrow-band spectral filter. The spectral bandwidth of mode-locked pulse reaches 11.4 nm, which approaches the gain bandwidth (about 13nm) of the ytterbium doped fiber around 980 nm. The pulse can be compressed down to 180 fs. With larger pump power, the bandwidth can reach up to 17.9 nm.

articleTitle: A novel ISAR imaging method for high speed moving target based on parametric sparse representation
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: ISAR imaging of high speed moving target has drawn extensive attention for its practical applications. However, the imaging quality is affected significantly by the phase modulation induced by high speed motion.
