To suppress the influences of high speed motion efficiently, a novel ISAR imaging method for high speed moving target based on the parametric sparse representation is proposed. First, the echo signal is sparse represented via designing a flexible parametric sensing matrix according to high speed motion. Subsequently, the sensing matrix is optimized after adaptive computation, during which the target velocity estimation is involved. Finally, a clear ISAR image can be reconstructed with less sampling data and without the motion compensation in conventional ISAR imaging. Compared to the existing method based on compressed sensing (CS), the proposed method possesses lower computational complexity and better robustness.

articleTitle: Research on the refractive index sensitivity of Ex-TFG sensor modified with 20 nm gold nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new method to modify excessively titled fiber gratings (Ex-TFGs) with 20 nm gold nanoparticles (GNPs) through 3-mercapt-otrimethoxysilane(MPTMS) was proposed. By monitoring the wavelength shift of Ex-TFGs for every modified step and using the scanning electron microscope (SEM), it proves that GN Ps are firmly combined on the surface of Ex-TFGs. Finally, by using different concentration of NaCl solutions to calibrate the refractive index (RI) sensitivity, we demonstrated that the sensitivity of the 81° Ex-TFG get an improvement increasing from ~150nm/R IU to ~160nm/RIU.

articleTitle: A design of an optical polarization division multiplexing system based on a Multi-slot and Multi-level Coding technique
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we design a 6 user (5Gbps) optical based on the Multi-slot and Multi-level Coding (MSAC) system with optical polarization multiplexing technique(PolDM). Compared with no polarization multiplexing system, an analysis of the relationship between system BER and the fiber length and the transmission rate was presented. Results show that the BER of the system which we designed reduces about 2-3 orders of magnitude than non-polarization multiplexing system. This shows that the system can support higher bit rate, and it is less sensitive to the chromatic dispersion effect.

articleTitle: Actively Q-switched cylindrical vector beam fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We report an actively Q-switched fiber laser with cylindrical vector beam emission using a few-mode fiber Bragg grating as mode selection and acousto-optic modulator to achieve the ideal ns pulse. Both radially and azimuthally polarized beams have been obtained by tuning the polarization controllers. The generated Q-switched CVB operates at central wavelength of 1055.6 nm with a spectrum bandwidth about 0.6 nm, signal-to-background ratio of more than 50 dB. The pulse width is about 64ns and the pulse energy is 1.3μ7 at a 20 kHz repetition rate.

articleTitle: On the characterization of a green-light directly-modulated diode-pumped solid-state laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Directly modulated semiconductor lasers for underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) have limitations in output power and beam quality. Diode-pumped solid-state lasers (DPSSLs) have the merits of long lifetime, high stability, large power and good beam quality, which are promising to realize long-each UWOC. We compose a DPSSL with discrete components and measure its key parameters. The bandwidth constraint of the DPSSL imposed by the long lifetime of the gain medium is circumvented with the strategy of orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM). After 5.74-m underwater transmission, the BERs of the 40.28-Mb/s 32-quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) signal and the 50.78-Mb/s 16-QAM signal are 1.09×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and 3.53×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, respectively. We also demonstrate that the QAM order generated by the directly modulated DPSSL can be as high as 128.

articleTitle: Application of a modified LED lens model on a double free-form surface
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A modified double free-form surface (FS) model is proposed to optimize the optical lens based on surface fitting technology. A LED lens with double FS structure is designed based on this optimized double FS model as an application. To verify the advantages of this model, both a ray tracing simulation and a normalized irradiant detection are trialed by a LED test system. The experimental result shows that the Reserved Mean Standard Deviation (RMSD) is less than 0.02 for double FS based LED lens and its energy delivery efficiency are up to 92.26%. It suggests that the lighting spot of double FS based LED lens has a well distribution performance.

articleTitle: A multiwavelength random fiber laser with odd and even order stokes output separated
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A multiwavelength random fiber laser based on stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) with odd and even order Stokes output separated is proposed and demonstrated experimentally. The gain is provided by the SBS and erbium doped fiber amplifier, while the Rayleigh scattering in single mode fiber (SMF) provides random distributed feedback. With a two-branch structure, we successfully make the laser output with odd and even order Stokes separated.

articleTitle: 177 fs, 16.5 nJ erbium-based all-fiber CPA system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate a simple all-fiber erbium-doped CPA system with a large mode area fiber compressor, delivering 177 fs pulse with ~16.5 nJ energy at 39.5 MHz pulse repetition rate.

articleTitle: High-sensitivity and large-dynamic-range fiber refractometer based on composite-cavity Fabry-Perot structure
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Most sensors have the tradeoff dilemma of high sensitivity and large dynamic range. We demonstrate here an all-fiber refractive index sensor based on a composite intrinsic Fabry-Perot interferometer (FPI), which possesses the co-existence advantages of high sensitivity and large dynamic range. Experimental trends are in good agreement with the theoretical predictions. The co-existence of high sensitivity and large dynamic range in a composite FPI is of great significance to practical refractive index measurement.

Author Keywords: high sensitivity larger dynamic range co-existence

articleTitle: Side-excitation fiber-optic laser-ultrasonic transducer based on fused taper fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel side-excitation fiber-optic laser-ultrasound transducer based on fused taper fiber is proposed and demonstrated. The transducer achieves ultrasound generation at optical fiber sidewall and performs a relative high conversion efficiency. In the experiments, 514 mV peak-to-peak power ultrasound wave has been obtained at the fiber sidewall with input 0.04 mJ laser pulse. Theoretical analysis and experimental results show that the strength of generated ultrasound wave can be controlled by adjusting the taper length of the fused fiber taper. The proposed method is promising candidate to achieve the multi-point laser-ultrasonic generation along a fiber.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of different ADO-OFDM channel equalization algorithms in visible light communication system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We investigate and analyze the asymmetrically clipped and direct-current-biased optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (ADO-OFDM) in visible light communication (VLC) system. Then we propose two modified channel equalization algorithms of ADO-OFDM in VLC systems. It is shown that the algorithm combined with channel estimation for interference cancellation to recover ADO-OFDM signal is more effective in VLC system, which has the best BER performance.

articleTitle: Joint routing and wavelength allocation algorithm for stealth and ordinary services in optical transport networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we develop two joint routing and resource allocation algorithms for stealth and ordinary services in optical networks. The transmission of stealth service needs to be hidden in ordinary services to achieve a better performance in privacy. Two heuristic algorithms construct paths for stealth and ordinary services base on the different routing methods. The proposed algorithms improve the success rate of optical steganography by slightly increasing more wavelength consumption.

articleTitle: A 8×8 arrayed waveguide grating router based on SOI platform
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design and experimentally fabricate a 8×8 arrayed waveguide grating router(AWGR) with a channel spacing of400 GHz based on silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform. The arrayed waveguide region of this device is horseshoe-shaped to realize a small footprint of 730 μm × 580 μm. Experimental results show good cyclic performance. The crosstalk and insertion loss are about -21 dB and 2.7 dB, respectively. This compact device can be used in optical interconnect systems.

articleTitle: A noise reduction algorithm based on EMD and wavelet for FBG-FP static-strain sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A static-strain FBG-FPs sensor with high resolution based on empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and wavelet algorithm is proposed. The FBG-FPs are interrogated by a narrow-linewidth fiber laser which is driven by an optical single sideband (SSB-SC) modulator. Adaptive basis functions which are denoised by wavelet algorithm can be extracted from two FBG-FPs' reflection spectra by EMD. Adaptive basis functions can be used to reconstruct the reflection spectra. The relative wavelength difference of the reconstructed reflection spectra is calculated. A minimum static-strain resolution of 0.42 nε is achieved.

articleTitle: A compensation method for blind pixels of infrared focal plane array
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: As influenced by environment, deterioration of material, while using infrared focal plane array (IRFPA) device, new blind pixels will appear inevitably The blind pixels can badly reduce the image quality. If there is no condition for precise detection and compensation afresh, a on-line method for blind pixels capture and compensation is introduced. The method has acquired well effect in actual work while using IRFPA device.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and delay fairness in Time Wavelength Division Multiplexed Passive Optical Network (TWDM-PON)
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Because of its high transmission rate, Time and Wavelength Division Multiplexed Passive Optical Network (TWDM-PON) has become a particular research topic. Due to the wavelength flexibility and multiple user's access, it becomes necessary and imperative to consider the fairness between all the Optical Network Units (ONUs) so that we can improve the quality of service of the users. This fairness includes the bandwidth allocation and the time delay of using a wavelength. We proposed an approach named Bandwidth and Delay Fairness (BDF) algorithm to improve the fairness. Simulation results show that our approach increases the fairness of all the ONUs.

articleTitle: MiFlO: A scheduling algorithm based on mice flows optimization in hybrid data center network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: With the rapid development of cloud computing and emerging services, traffic in data center network is experiencing an explosive growth, which has brought a great challenge to the existing electrical data center networks. In order to take full advantage of the large bandwidth of optical interconnects, the optical and electrical hybrid data center network is proposed. However, there are still some defects in terms of flow scheduling, such as huge computing burden on controller and indeterminate mice trans-mission delay, which have a negative effect on network performance. In this paper, we propose MiFlO, a new scheduling algorithm which classifies the mice/elephant flows in servers and ensures the priority of mice flows. In this way, MiFlO can reduce the computing overhead of switches and improve the communication performance of data center network. The results show that MiFlO has better performance than traditional scheduling algorithm FIFO. The average latency of mice flows in the network can be reduced by about 12% with MiFlO deployed.

articleTitle: LACE: A non-blocking on-chip optical router by utilizing the wavelength routing technology
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical Network-on-Chip (ONoC) is deemed as a promising candidate in future on-chip interconnection scenario. It is superior to the traditional electrical NoC in many aspects, such as the bandwidth density, power consumption and scalability. On-chip optical router is an indispensable building block in ONoC design. However, most reported optical routers are with four or five ports, which cannot be easily grafted into the network with the need for 3D interconnect or high concentration. In this paper, we propose LACE, a non-blocking on-chip optical router with 8 ports, which is appropriate for the 3D interconnect and high-concentration network. By embracing the Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) technique, LACE can implement non-blocking communication between different ports. The evaluation results show that LACE has lower area cost and lower insertion loss compared to the alternatives.

articleTitle: All-fiber mode converter based on fiber grating and multimode interference
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a novel mode converter (MC) based on multimode interference (MMI). This MC taking advantages of long-period fiber grating and multimode interference, it not only has high conversion efficiency, but also greatly reduces the interference between modes.

articleTitle: High-priority assignment first dynamic wavelength and bandwidth allocation algorithm in TWDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: As the differences in user business demand increasing, in order to effectively reduce the network delay and improve resource utilization, a High-priority Assignment First Dynamic Wavelength and Bandwidth Allocation algorithm (HAF-DWBA) in TWDM-PON is proposed. According to the Service-Level Agreement to determine the priority of ONUs, this algorithm can implement five types of T-CONT and four kinds of bandwidth allocation. Simulation results show that, HAF-DWBA can effectively reduce the average delay, slightly improve bandwidth utilization and make better fairness for different types of bandwidth allocation.

Author Keywords: Wavelength selection. High-priority. Dynamic bandwidth allocation

articleTitle: Quantization noise and sampling jitter impact of ADC/DAC in multi-IFoF based mobile fronthaul
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Multiple IFoF has long been a promising method to provide a high bandwidth efficient solution to connect remote radio unit and baseband unit pool in C-RAN architecture. To obtain stable performance, it is desirable to make frequency conversion and multiplexing in digital way, which makes ADC/DAC inevitable. In this work, we study the quantization noise and sampling jitter effect upon multi-IFoF system, providing valuable references for making technical choices during future fronthaul system construction.

articleTitle: Low complexity and high accuracy sampling frequency offset estimation and compensation algorithm in IMDD-OFDM system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel sampling frequency offset estimation algorithm to improve the performance of the practical intensity-modulation and direction-detection (IMDD)-based OFDM system. For this scheme, only OFDM symbol is used, which reduce the complexity of implement in practical system. And, by taking the relationship of phase rotating of subcarriers into account, we successfully estimate the SFO with the error limited within 3ppm by one OFDM symbols. After SFO compensation, the performance of OFDM signal is greatly enhanced that hard decision BER limit (3.8×10-3) can be achieved at sensitivity of -9dBm and 100 ppm SFO.

articleTitle: Security and coding performance of spectral phase coding
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Spectral phase coding by using 0/π-phase-shift and ±π/2-phase-shift are thoroughly studied. The security vulnerability and improvement are analysed by evaluating the encoded signal. ίπ/2-phase-shift spectral phase coding can guarantee the security by hiding the optical code in the encoded signal. In addition, coding performance of both spectral phase coding techniques is investigated by measuring auto-correlation and cross-correlation properties when using a set of 7-chip and 31-chip optical codes. ±π/2-phase-shift spectral phase coding presents better coding performance. It is for the first time revealed that the coding performance of spectral phase coding is irrelevant to the properties of the optical codes.

articleTitle: PAM-4 optical signal generation using a silicon Mach-Zehnder modulator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper we demonstrate the 4 level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) signal generation through a silicon Mach-Zehnder modulator. The baud speed of the PAM-4 signal generation is characterized up to 32 Gbaud (64Gb/s). And we have measured the device's bit error rate (BER) up to 32 Gbaud and the spurious free dynamic range (SFDR) of the distortion component of the modulated light.

articleTitle: Research of carbon coating on optical fiber sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The research on long-term stability of optical fiber sensor has drawn more and more attention in recent years, especially due to corrosion and hydrogen loss in harsh environment, while carbon plating on the surface of optical fiber sensor is proven to be an effective way to enhance the performance of optic-fiber sensor. Chemical vapor deposition (CVD) were introduced and a device for depositing carbon film on optical fiber sensor utilizing CVD was presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Microwave photonics based radar TRx modules and their application in ISAR
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents TRx modules based on microwave photonics developed by Tsinghua University and their application in ISAR. The Tx module is based on OAWG, and can produce signal with arbitrary waveforms on the demand with its frequency tuneable from GHz to 100GHz. its bandwidth up to 10GHz, and its maximum duration up to the order of millisecond. The Rx is a coherent frond end with its central frequency tuneable and its bandwidth reconfigurable to match the Tx. With the TRx, an ISAR experimental system is building up. imaging results show it has a range resolution of 5 cm and a velocity resolution of +/-2m/s in the case of TRx working at X band with the bandwidth of 4GHz.

articleTitle: Cascaded photonic crystal fibers for three stage non-integer order soliton compression
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A detailed fiber design was presented for the first time for three-stage non-integer order soliton compression at the wavelength of 1060 nm. A compression factor of 173.52 was realized, and the remained pedestal is only 32.21%.

articleTitle: Two modified constant modulus methods based on independent component analysis for polarization demultiplexing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Two modified constant modulus algorithms (CMA) based on independent component analysis (ICA) are proposed for polarization demultiplexing. We demonstrated a single carrier 16-Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) Polarization division multiplexing (PDM) coherent optical communication system with the modified CMA methods to prove that the proposed methods have the similar performance but solve the problem of slow convergence of the traditional CMA.

articleTitle: All-optical equalizer for bandwidth-limited RSOA to transmit 10 Gbps NRZ and ODB signals in WDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The finite gain recovery time of the reflective semiconductor optical amplifier (RSOA) causes distortion and pattern dependence at high bit rates in colorless optical network units (ONUs) of WDM passive. optical network (WDN-PON). The all-optical equalizers based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) and fiber Bragg grating (FBG) are proposed to improve RSOA bandwidth so that to achieve 10 Gbps upstream transmission. The operating principle of optical equalizer from theoretical calculations and simulation demonstration are analysed in detail. The improved received sensitivity is achieved and the open eye diagram is displayed. With the help of optical equalizer, the pattern dependence is effectively suppressed, which demonstrate the feasibility of FBG and MZI for optical equalizer.

articleTitle: Dynamics of gain and phase in semiconductor optical amplifiers in counter-propagating
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Gain and phase dynamics induced by ultra-short pulse in semiconductor optical amplifiers operating in counter-propagating scheme are numerically investigated by employing a field propagation model. The numerical model accounts for the carrier depletion, carrier heating, spectral hole burning and gain dispersion. Propagating schemes have significant influences on gain and phase dynamics, especially for the ultrafast dynamics. Compared to the co-propagating, the counter-propagating causes reduced ultrafast dynamics in gain and phase dynamics. Relatively slow saturation processes in gain dynamics are observed. Analysis results show the drive currents and active lengths of semiconductor optical amplifiers are the main factors influencing the slow saturation processes.

articleTitle: Light-tree based multicast flow aggregation scheme in elastic optical datacenter networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a light-tree based multicast flow aggregation (LT-MFA) scheme which can achieve the cost-efficient multicast service provisioning in elastic optical datacenter networks (EDONs). Moreover, a user-cover ratio based aggregation strategy is proposed for the LT-MFA scheme. An Integer Linear Program (ILP) model and a heuristic algorithm are developed to realize the LT-MFA scheme in the small-scale and large-scale EDONs. Simulations show that the LT-MFA scheme can effectively reduce network cost than conventional light-tree based optical multicasting scheme.

articleTitle: A methylcellulose coated humidity sensor based on Mach-Zehnder interferometer with photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A methylcellulose (MC) coated humidity sensor by using photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. It is fabricated by sandwiching a PCF between two standard single mode fibers (SMFs) with the air holes of the PCF in the fusion splicing region being fully collapsed. Experimental results show that this structure can not only carry on the intensity modulation, but also carry on the wavelength modulation, and the sensitivity in high humidity region is 0.57nm/%RH(relative humidity unit), 0.608dB/%RH respectively. We can be seen that the sensor has high sensitivity in high humidity area. It also shows that the humidity sensitive film of the wet characteristics of good, good stability, so it can be applied to humidity measurement.

articleTitle: A low-crosstalk optical router using multi-layer coupled MR for ONoC
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Crosstalk noise is a potential issue for optical router used by optical network-on-chip (ONoC). The huge crosstalk directly degrades the performance in optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) at optical router level, and greatly limits the scalability at ONoC level. This paper proposes ILCOR, a low-crosstalk optical router using multi-layer coupled MR. The use of multi-layer coupled MR enables less waveguide crossings which are closely related to crosstalk. As results show, the average OSNR for ILCOR increases by 1.7× and 6.7× compared with Cygnus and Crossbar, respectively.

articleTitle: Passively Q-switched Erbium-doped fiber lasers using PbS polystyrene film as saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have demonstrated a passively Q-switched Erbium-doped fiber laser using PbS quantum dots polystyrene film (QDPF) as saturable absorbers (SAs). Compared with other SA materials, PbS QDPFs have advantages of broad absorption range, high quantum yield, and facile preparation. We have successfully generated stable Q-switched pulse with a repetition rate of 20.98 kHz. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of passively Q-switched pulse generation using PbS QDPF as SAs.

articleTitle: The generation of dissipative soliton resonance from dumbbell-shaped Er-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrate an all fiber Er-doped mode-locked fiber laser based on dumbbell-shaped dual-amplifier structure. This laser functions in dissipative soliton resonance regime. Both a nonlinear optical fiber loop mirror and a nonlinear amplifying optical fiber loop mirror are employed to initiate the mode-locked laser. We find that one amplifier can control amplitude and duration of output pulse at the same time, however another can only control the amplitude by varying pump power of each amplifier. Pulse width can change from 0.8ns to 2.6ns and peak power varies from 13 W to 27 W. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) can approach 80 dB.

articleTitle: Crosstalk mitigation in a free space orbital angular momentum multiplexing system based on ICA
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Interference in free space OAM multiplexing system is mainly caused by atmospheric turbulence, which can cause the energy of the OAM beam to diffuse to adjacent beams to introduce crosstalk. We demonstrate the mitigation of crosstalk in a free space OAM multiplexing system based on ICA algorithm. The results show that the required OSNR at BER of 3.8×10-3 is reduced by 3dB with ICA algorithm.

articleTitle: A new type of few-mode photonic crystal fiber with nearly-zero flattened dispersion properties
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new Few-mode photonic crystal fiber (FM-PCF) is designed. By adding leakage channels of mode and replacing the circular air-holes of the first central ring with elliptic air-holes, the confinement loss of second-order mode and the high order model can be greater than 1dB/m, while a more flattened dispersion curve can be realized. The impacts of the parameters of the FM-PCF on the dispersion properties are analyzed. The results indicate that the second-order odd mode LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>(odd) was effectively suppressed to achieve the transmission of fundamental mode LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub>, second-order even mode LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>(even), and third-order mode LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>. The dispersion value in 1550nm of three mode are 0.13ps/(nm·km), 0.04ps/(nm·km), 0. 014ps/(nm·km) when PCF of Λ=20μm, d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>/Λ=0.85, d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/Λ=0.4, so this PCF can achieve dispersion-flattened transmission in the wavelength range of communication.

articleTitle: Wavelength switchable, free spectral range accurately control single-pass Mach-Zehnder interferometer comb filter
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a new and simple method to implement an all fiber, wavelength switchable, free spectral range (FSR) accurately controlled single-pass Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) comb filter, which consists of a polarization controller (PC) and a segment of tapered fiber in one arm. Through rotating the PC, the wavelength switchable operation was obtained. Using fused taper technology to draw the fiber in one arm can precisely control the optical path different, and the filter with expected FSR of 0.8 nm and 0.4 nm were achieved successfully in theory and experiment.

articleTitle: A converged communication system with ultra high bit rate based on photonic RF wave
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A converged communication system with 100 Gbps based on photonic RF wave is proposed. In the system, the mechanism of the photonic RF wave with 40 GHz is demonstrated. With the comprehensive applications of advanced modulation technologies and excellent algorithms, the wireless access rate of the downstream can reach up to 100 Gbps. Due to the photoelectric direct detection, the whole system becomes simple. The photonic RF wave is generated by optical high frequency multiplication technology, which makes that the local ultra-high frequency oscillator is simplified greatly. Compared with some of the recent public research reports, the cost of the system scheme is dropped sharply.

articleTitle: Humidity sensor based on core-offset fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer coated graphene oxide film
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Recently, some fiber sensing applications by coating graphene oxide or reduce graphene oxide have been proposed. In this paper, a novel humidity sensor based on core-offset fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer coated graphene oxide film has been carried out. Here, we use the chemical method to deal with the surface of the fiber first, and then coated graphene oxide on the surface of the optical fiber sensing arm. The sensitivity of 0.104dB/%RH with a linear correlation coefficient of 99.61% and good stability under the relative humidity range of 30%-60% was obtained.

articleTitle: Cross-layer Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation Algorithm Based on Convex Optimization Theory In satellite communication system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a novel Cross-layer Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation Algorithm Based on Convex Optimization Theory(CO-CDBA) in Digital Video Broadcast-Return Channel via Satellite system is proposed. A novel utility function by taking application layer, Data Link Layer and physical layer(PHY) parameters into account is established. The Dynamic Bandwidth Allocation(DBA) problem is converted to a convex optimization problem with constraints, which can be solved by using a fast interval iterative algorithm. The allocation result, utility value, users' fairness performance and allocation procedure based on CO-CDBA are simulated. Results show that CO-CDBA can reduce computational complexity and efficiently allocate bandwidth for each user. Fairness and utility are significantly improved compared with Max-Min and water-filling model.

articleTitle: An ultra-wideband polarization rotator based on SOI by using mode converters and a phase shifter
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We propose a scheme to realize polarization rotation (PR) based on SOI by using two mode converters and a phase shifter. Simulation results from 3D-FDTD show that the PR has extinction ratio (ER) larger than 20 dB and insertion loss less than 0.4 dB in an ultra-wide range from 1450 nm to 1650 nm for both TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. Moreover, the total length of the device is 33μm with a height of 220 nm.

articleTitle: High-speed free-space laser communications using advanced coherent modulation formats
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the high-speed free-space optical (FSO) transmission over 1 km using 20 Gbit/s advanced coherent quadrature phase-shift keying (QPSK) signals. The constellation diagram and the bit error rate (BER) are measured. The receiving sensitivity of the FSO transmission is about −23.9 dBm at the BER of 3.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>.

articleTitle: An adaptive method for network delay modification
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive method to modify network delay caused by clock skew. First, we introduce the concept of end-to-end network delay, and then we propose a method which aims at eliminate the effect cause by the difference clock frequency. The method first denoises the data set to remove error points, and then uses Least Square Method to estimate the clock skew in distributed network. Finally, the method modifies the network delay by a modification term according to the clock skew. Our algorithm calculates the the clock skew and updates the data set currently, which adaptively adjusts the modification term. The experimental results show that the method can effectively eliminate the influence of clock skew on network delay, and has good accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Risk balancing routing assignment mechanism based software defined optical network service importance
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The software defined optical network (SDON) service plays an important role in the production and operation of the network system. It's important to solve the problem of how to reduce the risk and distribute the service path more rationally. However, most of the existing algorithms do not take into account service importance. In this paper, a risk balancing routing assignment mechanism based service importance is proposed. Finally, the simulation shows that compared with the other two methods, the SIRBRM can reduce the link risk and the overall network risk, make the service distribution more uniform.

articleTitle: Latest industry trend in pluggable optics
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Pluggable optics can potentially fuel the optical transport network in a more efficient and manageable manner. To enable this revolutionary packet-optical engine, integrated photonics seems to be the only possible solution. We introduce the latest industry trend of pluggable optical module form factors, and review the latest progress and challenges of pluggable optics products. Furthermore, we discuss our recent demonstration on a compact solution to timing skew of coherent transmitter in the pluggable optical module.

articleTitle: Cascade co-pumping — A new way of efficient pumping of high-power rare-earth co-doped fiber lasers and amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a new efficient pumping scheme was proposed for high-power rare-earth co-doped fiber lasers and amplifiers. We show by numerical simulations that by introducing a resonant cavity oscillating in the sensitizer's emission band can effectively convert the cladding-pump to a more efficient core-pump. This method greatly helps to suppress the amplified spontaneous emission in the sensitizer's band, increase the efficiency, and reduce the gain fiber length.

articleTitle: Magneto-optical fiber sagnac sensor based on silica tube filled with magnetic fluid
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A magnetic field optical fiber sensor based on Sagnac interference is proposed by inserting a silica tube filled with magnetic fluid into the Sagnac loop. The birefringence of the sensor is present in the loop, and the transmission spectrum as a function of the magnetic field intensity has been theoretically analyzed and experimentally demonstrated. The results show that the spectral response is proportional to the magnetic field ranging from 0 to 250Oe with the maximum sensitivity of 0.006dB/Oe. This suggests that the proposed device could have various applications in optical fiber sensor and optical fiber communication.

articleTitle: Dynamic bandwidth defragmentation in TWDM-PON based ethernet fronthaul
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Using Ethernet in fronthaul can achieve statistical multiplexing gains based on the new function split. When TWDM-PON is used in Ethernet based fronthaul network, the large granularity of bandwidth requirements and the diversified service types will lead to the bandwidth fragmentation in OLT pooling. To solve this challenge, we develop a mathematical model by establishing the 0-1 relationship matrix among ONUs, OLTs and wavelengths. In the proposed location-based adaptive genetic algorithm, we capture the nearly optimal relationship matrix, improving the performance of network resource allocation. Under the assumed conditions, the simulations show that the proposed dynamic bandwidth defragmentation scheme effectively reduces the degree of bandwidth fragmentation from 0.7 to less than 0.2 under the limited strength of the migration.

articleTitle: Design of 16-mode PANDA polarization-maintaining ring-core fiber for MIMO-free space-division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A 16-mode PANDA polarization-maintaining ring-core fiber (PM-RCF) is presented and optimized, which adjacent LP-modes show effective refractive index differences larger than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> for multiple-input multiple-output-free (MIMO-free) space-division multiplexing (SDM) optical networks. Relative mode multiplicity factor (RMMF) is defined to evaluate the spatial efficiency of the presented PM-RCF.

articleTitle: High speed atmospheric laser communication system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A digital free-space optical (FSO) communication over 1km based on double-channel dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) is experimentally demonstrated. We successfully achieve multiplexing and demultiplexing of signals with different rates and different code types.

articleTitle: Multi-stratum joint strategy based on decomposition implement in SDON
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: For the current 5G mobile network, current OSNR computing is mainly oriented to the theory, and lack of the combination of the actual OTN network model. Thus, the deviation between theoretical and practical values. Therefore, this paper presents an OSNR-aware multi-stratum joint programming strategy based on decomposition implement in software defined optical network (SDON).

articleTitle: Game theoretical flexible service provisioning in IP over elastic optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this work, aiming to enhance network automation and service fairness, we formulate a stackelberg game for flexible service provisioning in an IP over elastic optical network (IP-over-EON). In the proposed game, the service provider is the leader and maximizes its revenue by pricing the lightpaths in the EON layer and changing their capacities adaptively, while the incoming requests are the followers and determine their routing schemes and capacity requirements individually to make the maximum profit for themselves. To study the existence of Stackelberg Equilibriums (SEs) in the game, we consider both the single-logic-link and multiple-logic-links scenarios.

articleTitle: Investigation of temperature measurement system based on fluorescence intensity ratio of erbium-doped fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: This paper presents a temperature measurement system based on fluorescence intensity ratio of erbium-doped fiber. A novel compact system architecture consisted of 980nm pumping laser, 980/1550nm wavelength division multiplexer (WDM), one way Erbium doped fiber was developed. The system performance was verified by the relationship between temperature and the fluorescence intensity ratio(FIR)of 1450nm and 1531nm, with test temperature ranges from 30°C to 210°C. Obvious temperature dependence of FIR was observed, which proves the feasibility of this compact temperature measurement architecture.

articleTitle: 835 MHz SESAM burnt-free mode locked femtosecond Er-doped fiber oscillator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a fundamentally semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) mode-locked fiber oscillator with a repetition rate up to 835 MHz at a central wavelength of 1572.3 nm. The average power of the output pulse is 6.02 mW, corresponding to a pulse energy of 7.2 pJ with an 150 mW incident pump power. Due to the intracavity anomalous dispersion, the laser is operating at soliton mode-locked regime with a spectral bandwidth of 12.7 nm and a pulse duration of 374 fs. Furthermore, with such high repetition rate, the mode-locked pulse maintains a clean pulse quality with a noise suppression of more than 75dB. The mode-locked fiber oscillator is compact, SESAM burnt-free and robust with an all-fiber configuration.

articleTitle: Analysis of Rytov variance in free space optical communication under the weak turbulence
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Turbulent environment can highly affect the performance of free space optical (FSO) communication links. Therefore, how to obtain the turbulence intensity is a very important issue. The paper has shown the detailed analysis to calculate the log irradiance variance (<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">σ</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>) along with the experimental verification under an indoor laboratory controlled turbulence condition. This paper verifies the consistency of the Rytov variance and the scintillation index under the weak condition based on theoretical and experimental results.

articleTitle: A PAPR reduction rechnique using FHT with repeated companding and filtering in CO-OFDM systems
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) reduction scheme based on the technique of the fast Hadamard transform (FHT) with repeated companding filtering (RCF)is proposed to reduce the PAPR in coherent optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CO-OFDM). The simulations show that the novel scheme could achieve significant reduction in PAPR and a good bit error rate (BER) performance. At the CCDF=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>, the PAPR of proposed scheme after 2 iterations is optimized by 0.28 dB and 0.59 dB compared to selective mapping (SLM) and partial transmit sequence (PTS) respectively. At BER=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>, the proposed scheme after 2 iterations is reduced by 1.83 dB and 1.24 dB compared to SLM and PTS.

articleTitle: A planning method of clustering ONUs based on reliability
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In Ethernet passive optical network (EPON), the distance between optical network units (ONUs) and optical line terminal (OLTs) is in a large range of changes. Only dividing ONUs into a network according to locations will influence the user's QoS. In view of this situation, this paper puts forward a planning strategy of ONUs clustering. We first consider the economy, network delay and network reliability, and establish the cost model, the reliability model and the network delay model. Secondly, we plan the number and location of access points (AP) and the method of clustering ONUs, and use the genetic algorithm to obtain the optimal clustering scheme of ONUs. Lastly, the simulation results demonstrate that the ONUs clustering method can achieve the optimal construction costs of the network, at the same time the method also can meet the requirements of network delay and reliability.

articleTitle: Sensitivity-enhanced temperature sensor based on metalized optical fiber grating for marine temperature monitoring
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A sensitivity-enhanced temperature sensor for marine monitoring based on fiber Bragg grating (FBG) has been proposed and experimentally investigated. The temperature sensor has been realized by electroplating a copper coating on a metalized FBG. Then, the coated FBG is packaged by a carbon film, which protects the copper coating from being corroded when the sensor is used in the ocean. The carbon film is fabricated with magnetron sputtering. Analyses have been made to prove that the carbon film is compact and contains some diamond. This carbon film containing some diamond is called diamond-like carbon. In this way, the coated FBG will have a high temperature sensitivity of 21.86 pm/ °C. The coated FBG sensor has been tested in a simulative environment which is similar to the ocean environment. Experimental results show that the sensor maintains stable in more than 38 days.

articleTitle: Teflon-functionalized microfiber coupler with a good thermal stability
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we fabricate a microfiber coupler (MFC) functionalized with Teflon thin film. Since Teflon has a negative thermo-optic coefficient, it can compensate for the thermal effects of silica. The temperature dependence of the MFC depends on the radius of microfiber which controls the thermal effect contributions of silica and polymer. The device we fabricate has the temperature sensitivity of ~ -2.9 pm/°C.

articleTitle: Noise figure measurement of narrow-band low noise system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The standard core protocol of Narrow Band Internet of Things (NB-IOT) was approved by the RAN plenary session in June 16, 2016. Global operators have a standardized IOT proprietary protocol. The successful completion of the standardization work also marks that the NB-IOT has entered the commercial stage. Modern wireless communication equipment must accommodate high power transmitter and high sensitivity receiver. To ensure the well work of the receiver, the narrow-band pass filter should be equipped before the low noise amplifier in the front end of the receiver. The accurate measurement of the noise figure of the low noise system is directly related to the gain and the measurement configuration under narrow-band condition. This paper presents a narrow-band measurement scheme, and analyzes the influence of gain error during the measurement of low noise figure.

articleTitle: Exposed antiresonant nodeless hollow core photonic crystal fiber for fast-response gas sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A novel design of an exposed antiresonant (AR) nodeless hollow core photonic crystal fiber (NHC-PCF) for gas sensing was proposed, which could enable gas samples to diffuse in or out of the AR NHC-PCF through the open cladding within a very short time. The unique properties of the designed AR NHC-PCF were investigated in detail, such as mode pattern, fraction of power in the central core, confinement loss and response time. The advantages and potential applications of these exposed AR NHC-PCF are discussed.

articleTitle: Calculation and simulation for spherical aberration of doublet lens based on MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In recent years, doublet lens has been used more and more widely in the ideal optical components of confocal 3D imaging due to its high resolution. But for doublet cemented lenses, spherical aberration becomes the biggest barrier to its application. In this paper, based on the formation mechanism of spherical aberration, not only the near and far axis optical path calculation method and equation are given, but also the MATLAB simulation tool is used to provide an intuitive way to calculate the spherical aberration of a doublet lens.

articleTitle: Study on the large-scale novel fiber sensor network based on cloud computing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The large-scale novel fiber sensor network based on cloud computing is proposed. The cross distribution of the fiber Bragg grating network and the distributed fiber sensor network expands in size of the fiber sensor network and realizes the three-dimensional measurement. Mass data acquisition and real-time analysis of the large-scale fiber sensor network have been a technology bottleneck. It can paralyze some network nodes. So the cloud computing technology is used to process mass data of large-scale fiber sensor network. It shares the work of one node to the other nodes, which not only reduces the operation load of single node, but also reduces the possible risks of the fiber sensor network.

articleTitle: An initialization scheme for blind equalization in VLC systems
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Inter-symbol interference (ISI) in visible light communication (VLC) systems has been considered as a major problem which seriously deteriorates system performance. Constant modulus algorithm (CMA) is a widely adopted blind equalization scheme to eliminate ISI in practice due to its computational simplicity and effectiveness. This paper proposed an initialization scheme for CMA based on received signal power. The similarity level of the channels is measured by the difference between the current received power and the pre-stored received power. If the difference appears in a specific range, the pre-stored weight vector already calculated can be used for initialization. Compared with the center-spike initial setting, the proposed scheme can accelerate the convergence rate of CMA and ensure that the equalizer will converge to a stable equilibrium near a desired global minimum.

articleTitle: Polarization diversity receivers with heterodyne demodulation for eliminating the polarization-induced fading of interferometric hydrophone
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A method of adding squared signals of three polarization diversity receiver to overcome the polarization induced fading (PIF) in the optical fibre hydrophone is proposed and experimentally verified. This triple polarization diversity receiver (tri-PDR) is first analysed and theoretically demonstrated. Then, a Mach-Zehnder interferometric sensor with polarization rotator in the reference arm is fabricated and tested. Experimental results show that PIF can be efficiently eliminated with the adding squared signals of tri-PDR. It's also found that background noise of high frequency (>500Hz) can be also suppressed.

articleTitle: Dense sub-carrier uniform division labeling optical transmission system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated a dense sub-carrier uniform division labeling transmission system by using MATLAB software. The simulation results indicated that dense sub-carrier uniform division labeling has a good advantage over that ordinary OFDM system, and the signals at a bit rate 50Gbit/s have a good performance which is more than 10 when OSNR is equal to 25dB over 1000km optical fiber channel which only concerns the influence of polarization-mode dispersion.

articleTitle: Study on the high frequency vibration measurement by using optical fiber sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, a high frequency vibration detection system of optical fiber sensing has been designed based on facet reflection principle, to satisfy the requirements of high frequency vibration measurement, including aerospace and fault diagnosis of high-speed rotating machinery, etc. The system modulates high frequency vibration signal by using the reflective intensity modulation fiber-optic sensor. The vibration signal is converted into electrical signal through photoelectric conversion and amplifying circuit, and then to deal with it in the detection unit. In this way, the vibration signal has been measured successfully. In the experiment, the maximum response frequency is 33 kHz, and 2 kHz is the minimum, the frequency measurement error is below 0.5%. Comparing with other optical methods of vibration measurement, the detection system has the wider bandwidth and higher response frequency.

articleTitle: Passively Q-switched Erbium-doped fiber lasers by a microfiber-based PbS quantum dot saturable absorber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We demonstrated the passively Q-switched Erbium-doped fiber laser by the microfiber-based PbS quantum dot (QDs) as saturable absorber (SA). Compared with other SA, the microfiber-based PbS QDs had higher thermal damage threshold and tunable spectroscopic properties. We fabricated the microfiber with the diameter of 5.86 μm and the interaction length of 2 mm and the PbS QDs with the peak of absorption spectrum at 1533nm. Finally we have successfully demonstrated the Q-switched fiber laser with the pulse width decreased from 3.68μs to 3.24μs and the repetition rate increased from 93.4 kHz to 101.9 kHz.

articleTitle: 2μm Switchable single-longitudinal-mode dual-wavelength fiber laser based on composite cavity and a core-offset structure
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a 2μm switchable single-longitudinal-mode dual-wavelength fiber laser based on composite cavity and a core-offset structure. The fiber laser is switchable, power-equalized and operating in single-longitudinal-mode.

articleTitle: 228 Gb/s vector-mode-division-multiplexing signal transmission in free-space based on optical frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a vector-mode-division-multiplexing (VMDM) system based on opticalfrequency comb (OFC) over 80cm free space optical (FSO) link. The 228 Gbit/s data transmission has been achieved by using two basic vector modes over 20 wavelengths with direct detection orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DD-OFDM) signal. The result shows that this VMDM system should be a good candidate in large-capacity short-reach optical transmission systems.

articleTitle: Micro fiber Mach-Zenhder interferometer vibration sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this study, we demonstrate In-line fiber Mach-Zenhder interferometer measuring for vibration in this device we using the hydrogen flame, this sample device can excited high order cladding mode then we used such interferometer to measure vibration.

articleTitle: A QoS-aware resource allocation algorithm based on dynamic virtual cluster for PFTTH network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The appearance of power and fiber to the home (PFTTH) network combining optical fiber composite low-voltage cable (OPLC) and passive optical network (PON) is crucial in both construction and operation of a smart grid, so it is an essential part to the success of the emerging smart grid. To achieve the purposes of accommodating more users, improving resource utilization and enhancing the flexibility of management and control in PFTTH network, we propose a PFTTH network based on dynamic virtual cluster and corresponding QoS-aware resource allocation algorithm in this paper. Furthermore, the performances of proposed network and algorithms are simulated and evaluated，the results verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Doppler noise in the inline FBG-based interferometric hydrophone array
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Doppler noise caused by the time delay of interrogation pulses in the inline FBG-based hydrophones is theoretically investigated and experimentally verified. This noise is first demonstrated by arranging a piezoelectric transducer (PZT) in front of a FBG-based interferometric senor. Measured Doppler noise is about -61.21dB, with time delay between two interrogation pulses of 210ns and frequency of applied signal of 1kHz, agreeing well with theoretical analyses. Then Doppler noise is further studied in a sensor array to illustrate the relationship between TDM crosstalk. It's found that crosstalk, induced by chaotic reflection between utilized gratings in the array, can be suppressed by low reflectivity of gratings. But the intrinsic Doppler noise caused by inline architecture is hardly affected by the reflectivity and will become more deteriorate with increasing sensing number.

articleTitle: High speed bidirectional chaotic communication based on bidirectionally coupled semiconductor lasers
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We have numerically demonstrated a high-speed bidirectional chaotic communication, where chaotic optical signal with suppressed time delay signature is used. In this scheme, the output of a third semiconductor laser is used as the common signal driving the other two identical lasers with self-feedback to be synchronized. To enhance the bandwidth of the chaotic signal employing in the communication, part of output of the driven laser is coupled into the third laser and appropriate frequency detuning is also considered. Since the relative strong wide-bandwidth optical injection, the native time delay signature of chaos generated by the driven laser is suppressed. Moreover, the results shows that high-speed chaotic communication over 10Gb/s can be achieved due to the enhancement of the chaotic bandwidth.

articleTitle: Energy-efficient grooming with distance-adaptive load balancing in flexible bandwidth optical networks
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the energy-efficient grooming with distance-adaptive load balancing (EEG-DALB) in flexible bandwidth optical networks. For comparison, an existing energy-efficient approach without grooming and load balancing (EEA-WGLB) is also introduced. Simulation results show that the proposed EEG-DALB achieves better performance in terms of the blocking probability and average power consumption compared to EEEA-WG.

articleTitle: High speed DPSK modulation up to 30 Gbps for short reach optical communications using a silicon microring modulator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the high speed DPSK modulation and demodulation for short reach optical communications by using a silicon microring modulator and a Sagnac interferometer at speed up to 30 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Wavelength-swept fiber laser based on linear chirped fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A new wavelength-swept fiber laser is proposed and successfully demonstrated based on two linear chirped fiber Bragg gratings (LC-FBGs) with perfect opposite dispersion response. It is based on intra-cavity pulse stretching and compression provided respectively by two chirped gratings. Experimental results demonstrate a wavelength-swept fiber laser that exhibits a sweep rate of about 3.48 MHz over a 6 nm sweeping range with a center wavelength of about 1549 nm.

articleTitle: Design of bandwidth-variable TWDM access network supporting inter-ONU communication based on tunable bandwidth wavelength selective switch
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a bandwidth-variable TWDM access network structure which could simultaneously support upstream, downstream and peer-to-peer (PtP) communication directly inter ONUs based on the LCoS-based tunable bandwidth WSS in RN. The WSS improve the network flexibility due to its scalable technology and programmable filtering characteristics. Equivalent experiments are performed to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Low-phase-noise frequency synthesizer based on optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We design and investigate a frequency synthesizer for generating a serial of low-phase-noise frequencies from 5.9GHz to 12.9GHz using an optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) as the reference. The 10 GHz free-running OEO has an ultra-low phase noise of −136dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset. The phase noise of the constructed frequency synthesizer at 10 kHz offset is from −135dBc/Hz to −125dBc/Hz. The spurious suppression ratio is more than 55dBc and the frequency hopping time is shorter than 1.5us for a 20-MHz frequency transition. The results verify that, OEO is a good candidate for the reference of a frequency synthesizer to achieve low phase noise frequencies.

articleTitle: Blind estimation of primary signal in cognitive satellite communication systems
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: The cognitive radio (CR) have been proposed to improve spectral efficiency and to meet growing demands for higher data rates in mobile communications and satellite communications. In this paper, we propose a blind estimation algorithm for a secondary user to estimate transmission parameters of the primary signal in an OFDM overlay system, using only the available fast Fourier transform (FFT) component of the secondary user. The algorithm does not require any a priori knowledge of the primary signal or the environmental noise. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithm outperforms existing blind estimation methods especially in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) regions.

articleTitle: Low-loss and wide-band polarization converter based on a hybrid plasmonic waveguide with asymmetric Ag strips
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A polarization converter (PC) based on the mode coupling in a hybrid plasmonic waveguide (HPW) is proposed. This PC comprises a Si core, a low index insulator layer surrounding the Si core, and two asymmetrically arranged Ag strips. Two orthogonal hybrid polarization modes are excited within the low index insulator layer. By exploiting the mode characteristics of these two hybrid polarization modes, a compact and low loss polarization converter can be realized. As a comparison, SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> are used as the low index layer. Numerical simulations show that a better polarization conversion performance is obtained when SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is used in the HPW-PC, which exhibits a polarization conversion efficiency (PCE) of99.99%, an insertion loss (IL) of 0.82dB and an extinction ratio (ER) of 30.4 dB at the wavelength of1550 nm for a conversion length of 4.58μm. Also, for the C-band, the PCE is greater than 99.6%, the IL is below 1dB and the ER is larger than 24dB.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a visible-light parallel communication link based on hexadecimal vector beam array coding/decoding
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate visible-light co ding/de co ding utilizing hexadecimal vector beam array for parallel communication link. The hexadecimal base mode is investigated and 128-ary is also available. We present vector beam array carrying 4×6/6×8/12×16 hexadecimal numbers and error-free data stream transmission performance is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Single-channel 102.4-Gb/s transmission over 240-km SSMF with optical SSB Nyquist-PAM-4 and direct detection
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: By an orchestra of multiple enabling techniques at the transmitter and receiver, we experimentally demonstrate a single-channel 102.4-Gb/s transmission up to 240-km standard single-mode fiber (SSMF) at C-band with direct detection. At the transmitter, we realize Nyquist-pulse shaping PAM-4 (NPAM-4) modulation and single-sideband modulation by using a dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator. At the receiver, we use FFE and high-order terms of Volterra filter, Hilbert superposition cancellation, to mitigate the linear and nonlinear interference. The fiber dispersion can be compensated at either the transmitter or receiver.

articleTitle: Artificial neural network for nonlinear distortion mitigation in optical SSB NPAM-4 direct-detection system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We study the artificial neural network (ANN) and feed forward equalizer jointly to mitigate the inter-symbol interference (ISI) and the nonlinear distortions in the optical single-side band and direct-detection (DD) system. The optical SSB signal is generated by a relatively low-cost dual-drive Mach-Zehnder modulator (DDMZM). The two driving signals are a pair of Hilbert signals with Nyquist pulse-shaped four-level pulse amplitude modulation (NPAM-4). In this paper, we experimentally compare the performance of feedforward equalizer (FFE) with BP (back propagation) network combined with FFE. The experimental results show that the performance of BP network with FFE equalizer outperforms FFE equalizer, because it can efficiently mitigate the nonlinear distortions. We have experimentally demonstrated that a 40 Gb/s NPAM-4 signal transmit over 80 km standard single mode fiber (SSMF) without any inline dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: Wavelength-tunable mode-locked fiber laser with birefringence-enhanced cavity
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A wavelength-tunable Erbium-doped fiber laser with birefringence-enhanced cavity is proposed. A 45° tiled fiber grating (45°TFG) and a section of polarization maintaining (PM) fiber are placed between two two polarization controllers (PCs). Two PCs and PM fiber are employed to enhance the birefringence effect. The 45° TFG plays the role of an in-fiber polarizer. The fiber laser is mode-locked by single walled carbon nanotube polyvinyl alcohol (SWCNTs-PVA) composite film. Central wavelength of the fiber laser can be tuned from 1552.52nm to 1575.28nm with a tuning range of 22.76nm. The demonstrated laser provided the widest tuning range in a high repetition rate all-fiber Erbium doped laser based on SWCNT.

articleTitle: A multi-wavelength random distributed feedback fiber laser with a Sagnac loop mirror
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A multi-wavelength random distributed feedback fiber laser consisting of a length of erbium-doped fiber, a 20-km-long single-mode fiber and a Sagnac loop mirror was demonstrated experimentally. Under the pump power was changed from 30 to 180 mW, variable channel number of 2 to 8 was achieved, meaning that wavelength competition caused by homogenous gain broadening in erbium-doped fiber was significantly suppressed. The laser shows several other advantages such as low-cost, low threshold pump power, low coherence and simple configuration.

articleTitle: A sandwich fiber sensor for simultaneous measurement of RI and temperature
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A simple and compact all-fiber sensor based on a sandwich fiber structure for simultaneous measurement of refractive index and temperature is proposed and demonstrated. The sensing element was made by cascading two core-offset attenuators with a fiber Bragg grating (FBG) in between. The two core-offset attenuators make up a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The transmission spectrum would shift with the variation of the ambient refractive index (RI) and/or temperature. The experimental results show that the RI sensitivity and the temperature sensitivity for the sensor are 35.9611 nm/RIU (refractive index unit) and 0.0501 nm/°C, respectively.

articleTitle: Coverage-oriented pon planning with LTE networks deployed for power distribution communication network
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: LTE-PON hybrid access architecture for Power Distribution Communication Network (PDCN) allows a good trade-off among cost, flexibility, and reliability. In this paper, we focus on the case where LTE-based wireless power private network already deployed in PDCN and Aggregation Points (APs), which forward data between client terminals and the control center, can be served by either LTE network or PON. Given a limit budget, this paper puts forward a PON planning model to cover as many as APs. Then a heuristic algorithm is proposed for this NP-hard problem on the basis of the Genetic Algorithm incorporated Ant Colony Optimization (GA-ACO). Simulation results prove the effectiveness and convergence of the proposed method.

articleTitle: All-optical multilevel regeneration in nonlinear optical loop mirror
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: An all-optical multilevel amplitude regenerator is optimized based on the transmission response of a nonlinear optical loop mirror (NOLM). Three regenerative regions defined by the power-transfer-function (PTF) slope of less than 1 are obtained, and noise suppression is shown for a PAM4 signal. Using amplitude dithering we were able to experimentally characterize the transfer function slope and confirm the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of photodiode array electrodes
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: We designed and optimized a high-speed, low-loss electrodes applied to photodiode array (PDA) using simulating software HFSS. Optimized and un-optimized electrodes were fabricated and tested. A 1.1dB reduce of the insertion loss at 40GHz was achieved by the optimization. Meanwhile, photodiode array implementing the optimized electrodes has a 6.6GHz higher 3dB-bandwidth comparing to the photodiode with un-optimized electrodes.

articleTitle: Single-longitudinal-mode(SLM) fiber ring laser based on semicircular single mode fiberstructure
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A single longitudinal mode (SLM) fiber ring laser based on a semicircular single mode fiber (SSMF) structure is proposed. In the fiber ring laser, a piece of erbium doped fiber (EDF) pumped by a 980 nm semiconductor laser diode (LD) through a wavelength division multiplexer (WDM).A fiber Bragg grating (FBG) is used as a filter. And a commercial single mode fiber (SMF)is bent into semicircular structure between a one-dimensional precision translation stage (TS) and a fixed stage (FS) to form SSMF structure. Birefringence interference in the SSMF with much bigger free spectrum range of 9.42 nm than the linewidth of FBG is very benefit for beat noise suppression because of Vernier effect. As a result, multi longitudinal mode laser, vanishing laser and SLM laser can be observed periodically by tuning the TS little by little. The side mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of SLM laser is 31.5 dB and the peak power is -13dBm. The system is very simple and lower cost.

articleTitle: Twist characteristics of the helical long-period fiber gratings written in the polarization maintaining fiber
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A helical long-period grating (HLPG) was written in a polarization maintaining fiber (PMF) with CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser. The twist characteristics of individual and cascaded PMF-HLPG were investigated experimentally. It was found that PMF-HLPG behaved differently with a different light input. When a polarized light was launched into the cascaded PMF-HLPGs with opposite helical direction, a high twist sensitivity of 0.8 nm/rad/m could be achieved in a narrow twist rate range of 0–8 rad/m. The proposed PMF-HLPG would have a promising prospect for the application of the twist monitor.

articleTitle: Optical waveguide sensors based on Vernier effect
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: Optical waveguide sensing has developed rapidly in recent years. In this paper, we review our previous work about the high-sensitivity optical waveguide sensors based on Vernier effect. Experimental results show these optical waveguide sensors have the great potential applications in biological research and environment monitoring.

articleTitle: Novel training symbol design for transmitter IQ mismatch estimation for PDM CO-OFDM at 120Gb/s
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: In this paper, we design a novel training symbol structure to estimate in-phase/quadrature (IQ) mismatch. Based on this structure the estimation method is deduced in frequency domain which can achieve the estimation of IQ mismatch and channel distortion independently and improve the system performance obviously. Numerical simulation shows that the proposed method has better system BER performance than the compared method at the data rate of 120Gb/s over 320 km transmission while against IQ imbalance.

articleTitle: Measurement of impairments in few-mode fiber for MDM system
publicationTitle: 2017 16th International Conference on Optical Communications and Networks (ICOCN)
abstract: A challenge is to measure the impairments of few-mode fiber (FMF) for mode division multiplexing (MDM) system, so as to quantify the few-mode fiber and compensate the impairments, and thus improves the transmission performance of MDM system. In this paper, the experimental setup of impairments measurement with the structure of Photonic Lantern and optical circulators is established. Not only the two kinds of mode coupling (MC) in 9.8 km 3-mode fiber and at splicing of two FMFs (0.9km and 9.8km) with an off-axis distance of 2.0μm and 2.4μm, but also the mode dependent loss (MDL) between LP<inf>01</inf> and LP<inf>11</inf> are successfully measured.
